items.title: [Windows/Desktop] Desktop update button fails with PermissionError: WinError 5 since Hermes-managed Node introduction

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Describe the bug
On Windows, the Desktop App's 1-click "Update" button has completely stopped working. It fails with a `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied` pointing to `%HERMES_HOME%\node\npm.cmd`.

### Root Cause
This is a regression introduced by the new **Hermes-managed Node** feature.

**Before** (previous versions):
- The desktop app used the system's own Node.js/npm (if installed).
- Updates were completely isolated — the updater never touched the system's Node environment.

**After** (current versions):
- Hermes forcibly downloads and manages its own Node.js runtime in `AppData\Local\hermes\node`.
- The desktop app itself runs from this managed environment.
- When the user clicks "Update" from within the GUI, the updater script attempts to verify/rebuild this same managed Node directory.
- Windows enforces strict file locks on any program in use. The updater cannot touch `npm.cmd` while it is being used, causing the failure.

### Impact
- The convenient 1-click update from the desktop app is broken on Windows.
- Users are forced to:
  1. Shut down the desktop app completely.
  2. Kill any background `node.exe` processes.
  3. Run `hermes update` from an external terminal.

### Expected behavior
The updater needs a Windows-safe mechanism for self-updating the active Node runtime. Possible solutions:
- Use a detached bootstrap/updater process that guarantees the desktop app and all Node subprocesses are completely terminated *before* touching the `%HERMES_HOME%\node` directory.
- Download the new Node tree to a side-by-side temporary directory and perform an atomic swap only upon the next cold start.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 10 / 11
- Surface: Hermes Desktop App
- Version: `0.19.0` / `0.20.0` (current)

items.title: [Bug]: Model switch before first message titles session "[System: The active model..." (and leaves title NULL)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### What happened

Switching the active model **before** sending the first real message in a new session causes the session to be titled from the model-switch marker instead of the user's actual question.

The sidebar shows:

```
[System: The active model for this chat has…
```

Inspecting the DB, the `sessions.title` column is actually `NULL` — the string above is the UI falling back to rendering the first message. So the session is not merely mis-titled, it is **never titled at all**.

### Why it happens

`_append_model_switch_marker` (`tui_gateway/server.py`) persists its notice with `role="user"`:

```python
entry = {"role": "user", "content": marker, "display_kind": "model_switch"}
```

That is deliberate — strict OpenAI-compatible providers (vLLM, Qwen) reject a system message that is not first (#48338). But titling cannot distinguish it from a genuine opening turn, which produces two separate bugs:

**1. The marker is not recognised as machine-authored.**

`agent/title_generator.py` already has a guard list:

```python
_MACHINE_PREFIXES = (
    "[CONTEXT COMPACTION",
    "[Runtime note:",
    "[SYSTEM]",
)
```

The marker begins `[System: The active model for this chat has changed to `. That matches **none** of the three — `[SYSTEM]` differs in case and has a closing bracket. So `is_titleable_user_message()` returns `True`:

```
>>> is_titleable_user_message(marker)
True
>>> derive_title(marker)
'[System: The active model for this chat has…'
```

**2. The marker consumes the session's only titling opportunity.**

`maybe_auto_title()` detects the opening turn by counting user messages:

```python
user_msg_count = sum(
    1 for m in (conversation_history or [])
    if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("role") == "user"
)
if user_msg_count > 1:
    return
```

The marker counts. So when the first real question arrives, `user_msg_count == 2` and the function returns early — no title is ever written. This is why the column stays `NULL`.

Fixing only (1) would trade a wrong title for a permanently missing one; both need addressing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a new session (Desktop or TUI).
2. Switch the model before sending anything, e.g. `/model custom:<provider>:<model>`.
3. Send a normal first question, e.g. `hourly weather forecast for <city>`.
4. Look at the sidebar: the session is titled `[System: The active model for this chat has…`.
5. Confirm the underlying cause:

```bash
python3 -c "
import sqlite3, os
db = sqlite3.connect('file:' + os.path.expanduser('~/.hermes/state.db') + '?mode=ro', uri=True)
print(db.execute('SELECT id, title, title_source FROM sessions ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1').fetchone())
"
# -> (..., None, None)   title is NULL
```

### Expected

The session should be titled from the first message that carries real user intent, ignoring machine-authored openers — the same way compaction handoffs and runtime notes are already ignored.

### Environment

- Hermes: `main` @ b79e83827d
- OS: macOS 26.6.1 (Apple Silicon)
- Python: 3.11 (project venv)
- Surface: Desktop app (the titling path is shared with the TUI)

### Related

- #48338 — why the marker is `role="user"` in the first place
- #65891 — prior work on marker accumulation in history

items.title: Interrupted cron job's failure notification is lost: gateway disconnects adapters before the worker can deliver it

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

When the gateway shutdown interrupts an in-flight cron job, the job's "this run was interrupted" notification is **never delivered to the user**, and the delivery failure itself is **not even recorded**. The run's only trace is a generic `last_status` line in `jobs.json`.

This was observed while investigating #82161, whose reporter measured the race precisely:

> Additionally, the failure notification is undeliverable — Telegram disconnects at 08:01:30,913, six milliseconds before the job is marked failed at 08:01:30,919 — so no alert reaches the user. The error is only discoverable by inspecting jobs.json directly.

It is filed separately because it is an independent defect with an independent fix: it reproduces on **any** interrupted cron run, including ones where the drain behaved perfectly. Fixing the drain budget (#82224) reduces how often the interrupt happens; it does not make the notification arrive when it does.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a cron job with a delivering target (e.g. `deliver: origin` or `deliver: telegram:<chat_id>`).
2. Start it so it is mid-run (an LLM agent job, or any job with a slow tool call).
3. Restart or stop the gateway while the job is in flight, long enough that the drain times out and the job is interrupted.
4. Observe: no message arrives on the configured target. `jobs.json` holds `"Gateway shut down (final cleanup) killed the jobs tool sub process before the run finished."` and nothing else.

### Expected Behavior

If the gateway kills a cron run, the owner of that run should be told, on the job's configured delivery target, while the transport is still available. If the notice genuinely cannot be sent, the delivery failure should at least be persisted so `cron list` / `jobs.json` shows *both* that the run was interrupted *and* that the alert never went out.

### Actual Behavior

The cron worker does try to notify — and loses a race it cannot win, because the gateway tears the transport down underneath it.

Shutdown ordering in `gateway/run.py::_stop_impl_body` is:

| Phase | Adapters |
|---|---|
| `_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown()` | **connected** |
| drain | connected |
| `_kill_tool_subprocesses("post-interrupt")` → `mark_running_jobs_interrupted()` | **connected** |
| `_bounded_adapter_teardown()` for every adapter | **→ disconnected** |
| `_kill_tool_subprocesses("final-cleanup")` → `mark_running_jobs_interrupted()` | disconnected |

Meanwhile the cron worker thread, still alive in the same process, reaches its own completion path in `cron/scheduler.py::run_one_job` **asynchronously**:

1. `_is_interrupted(job["id"])` forces `success = False` with an honest *"Interrupted by gateway shutdown before the run finished"* error (correct — #60432 deliberately prevents the truncated output from being delivered as a success).
2. Failed jobs always deliver, so it calls `_deliver_result()` → `_send_to_platform()`. **By now the adapters are gone**, so the send fails and sets `delivery_error`.
3. `if not _consume_interrupted_flag(job["id"]):` is **False** — the gateway already wrote `last_status` — so `mark_job_run(...)` is skipped entirely, **and `delivery_error` is discarded with it**.

So the user gets no alert, and the record of *why* they got no alert is dropped on the floor. There is no synchronization point anywhere: `stop()` never waits for interrupted cron jobs to flush a notification, and it never notifies on their behalf.

The gateway already has exactly the right primitive for this — `_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown()`, whose own comment reads *"Adapters are still connected here, so messages can be sent"* — but it iterates `self._running_agents` only. Cron jobs run on `cron/scheduler.py`'s own thread pool and are tracked in `_running_job_ids`, entirely outside that dict. This is the same structural blindness already fixed for **counting** (#60432) and for **draining** (#63529, #82224), but never fixed for **notification**.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Cron

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown()` is blind to in-flight cron work, so the only component that could notify while the transport is up never tries; and the component that does try (the cron worker) runs after teardown and has its failure record suppressed by the `_consume_interrupted_flag()` short-circuit.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Two parts, both narrow:

1. **Notify while the transport is up.** In the post-interrupt phase — after `mark_running_jobs_interrupted()` returns the job IDs it just marked, and *before* adapter teardown — send an interrupted-run notice to each job's resolved delivery targets, reusing `_resolve_delivery_targets()` and the same adapter/metadata path `_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown()` already uses. Best-effort and bounded, so it can never extend or block shutdown. Jobs with `deliver: local` (or no resolvable origin, #43014) resolve to zero targets and stay silent.

2. **Stop discarding the delivery failure.** When `_consume_interrupted_flag()` short-circuits `mark_job_run()`, persist the `delivery_error` anyway so the run's record shows the alert failed rather than silently omitting it.

Notably this must *not* reorder adapter teardown — that ordering is load-bearing for #53175 and #8202.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

Related: #82161, #82224 (drain floor), #60432 (interrupt marking), #63529.

items.title: [Bug] HUD mode opens on the wrong profile (default) instead of the active conversation's profile

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Bug description

On a desktop app with multiple Hermes profiles, activating HUD mode (Ctrl+Shift+H) from a conversation in profile X opens the HUD on the **default** profile instead of profile X. The HUD shows the last session of the default profile, not the conversation that was in focus.

The composer's model pill shows the model of the default profile (which can look identical when two profiles share the same model), so it is not immediately obvious — the transcript is what reveals it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have at least 2 profiles configured (e.g. `default` + a second profile), possibly with the same model on both.
2. Open the desktop app, start/join a conversation in the second profile.
3. Make sure that conversation is the focused/selected one.
4. Press Ctrl+Shift+H (or the titlebar HUD toggle).
5. Observe: the HUD transcript is a conversation from `default`, not the one that was focused.

## Expected behavior

The HUD opens on the same conversation (same profile) that was in focus in the app window, per the handoff design (`hudTargetSessionId()` / `useHudHandoff`).

## Actual behavior

The HUD boots on the primary/`default` profile. The focused session (belonging to a non-primary profile) is not found on that backend, so the HUD falls back to whatever the `default` backend's last session is.

## Root cause (from code reading, desktop 0.17.0 / agent 3dcbe9001)

- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` `hudUrl(sessionId)` carries only `?win=hud` + `#/<sessionId>` — **no profile**.
- The HUD renderer boots through the same gateway boot as a normal window; `src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.ts` `adoptPrimaryProfile()` does `(await desktop.profile?.get?.())?.profile ?? 'default'` — it adopts the **primary** backend profile, which is not necessarily the profile of the conversation that was active.
- So the target session id is resolved against the wrong profile's backend; it is not found; the HUD falls back to that backend's last session.

## Environment

- Windows 11
- Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (win-unpacked build from source at 3dcbe9001)
- Hermes Agent 0.20.0
- Multiple profiles configured (default + several others)

## Notes

- Screenshots available on request (the HUD transcript shows a `default`-profile conversation; the composer pill shows the default profile's model).
- Workaround attempted (does not help): focusing the target conversation immediately before toggling HUD — the HUD still lands on `default`.
- Also seen (possibly related / separate): with a multi-profile setup the HUD layout can look misaligned (composer narrower than the transcript sheet, first transcript line clipped under the bar) — likely aggravated by the wrong profile/session state; related issue #82214 describes the macOS variant.

items.title: fix(terminal): lifecycle guard crashes on NUL-bearing referenced script path
items.body:
## Bug description

The gateway lifecycle safety guard can crash the `terminal` tool before the requested command runs:

```text
ValueError: embedded null byte
```

The failure occurs in `cron/lifecycle_guard.py::_read_referenced_script()` at `os.open(path, flags)` while the terminal tool calls `contains_gateway_lifecycle_command_or_referenced_script()`.

This is a guard failure, not a failure from the command being executed. The guard is intended to inspect referenced shell scripts for unsafe gateway lifecycle actions, but its recursive scanner can derive a `Path` whose string representation contains a NUL byte and pass it to `os.open()`.

## Environment

- Hermes release: `v2026.8.3` (`3c27eb62`, release `v0.20.0`)
- OS: Linux `6.18.29+rpt-rpi-v8` (Raspberry Pi)
- Execution surface: Telegram gateway / terminal tool
- Python: 3.11.15

## Reproduction

From a gateway-backed session, run a normal Python script through `uv`:

```bash
UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/uv-cache /home/amit/.local/bin/uv run python3 scripts/mark_paid.py SBI_PRIME_9973 2026-07 --date 2026-08-06
```

Expected: the lifecycle guard scans safely and the command is allowed (assuming it contains no gateway lifecycle operation).

Actual: the terminal tool fails before the script starts:

```text
Failed to execute command: embedded null byte
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../tools/terminal_tool.py", line 2560, in terminal_tool
    if contains_gateway_lifecycle_command_or_referenced_script(...):
  File ".../cron/lifecycle_guard.py", line 353, in contains_gateway_lifecycle_command_or_referenced_script
    return _contains_unsafe_gateway_action(...)
  File ".../cron/lifecycle_guard.py", line 335, in _contains_unsafe_gateway_action
    if script_text and _contains_unsafe_gateway_action(...):
  File ".../cron/lifecycle_guard.py", line 324, in _contains_unsafe_gateway_action
    script_text, unsafe = _read_referenced_script(script_path)
  File ".../cron/lifecycle_guard.py", line 260, in _read_referenced_script
    descriptor = os.open(path, flags)
ValueError: embedded null byte
```

A trivial command (`true`) succeeds in the same session, so this is specific to recursive referenced-script scanning.

## Root-cause hypothesis

`_contains_unsafe_gateway_action()` catches `ValueError` around `script_path.resolve()` (lines 314–320), but then still calls `_read_referenced_script(script_path)`. `_read_referenced_script()` only catches `OSError` around `os.open()`, not `ValueError`. Therefore a candidate path containing `\x00` can escape the resolver safeguard and crash the terminal guard at the open step.

The file already has related comments describing this exact error class, but the protection is incomplete.

## Proposed fix

1. Make `_read_referenced_script()` treat `ValueError` from `os.open()` as a non-readable / non-script candidate, the same way it treats `OSError`.
2. Optionally reject a NUL-containing candidate before opening it, to make the invariant explicit.
3. Add regression tests that exercise the public guard function with a NUL-bearing referenced-script token and assert:
   - it does not raise;
   - it returns `False` when no lifecycle command is present;
   - a real nested lifecycle command is still detected.
4. Add coverage for both direct execution and shell-wrapper paths so the fix does not weaken the security boundary.

## Impact

The terminal tool becomes unusable for otherwise safe commands whose wrapper/script structure triggers this parser edge case. More importantly, a safety guard must fail safely and predictably; it should not crash the command-execution pathway on malformed or binary-derived candidate paths.

items.title: Desktop app: cannot return to Chat after opening Terminal pane (focus trap)
items.body:
**Bug: Desktop app — after opening the Terminal pane, focus cannot return to the Chat**

**Environment**
- Hermes desktop app version: 0.0.1
- OS: macOS 26.6 (Tahoe), Apple Silicon (MacBook Air, arm64)
- UI language / locale: Ukrainian (UI labels render in Ukrainian)

**Summary**
In the native desktop app, clicking the **«Термінал» (Terminal)** control opens the embedded terminal pane. Once it is open, there is no working UI control — button, tab, pane-switcher, or keyboard shortcut — to return focus to the conversation (chat) pane. The user gets "trapped" in the terminal and cannot get back to the chat without restarting the app.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Launch the Hermes desktop app.
2. Click **«Термінал»** to open the embedded terminal pane.
3. Try to return to the chat — click the chat area, look for a pane switcher / tab, or a shortcut.

**Expected**
A clear, always-available way to switch back to the chat (clicking the chat pane, a tab/pane switcher, or a keyboard shortcut).

**Actual**
No UI element returns focus to the chat; the conversation is effectively unreachable while the terminal pane is active.

**Note for maintainers**
The programmatic agent tool `focus_pane(pane="chat")` *does* successfully return focus to the chat, so the underlying pane switch works — it appears the **UI control** that triggers it (the chat tab / pane switcher / shortcut) is missing, disabled, or broken when the terminal pane is focused. Suggested fix: keep the pane switcher / chat tab clickable in every state, and/or bind shortcuts (e.g. Cmd+1 = chat, Cmd+2 = terminal).

**Additional context**
- Reported by a user through the in-app agent. A screenshot could not be attached automatically because the agent process lacks macOS *Screen Recording* permission (screencapture / osascript are blocked by TCC). I can attach one if the permission is granted, or the user can paste a screenshot here.

items.title: [Bug]: Session auto-title poisoned by vision description prepended for attached images (_enrich_with_attached_images)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

Session auto-title generation can be **poisoned by the vision description** that `tui_gateway/server.py::_enrich_with_attached_images` prepends to the user's message when an image is attached.

Flow: user sends a first message with a screenshot → the gateway runs the auxiliary vision model over the image and prepends `[The user attached an image:\n<description>]\n` to the user text → `maybe_auto_title` → `generate_title()` titles the session from **that enhanced text** (not the user's original words). Two observed failure modes:

1. **Vision misclassification becomes the title.** A screenshot of an IME candidate popup (Rime, typing "iss") was described by the vision model as *"a close-up view of a browser's search or address bar … a list of autocomplete suggestions …"* — the session was titled "修复搜索自动补全下拉菜单显示问题" ("fix search-autocomplete dropdown display issue"), which has nothing to do with what the user asked (IME candidate ordering).

2. **Text visible in the screenshot is copied into the title.** A second screenshot showed the desktop app UI with the *previous* session's title visible in the tab/sidebar; the vision description included that title text, and the new session was titled with a copy of it ("修复搜索自动补全下拉" — an almost exact copy of the previous session's title). This looks like cross-session title leakage but is really the model restating text it saw in the image description.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Desktop app (or any surface routed through `tui_gateway`). Start a new session.
2. First message: text + an attached screenshot whose visible content (or a vision misread of it) differs from the user's intent — e.g. an input-method candidate list, or a UI screenshot showing another session's title.
3. The session title is generated from the vision description prepended by `_enrich_with_attached_images`, not from the user's actual request.

### Evidence

- **Replay of the exact same input without the description** (same provider/model/key via `call_llm(task="title_generation", ...)`): the user's message alone yields sane titles (`"小狼毫输入法问题"`, `"候选词排序问题排查"`), `prompt_tokens` = 300/315.
- **The real calls** had `prompt_tokens` = 486/795 — the difference (~190/~495 tokens) matches the length of the prepended vision description for each screenshot (the UI screenshot is description-heavy).
- **Vision reproduction**: running the same `"Describe everything visible in this image..."` prompt over the IME screenshot returns the "browser search bar / autocomplete suggestions" reading quoted above.
- `title_source` is `llm` (title generation itself succeeded) — this is **not** the silent-failure mode of #82291.

### Expected Behavior

Session titles should reflect the **user's actual message text**, never the vision model's reading of an attached image. The title generator should either receive the un-enriched user text (with `@image:` refs only), or `generate_title()` should strip `[The user attached an image: ...]` blocks before titling.

### Suggested Fix

In `agent/title_generator.py::_summarize_user_message` (or at the `tui_gateway` call site), strip the `[The user attached an image: ...]` / `[You can examine it with vision_analyze ...]` envelope before titling. The persisted `@image:<path>` reference form is fine to keep (it is the format `_build_persist_message_with_image_refs` already uses and is not descriptive).

### Affected Component

Agent Core (session title generation) / tui_gateway image enrichment

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes: v0.20.0 (git 3e6a081d60)
- Provider: opencode-go (auxiliary.title_generation = mimo-v2.5)
- Surface: Desktop app

Related: #82291 (different root cause — silent failure), #66829 (image preprocessing even when main model supports vision).

items.title: search_files returns 0 results on Windows — rg receives MSYS paths it can't resolve

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
# search_files returns 0 results on Windows — rg receives MSYS paths it can't resolve

## Summary

On Windows (Git Bash / MSYS2 environment), `search_files` **always returns 0 results** with no error. The root cause is a path-format mismatch: `_escape_shell_arg` converts Windows paths to MSYS `/c/Users/x` form for bash builtins, but `rg` (ripgrep) is a **native Windows binary** that cannot resolve MSYS-style paths. Since all rg invocations redirect stderr to `2>/dev/null`, the error is silently swallowed.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10/11
- Shell: Git Bash (MSYS2/MINGW64)
- ripgrep: 15.1.0 (native Windows binary from WinGet)
- Hermes Agent: latest main (commit 70db671fa)

## Reproduction

```python
# Any search_files call on Windows:
search_files(pattern="SKILL.md", target="files", path="C:\\Users\\Education\\AppData\\Local\\hermes\\skills")
# → {"total_count": 0}  (but files exist!)
```

### Manual verification

```bash
# rg with MSYS path (what search_files currently passes) — FAILS silently:
$ rg --files --sortr=modified -g '*SKILL.md' '/c/Users/Education/AppData/Local/hermes/skills' 2>/dev/null
# (empty output, exit code 2)

# rg with Windows path — WORKS:
$ rg --files --sortr=modified -g '*SKILL.md' 'C:/Users/Education/AppData/Local/hermes/skills' 2>/dev/null
C:/Users/Education/AppData/Local/hermes/skills\autonomous-ai-agents\agent-causal-reasoning\SKILL.md
C:/Users/Education/AppData/Local/hermes/skills\software-development\skill-split-slimming\SKILL.md
...

# bash builtins work fine with MSYS paths (so path-existence checks pass):
$ test -e '/c/Users/Education/AppData/Local/hermes/skills' && echo exists
exists
```

## Root Cause

In `tools/file_operations.py`, `ShellFileOperations._escape_shell_arg()` calls `_bash_safe_path()` which converts `C:\Users\x` → `/c/Users/x` for bash compatibility. This is correct for bash builtins (`test`, `ls`, `cd`, `head`, `cat`, etc.) but wrong for `rg`, which is a native Windows binary:

1. `search()` calls `self._expand_path(path)` — `~` expands to `$HOME` = `/c/Users/Education`
2. `test -e {path}` passes (bash builtin understands `/c/` paths)
3. `rg --files ... {path} 2>/dev/null` — rg gets `/c/Users/...`, fails with "IO error: 系统找不到指定的路径", stderr swallowed by `2>/dev/null`
4. Result: `total_count: 0`, no error message

## Affected Code Paths

All 7 `rg` invocations in `ShellFileOperations` use `self._escape_shell_arg(path)` for the path argument:

1. `_zero_match_probe` — 3 rg calls (case-insensitive probe, hidden probe, fixed-string probe)
2. `_search_files_rg` — 2 rg calls (sorted + unsorted fallback)
3. `_search_with_rg` — 1 rg call (content search)
4. `_search_with_grep` — 1 rg/grep call (grep fallback, also uses native binary)

## Fix

Added `_rg_escape_path()` method that converts MSYS paths **back** to native Windows form before passing to rg, using the existing `_msys_to_windows_path()` from `tools/environments/local.py`:

```python
def _rg_escape_path(self, path: str) -> str:
    """Escape a path argument for use with rg (ripgrep) on Windows.

    rg is a native Windows binary; unlike bash builtins it does not
    understand MSYS-style /c/Users/x paths. _escape_shell_arg converts
    drive paths *to* MSYS form for bash, which silently breaks every
    rg invocation (rg errors on stderr, but 2>/dev/null swallows it,
    so search_files returns 0 matches with no error).

    This method converts the path *back* to a native Windows form
    (C:\\Users\\x) before single-quoting it, so rg receives a path
    it can resolve. No-op off Windows.
    """
    if not path:
        return "''"
    import platform
    if platform.system() == "Windows":
        from tools.environments.local import _msys_to_windows_path
        path = _msys_to_windows_path(path)
    return "'" + path.replace("'", "'\"'\"'") + "'"
```

Then replaced all 7 `self._escape_shell_arg(path)` calls in rg command strings with `self._rg_escape_path(path)`.

### Diff


items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — Edit failed: target user message is no longer in session history (Grok / long sessions)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

Editing (or rewinding/restoring) a past user message fails with:

> **Edit failed** — `target user message is no longer in session history`

Seen on a long-running chat using **Grok via xAI OAuth subscription** (`grok-4.5` / `xai-oauth`). The UI still shows the user message; the gateway rejects the edit because the `truncate_before_user_ordinal` sent by Desktop is out of range for the live session history.

Impact: user cannot edit an earlier prompt and re-run the turn. Work is blocked on long Grok threads (high context / many tool turns).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Desktop session on **Grok 4.5** (xAI OAuth subscription).
2. Run a long multi-turn agent chat (tools, large history; enough that context compression / history rewrite can fire — sessions in the 100k–250k token range reproduce).
3. In the transcript, edit an **earlier** user message (not only the latest) and submit.
4. Observe toast/error: **Edit failed** with message containing `target user message is no longer in session history`.

## Expected Behavior

- Edit rewinds server history to that user turn and resubmits with the new text.
- If the target turn was truly removed by compaction, Desktop should recover cleanly (resync history + recompute ordinal, or disable edit with a clear reason) — not surface a dead-end **Edit failed**.

## Actual Behavior

- Gateway returns JSON-RPC error **code 4018**: `target user message is no longer in session history`.
- Desktop shows **Edit failed** (`copy.editFailed`).
- There is a one-shot stale-target retry that drops the ordinal and plain-resubmits (`editMessage` in `use-prompt-actions`), but that path is not sufficient: users still hit a failed edit on long Grok sessions (retry fails or does not preserve true edit semantics).

## Affected Component

- **Surface:** macOS Desktop (also TUI gateway path; same `prompt.submit` contract)
- **Gateway:** `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py` — ordinal gate on `prompt.submit`
- **Desktop client:** `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/` — `planEdit` / `visibleUserOrdinal` / `editMessage`

## Root Cause Analysis

| Layer | Location | Behavior |
|-------|----------|----------|
| Gateway reject | `tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py` ~196–206 | Builds `user_indices` from live `session["history"]` where `role == "user"` and **not** `display_kind`. If `ordinal < 0` or `ordinal >= len(user_indices)` → **`_err(rid, 4018, "target user message is no longer in session history")`**. |
| Desktop ordinal | `apps/desktop/.../use-prompt-actions/utils.ts` `visibleUserOrdinal` | Counts client messages with `role === 'user' && !m.hidden` up to the edited index. |
| Desktop edit plan | `.../rewind.ts` `planEdit` | Sets `truncateOrdinal: visibleUserOrdinal(messages, sourceIndex)` (unless failed-turn path). |
| Submit | `.../rewind.ts` `truncateSubmitParams` | Sends `truncate_before_user_ordinal` + `confirm_truncate: true`. |
| Soft recovery | `.../use-prompt-actions/index.ts` `editMessage` ~923–939 | On stale-target regex match, retries **without** ordinal (plain resubmit). Does not resync gateway history or recompute ordinal against server user count. |

**Mismatch:** client ordinal is computed from **Desktop transcript** (hidden flag). Server validates against **in-memory gateway history** (display_kind + post-compaction shape). After long Grok runs, compression / history rewrite / resume can leave fewer non-display user turns on the server than the UI still renders, so a still-visible bubble maps to an ordinal past `len(user_indices)`.

Grok subscription is a **repro amplifier** (long tool-heavy threads, large prompts), not a separate provider bug in xAI’s API.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Authoritative ordinal (preferred):** before edit submit, ask gateway for user-turn count / message ids (or include stable message ids in history sync) and resolve truncate by **id**, not by client-only ordinal.
2. **On 4018:** Desktop must `session.resume` / reload history, recompute ordinal against server user turns, retry edit once; if target is gone, show “this turn was compressed away — edit disabled” instead of generic Edit failed.
3. **Gateway:** when ordinal is OOR but `confirm_truncate` is set, return structured payload `{ code: 4018, user_turn_count, hint }` so the client can recover without parsing English.
4. Align counting rules: client should ignore the same rows server ignores (`display_kind` / synthetic), and server docs already say display_kind is not counted — ensure Desktop never counts rows the server drops.

Minimal sketch (gateway side, clearer error):

```python
if ordinal < 0 or ordinal >= len(user_indices):
    return _err(
        rid, 4018,
        "target user message is no longer in session history",
        data={"user_turn_count": len(user_indices), "ordinal": ordinal},
    )
```

Minimal sketch (Desktop): on 4018 → reload session messages → `planEdit` again → if still OOR, notify specifically; else retry with new ordinal.

## Tests

- `tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py` — extend 4018 cases: history shorter than client ordinal after simulated compaction; assert structured error includes `user_turn_count`.
- `apps/desktop/.../use-prompt-actions/index.test.tsx` — edit when server history has fewer user turns than UI; expect resume + recompute, not permanent Edit failed.
- `rewind.test.ts` — `visibleUserOrdinal` excludes the same synthetic/display rows gateway excludes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Editing a still-visible user message on a long Grok (xAI OAuth) session succeeds, or fails with an explicit “turn no longer in server history” state that does not look like a generic crash.
- [ ] 4018 never leaves the transcript optimistically truncated without recovery.
- [ ] Client and gateway user-turn indexing rules are documented and unit-tested to match.
- [ ] Regression test covers post-compaction ordinal OOR.

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS
- **App:** Hermes Desktop
- **Hermes:** v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), install commit `0b33ee88`
- **Model / provider:** Grok 4.5 via xAI OAuth (`provider=xai-oauth`)
- **Platform path:** Desktop → TUI gateway `prompt.submit`

items.title: [Bug]: TUI status bar session-name chip renders white text on bright yellow (#FFBF00) background, unreadable on default dark theme
items.body:
## Bug: session name chip in TUI status bar is white-on-bright-yellow — unreadable

The session title shown at the right end of the TUI status bar renders as light/white text on a bright yellow background. On the default dark theme it is almost unreadable, and the saturated fill looks out of place next to the rest of the bar.

### What's happening

In `ui-tui/src/components/appChrome.tsx`, the right-side label gets a full-saturation accent fill whenever a session title is set:

```tsx
<Text
  backgroundColor={sessionTitle ? t.color.accent : undefined}
  bold={!!sessionTitle}
  color={sessionTitle ? t.color.statusFg : t.color.label}
  wrap="truncate-end"
>
  {rightLabel}
</Text>
```

Two token problems stack:

1. `t.color.accent` is the accent *identity* hue, not a fill color. In `DARK_SEEDS` (`ui-tui/src/theme.ts`) it is `#FFBF00` — bright yellow. Nothing else in the theme paints a full `accent` background; fills are softened (e.g. `activeRow: '#333355'`, `selection: '#3a3a55'`, `activeRow = mix(surface, accent, 0.22)`).
2. `t.color.statusFg` is derived as `grayOf(mix(text, bg, 0.24))` — a light gray lifted toward the near-white text. On `#FFBF00` that is roughly a 1.5–2:1 contrast ratio, far below any readable threshold.

So the chip is exactly what the seeds comment warns against: the raw accent hue used as a solid fill, with a foreground tone that was never designed to sit on it.

```
Current (dark theme):

┌ status bar ──────────────────────────────────────── ║  My Project  ┐
   ctx  model  cost  ⏱ …            ← bar segments      ↑ ↑
                                                   white/gray text
                                                   #FFBF00 bg (raw accent)
```

### Why it matters

The status bar is the always-visible chrome. A session title is one of the few persistent, user-authored strings in it, and right now it is the least legible element in the whole TUI — on the default theme, no less. It also sets a bad example for skin authors: if `accent` as a fill is this broken, it will be copy-pasted into skins.

### Proposed direction

Two options, both small:

1. Simplest (and what I'd ship first): drop the accent fill when the title is present. Render the title as `color={t.color.accent}` on the normal status bar background — same highlight intent, readable contrast on both dark and light seeds (`#FFBF00` on `#1a1a2e`/`#101014` is fine, `#956E00` on white is fine).
2. If a filled chip is wanted for visual weight, use a softened chip tone like the theme already derives for rows: `mix(surface, accent, 0.2-0.25)` as the background with `accent` (or `statusFg` only if it passes contrast) as the foreground. That matches the `activeRow`/`selection` family and keeps the bar consistent.

```
Proposed (option 1):

┌ status bar ──────────────────────────────────────── ║  My Project  ┐
   ctx  model  cost  ⏱ …            ← bar segments      ↑
                                                  accent-colored text,
                                                  no background
```

The `statusFg` token itself is fine as-is for its normal role (bar text on the `surface`/`statusBg` fill); the bug is only the accent-background pairing on the session chip.

Related: #13490 covers making the status bar fields/config skin-aware — complementary scope. This report is specifically about the default-theme readability bug in the current chip rendering.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop cron uses local profile alias on mapped SSH backend

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug description

Hermes Desktop can map a local profile label to a differently named profile on a managed SSH gateway. For example:

- local Desktop profile: `mara`
- connection: managed SSH remote
- remote Hermes profile: `default`

Opening the full Cron window while `mara` is active fails because Desktop routes the REST request to `mara`'s remote backend but leaves the endpoint filter in the local namespace:

```text
/api/cron/jobs?profile=mara
```

The remote backend is scoped to `default`, so it cannot resolve `mara`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Keep the local `default` profile connected to the local gateway.
2. Configure a second Desktop profile named `mara` to use a managed SSH gateway.
3. Set that SSH connection's remote profile to `default`.
4. Activate `mara` and open the full Cron modal.

## Actual behavior

The cron request filters by the Desktop alias `mara`, and the remote backend reports that the profile cannot be found.

## Expected behavior

Desktop should keep using `mara` to select the connection, but translate endpoint-level self-profile filters to the configured remote profile:

```text
/api/cron/jobs?profile=mara
→ /api/cron/jobs?profile=default
```

Cross-profile selectors such as `profile=all` or another concrete profile must remain unchanged.

## Root cause

`request.profile` correctly selects the per-profile SSH backend in Electron, while the request path independently carries `?profile=<desktop alias>`. The generic REST path resolver knows whether a backend is shared, but it does not know the managed SSH connection's `remoteProfile` mapping.

## Scope

The fix should apply at the Electron REST routing boundary so all endpoint-level self-profile filters use the backend namespace, including Cron list and Cron blueprint instantiation, without changing cross-profile selectors.

## Environment

- Surface: Hermes Desktop
- Connection: per-profile managed SSH
- Local profile and remote profile have different names

items.title: Telegram gateway connect hangs on hosts without global IPv6 ('attempt 1/8' + 409) despite working plain PTB client

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Summary
Hermes gateway Telegram connect hangs indefinitely on a no-global-IPv6 host at
"Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)" — the strict cold-start progress gate never
closes even though a plain python-telegram-bot (PTB) client connects and polls fine
from the same machine. Workaround envs (`HERMES_TELEGRAM_DISABLE_FALLBACK_IPS`,
`TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS`) do not reliably fix it.

### Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
- python-telegram-bot v22.6, Python 3.11.15 / 3.12.3
- Oracle Cloud Always-Free A1.Flex ARM (2 OCPU / 11 GB) and E2.1.Micro
- Ubuntu 24.04, **no global IPv6 route** (`::1` and link-local `fe80::` only);
  DNS returns an IPv6 AAAA (`2001:67c:...`) for api.telegram.org

### Repro / symptom
1. Run the gateway (`hermes gateway run`) with Telegram platform enabled.
2. Log repeats: `[Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)`.
3. No `Connected to Telegram (polling mode)` appears. After ~60s the strict
   cold-start gate errors:
   `Telegram getUpdates made no progress within 60.0s during initial connect`
   (or `Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request`).
4. `py-spy dump` on the hung process: **MainThread idle in the event loop** —
   no telegram coroutine is actually running; two `ESTABLISHED` sockets to
   149.154.166.110:443 exist (fd 23/24).

### Key evidence
- **Plain PTB client works from the same box.** A standalone script using
  `Application.builder().token(...)build()` + `updater.start_polling()` completes
  `getMe` (200), `deleteWebhook` (200), and `getUpdates` (200) and reaches
  `updater.running=True` in well under 1s — even with the gateway's exact
  `request_kwargs` (pool 512, timeouts), and with `HERMES_TELEGRAM_DISABLE_FALLBACK_IPS=true`.
- So the network path, token, and PTB are all fine. The hang is inside the
  gateway's Telegram connect plumbing, not Telegram/Oracle/the token.
- Tracing `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`:
  - `_start_polling_resilient(require_progress=True)` waits on a **strict progress
    gate** (`_INITIAL_POLLING_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT = 60.0`, line 595) and `_await_with_thread_deadline`
    (line 97) which uses a `threading.Timer` to wake a cancellation-shielded anyio scope.
  - The fallback branch (line 3836) builds a **`TelegramFallbackTransport`** that (a)
    runs `discover_fallback_ips()` DNS-over-HTTPS (line 3827) and (b) opens **two**
    HTTPXRequest clients (`request` + `get_updates_request`), producing two
    concurrent `getUpdates` connections on the same token → 409 conflict / stalled.
- On a host with no global IPv6, `getaddrinfo` returns the IPv6 AAAA first; the
  fallback transport / DoH discovery can stall there.

### Workarounds tried (none reliably fixes the gateway path)
- `HERMES_TELEGRAM_DISABLE_FALLBACK_IPS=true` (uses plain single client — my repro
  then works, but the gateway still doesn't reach "Connected")
- `TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS` set to known IPv4s
- `/etc/hosts` pinning api.telegram.org to IPv4
- Disabling IPv6 via sysctl
- `HERMES_TELEGRAM_HTTP_POOL_SIZE=32`

### Suggested fix area
- In `adapter.py`, the strict cold-start gate should not await a progress event
  that depends on the fallback transport when the platform is otherwise reachable;
  or the default connect path should prefer the plain single PTB client (which
  demonstrably works) and make the fallback transport opt-in / no-dual-polling.
- Investigate why the strict-progress Event never fires under the gateway loop on
  these hosts while it does in the standalone repro (interaction between
  `_await_with_thread_deadline`'s timer wake, the shielded updater scope, and the
  gateway's asyncio loop).

### Notes
- This is part of a broader free-tier Oracle Always-Free VPS + Hermes migration.
  The workaround that ships today is: run Telegram on a Mac (default path works)
  and use the VPS as a cron-only agent. Happy to test a fix if maintainers want a
  repro host.

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
