items.body:
# [Bug]: Web dashboard (`:9119`) leaks sqlite connections; hits macOS 256-FD limit after ~2 days uptime

## Summary

The `hermes_cli dashboard` web process on macOS accumulates open file descriptors until it hits the launchd soft limit of 256, then starts returning **500 Internal Server Error** on endpoints that touch the session database (e.g. `GET /api/sessions`). Distinct from the recently filed #77573 (Desktop SSH serve) — same root cause, different surface; this is the Python web server, not the Electron desktop app.

## Environment

- **Hermes Agent**: `v0.20.0` (release 2026.8.3)
- **Platform**: macOS (Darwin)
- **Launchd FD limits**: `maxfiles soft=256 hard=unlimited` (the default)
- **Dashboard command**: `hermes_cli.main dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --insecure --tui --no-open`
- **Uptime to failure**: ~2 days 6 hours (the leak is gradual, not a single-request trigger)

## Reproduction

1. Start the dashboard on macOS: `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --insecure --tui --no-open`
2. Leave it running for 24-72 hours with normal GUI traffic (browsing sessions, switching tabs, etc.)
3. Open the web GUI and hit any endpoint that reads `state.db` (e.g. the Sessions view → `GET /api/sessions`)
4. Observe `500 Internal Server Error` in the browser and `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file` in `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log`

## Evidence

`lsof -p <dashboard_pid> | grep REG | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head` after ~2d6h uptime:

```
  94  /Users/kamil/.hermes/state.db
  92  /Users/kamil/.hermes/state.db-wal
   2  /Users/kamil/.hermes/state.db-shm
  ...
```

`state.db` is opened **94 times** by a single process, `state.db-wal` another **92**. Total FD on the dashboard PID: **260** — over the `launchd` soft limit of **256**.

From `errors.log`:

```
2026-08-09 17:19:52,343 ERROR asyncio: socket.accept() out of system resource
OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files
2026-08-09 17:19:52,356 ERROR hermes_cli.web_server: GET /api/sessions failed
  ...
  File ".../hermes_state_schema.py", line 324, in _fts_table_probe
    cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table_name} LIMIT 0")
sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file
```

Other side-effects of the same root cause that show up first in logs:

- `Failed to parse /Users/kamil/.hermes/config.yaml: [Errno 24] Too many open files` (config also can't be re-read)
- `dashboard-auth audit log write failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files`
- `socket.accept() out of system resource` on the 9119 listener

## Root cause

Two layers, both fixable:

1. **Leak (the real bug)**: `hermes_state.py:2291` (via `hermes_cli/web_server.py:11325` → `_open_session_db_for_profile` → `_fts_table_probe` in `hermes_state_schema.py:324`) opens a new sqlite connection per request and doesn't close it. After ~2 days the same `state.db` file is held open 94×. The pattern suggests no connection pool and no `with` context manager around the open.

2. **Amplifier (a separate but contributing issue)**: the web server inherits macOS's `launchd` soft FD limit (256) without raising it. Even with no leak, a long-lived dashboard with normal plugin/connection overhead will eventually graze this ceiling.

I see a second loop in `dashboard.error.log` (`address already in use` on `:9119` every second) — some watchdog/launchd cycle keeps trying to start a new dashboard because the original appears unhealthy. May be related to 5xx above, may be separate; flagging in case it's the same code path.

## Suggested fix

For (1), the highest-leverage change is to introduce a single shared `sqlite3.Connection` (or a small pool keyed by profile) and reuse it via `with conn:` blocks. Per-call connection open is also ~1ms wasted per request. A minimal patch would:

- Add a `SessionDB` holder at module scope, lazy-initialised per profile
- Replace the bare `sqlite3.connect(...)` in `_open_session_db_at_path` with `holder.get()`
- Have the holder manage `conn.close()` on shutdown / `atexit`

For (2), add a `ulimit -n 65536` (or equivalent `resource.setrlimit`) call at the top of `dashboard` startup so the process enters with a sane FD ceiling. Optionally a YAML key like `dashboard.max_open_files` for users who want to tune it.

## Related

- #77573 — *Desktop SSH serve inherits macOS 256-FD limit with no YAML override* — same launchd / macOS layer, different surface (Electron desktop SSH, not web). Worth linking these two for the maintainer so a single FD-management PR can fix both.

## Workaround (until fixed)

```bash
kill <dashboard_pid>      # or: cd /Users/kamil/hermes-webui && ./ctl.sh restart
# plus, for longer breathing room:
sudo sh -c 'echo "limit maxfiles 65536 200000" > /etc/launchd.conf'   # requires reboot
```

items.title: Tracking: gateway session continuity breaks under state.db FTS corruption — orphan session fork + stale-session resume after restart

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
# Tracking: gateway session continuity breaks under state.db FTS corruption — orphan session fork + stale-session resume after restart

## The contract this violates

A gateway chat (e.g. a Telegram DM) is supposed to be **one continuous session, compacted repeatedly, forever** — until the user explicitly runs `/new` (or equivalent). No code path may silently fork, reset, or time-travel the conversation.

A live incident (Teknium's own DM, Aug 6–9 2026) shows three cooperating failures that break this contract. All data survived, but the DM silently resumed a 2.7-day-old context after a gateway restart.

## Incident timeline (from production `state.db` + `gateway.log`)

| When | Event |
|---|---|
| Aug 6, all day | Gateway repeatedly logs `Persisted transcript lagged live cached history for session agent:main:telegram:dm:<chat> (disk=0, memory=N); preserving live conversation context (possible FTS write corruption)` — every persisted-transcript read-back returns **0 rows** while in-memory history is fine |
| Aug 6 16:18:59 | ~45s after an inbound message, a **new session row** `20260806_161836_04c1d6c6` appears — created by a recovery path. It is written with `session_key=NULL, chat_id=NULL, chat_type=NULL, origin_json=NULL` |
| Aug 6 16:18 → Aug 8 14:05 | 798 messages of real conversation persist under the orphan row. In-memory mapping keeps the user's experience continuous — the fork is invisible |
| Aug 8 17:03:20 | Gateway restarts after a crash: `pruning stale sessions.json entry 'agent:main:telegram:dm:<chat>' -> 20260803_120103_37976afb (end_reason='agent_close'); left by a crashed gateway` — the live chat→session mapping is discarded |
| Aug 9 09:40 | Next inbound DM. Gateway resolves the chat by `session_key` from the DB. The **only** row carrying the key is the stale Aug 3 session (`20260803_120103_37976afb`, last activity Aug 6 16:18). The DM resumes a 3-day-old context; the model makes small talk about a PR merged days earlier. User-visible context loss |

DB evidence (production, read-only):

```
20260803_120103_37976afb   session_key=agent:main:telegram:dm:<chat>  chat_id=<chat>  origin_json={...}  ended_at=None
20260806_161836_04c1d6c6   session_key=None                           chat_id=None    origin_json=None   ended_at=None  (798 msgs, the REAL conversation)
```

## Three failures, one class

**Session identity/routing is not durably owned by the DB.**

1. **Recovery forks instead of preserving.** When the persisted-transcript read comes back empty (`disk=0`), the recovery path creates a *new* session id rather than continuing the existing one. The fork itself is questionable — the disk read failing does not mean the session is gone.
2. **Recovery-created rows are never identity-stamped.** The normal create path writes `session_key`/`chat_id`/`chat_type`/`origin_json`; the recovery path writes none of them. The DB row is an orphan from birth. (Same class as #12857 — auto-reset never stores parent session id.)
3. **Restart resolution trusts the key column blindly.** After the crash-prune of `sessions.json`, the gateway resolves chat→session purely by `session_key` in the DB. With the real session unstamped, the stale row wins. No recency check (`last_activity_at`), no tie-breaking, no detection that the "resumed" session is days older than a sibling with recent activity.

Underneath all three sits the trigger: **state.db FTS corruption breaking the transcript write/read path** (see #78182: one-shot FTS rebuild claims success without verifying the write path; #69672: trigram index eats the `\x00json:` multimodal sentinel → "malformed inverted index", SQLite-version-dependent).

## Who this affects

Any gateway user (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp/…) whose `state.db` hits FTS/write-path corruption — most likely on:
- installs where SQLite version changed under the DB (e.g. venv vs managed runtime mismatch; #69672 makes integrity SQLite-version-dependent),
- multimodal-heavy sessions (the `\x00json:` sentinel),
- long-lived DM sessions that eventually restart the gateway (update, crash, reboot).

The failure is **silent** for days: in-memory continuity masks the fork; only a restart reveals it. Users perceive it as "Hermes forgot everything after the update", and the misleading warning text ("possible FTS write corruption", `disk=0`) reads like hardware failure.

## Related open issues

- #78182 — gateway writes through corrupt state.db indefinitely; FTS rebuild unverified; 200-cap pending queue rotates transcripts away *(the write-path trigger)*
- #69672 — messages_fts_trigram indexes `\x00json:` sentinel → SQLite-version-dependent "malformed inverted index" + bloat *(root-cause candidate)*
- #63386 — state.db FTS corruption on macOS (write-health probe fails) *(same corruption, macOS)*
- #12857 — auto-reset in gateway discards context; parent session ID never stored *(same identity-loss class, April 2026)*
- #79576 — Telegram: SQLite corruption + provider failure + context persist → context loss loop
- #71999 — #50502 cached-history guard false-fires every tool-use turn (alternation-merged view misread as write loss) *(noise source on the same warning)*
- #80255 — close() still uses TRUNCATE checkpoint (#45383 recurrence) *(crash/shutdown data-risk adjacent)*

## Related open PRs (to review as part of this cluster)

- #77895 — fix(gateway): distinguish durable cached transcript rows
- #72732 — fix(state): keep canonical writes available when FTS is corrupt
- #82280 — fix(state): harden state.db — write lock, WAL protections, reconnect self-heal
- #75194 — fix(state): self-heal orphaned FK references in state.db

## Work items

- [ ] **Repro**: minimal script — corrupt/blank the FTS read path under a live gateway session, verify the fork + orphan row; then restart-resolve and verify stale resume
- [ ] **Fix 1 (identity stamping)**: every session row created for a gateway chat gets `session_key`/`chat_id`/`origin` stamped **atomically at INSERT**, on every creation path (normal, recovery, rotation, auto-reset). Class fix — one owner function, all sites migrated
- [ ] **Fix 2 (no fork on read failure)**: `disk=0` recovery must not mint a new session id while the old one is alive; preserve id, or at minimum stamp lineage (`parent_session_id`) + key handoff (close predecessor / release key)
- [ ] **Fix 3 (restart resolution)**: resolve chat→session by `(session_key, NOT ended, max(last_activity_at))`; log + prefer a newer sibling when the keyed row is stale; heals historical damage automatically
- [ ] **Recovery tooling**: `hermes sessions repair` (or doctor extension) — detect orphan gateway sessions (key=NULL but gateway-shaped traffic), re-stamp from message content/origin, mark superseded predecessors
- [ ] **Warning UX**: reword `disk=0 ... possible FTS write corruption` so it doesn't read as hardware failure; surface a user-visible degraded-state notice instead of a silent WARNING
- [ ] Verify overlap with / salvage the related PRs above rather than duplicating

## Recovery (for affected users, until tooling ships)

The data is not lost. The real conversation lives in the unstamped row. Manual repair = stamp the orphan row with the correct `session_key`/`chat_id`/`origin_json` copied from the stale sibling, and set `ended_at`/`end_reason` on the stale row so restart resolution picks the right one. A guided procedure will be posted in this issue after validation.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — Esc on the Settings page interrupts the running session (global composer.cancel fires outside chat)
items.body:
## Bug Description
In the Desktop app, pressing `Esc` while on the **Settings** page stops/interrupts the currently running session — even though the user is not in the chat view and never meant to cancel the turn.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Hermes Desktop, start a session and let the agent respond (or run a long tool call).
2. While the turn is running, open **Settings** (gear icon).
3. Click anywhere on the page so focus is on a non-editable element (button, label, page background).
4. Press `Esc`.
5. Switch back to chat: the session has been interrupted (turn stopped, `interrupted: true`).

## Expected Behavior
Esc on the Settings page should either do nothing, dismiss the current control, or close/navigate away from Settings — it should **not** interrupt the session, since that's a chat-scoped action.

## Actual Behavior
The running turn is cancelled as if the user pressed the stop button.

## Root Cause
`Esc` is a **global** keybind for `composer.cancel`:
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/keybinds/actions.ts:240` — `{ id: 'composer.cancel', category: 'composer', keys: ['escape'] }`
- The dispatcher (`apps/desktop/src/app/hooks/use-keybinds.ts`) is a capture-phase `window` keydown listener that fires on **every** page/route. Only a few surfaces claim the combo for themselves: the find-in-page bar (`findBarClaimsCombo`, `lib/find-in-page.ts:107`), the session switcher, and keybind capture mode.
- The Settings page (`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/`) is a plain route, not a modal, and registers **no** claim on Esc, so the keystroke falls through to the global dispatcher.
- `composer.cancel` → `cancelRun` (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.ts:620`) → sends `session.interrupt` to the backend and marks the session interrupted.

Note: Esc is suppressed while focus is in an editable input (`comboAllowedInInput`, `lib/keybinds/combo.ts:228` only allows mod/ctrl combos in inputs), so the bug only triggers when focus is on a non-editable element on the settings page.

## Suggested Fix
Follow the existing find-bar ownership pattern: have the Settings route claim `escape` (e.g. a `settingsClaimsCombo('escape')` consulted by the dispatcher, mirroring `findBarClaimsCombo`), and have the Settings page handle Esc itself (dismiss focused control → close Settings / return to chat). This also partially addresses #70656.

## Environment
- macOS
- Hermes Desktop (Electron), recent main

items.title: Desktop: open keep-alive tabs go blank after sleep/wake reclaim (history intact in state.db)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

After macOS sleep/wake (or overnight idle) with Hermes Desktop left open, **already-open chat tabs paint an empty transcript** while shell chrome stays healthy (sidebar, tab titles, composer, “Gateway ready”). **History is not deleted** — `state.db` still has full active message rows. Full app restart (or re-opening the stored session) restores the transcript.

This is a **recovery/UX hole on top of intentional reclaim**, not data loss.

**Recommended priority: P3** — data-safe, intermittent (long sleep + multi-tab keep-alive), workaround exists (restart or re-click session). Worth tracking so it is not rediscovered every few weeks.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|--------|
| Reporter | @VGFreakXBL |
| OS | macOS 15.6.1 |
| Hermes | v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) |
| Install | local git `20fece3b4` |
| Desktop package | `apps/desktop` 0.17.0 |
| Desktop build stamp | `builtAt` 2026-08-08T18:21:47Z, `sourceMode: false` |
| Surface | Hermes Desktop, multi-tab keep-alive open overnight |
| Backend | local embedded serve (Desktop child) |

## Expected vs actual

**Expected**

- After sleep disconnect / orphan reclaim / idle timeout, still-open tabs either:
  1. **Auto-rehydrate** from `stored_session_id` once the gateway is back, or
  2. Show an explicit non-live empty state (“Session ended — click to restore”) instead of a silent blank pane that looks like a live chat.

**Actual**

- Tabs stay mounted with title + chrome + composer.
- Main message pane is blank (watermark only).
- New chat works immediately (gateway healthy).
- Quit/relaunch Desktop self-corrects; history was in DB the whole time.

## Observational evidence (natural hit, 2026-08-09)

Machine left with Desktop up across sleep. After wake, open tabs blank. Investigation before/while recovering:

### Backend ends (not missing rows)

| Open tab title | `session_id` | active msgs in DB | `end_reason` | `ended_at` (local) |
|----------------|--------------|-------------------|--------------|--------------------|
| Hermes HUD Mode Feature | `20260808_122136_084329` | 34 | `ws_orphan_reap` | 2026-08-09 00:04:53 |
| Ops Layer Video Ideas Expansion | `20260808_222710_22bc68` | 58 | `idle_timeout` | 2026-08-09 06:05:59 |
| Scraping Gadget Specs… | `20260806_223700_b0daf1` | 68 | earlier `ws_orphan_reap` | — |
| New chat after wake | `20260809_100817_eafe0b` | live | — | works |

### Gateway / power timeline

From `~/.hermes/logs/gui.log`:

- `2026-08-09 00:04:30` WS closed `client_disconnect(code=1006)` with `detached_sessions=4`, then WS re-accepted
- `wake.start(gui): disabled (enabled=False, surface=auto)`
- HUD reaped ~23s later as `ws_orphan_reap`
- Morning wake: gateway “ready”, MCP discovery noise; **new Desktop session fine**; prior open tabs blank until full app reset

### What is *not* the bug

- Not SQLite wipe / corrupt empty DB (message counts non-zero; restart restores)
- Not full-window GPU black screen (sidebar/tabs/composer paint)
- Not multi-M transcript-clone / “Cannot compress further” zombie (separate class; sessions here were normal size)
- Not “session never existed”

## Root cause (source-grounded)

Three pieces compose the failure mode:

### 1. Backend reclaim is intentional

Live runtimes are ended on WS orphan / idle (`ws_orphan_reap`, `idle_timeout`). Stored rows remain.

### 2. Desktop drops open-tab message cache on `session.reclaimed` and does not rehydrate keep-alive tabs

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts
} else if (event.type === 'session.reclaimed') {
  // Drop the cached state now — the stored row is untouched, so the sidebar keeps the
  // conversation and reopening it resumes from the DB.
  dropSessionState(reclaimedRuntimeId)
  notifySessionsChanged()
  return
}
```

Unit coverage (`session-reclaimed.test.tsx`) asserts **cache drop only**. Comment contract assumes the user **reopens** the conversation. Keep-alive open tabs remain bound to the dead runtime id with empty `$sessionStates` → blank pane.

### 3. Power-resume only reconnects the socket

```ts
// apps/desktop/electron/main.ts
// Sleep silently drops the renderer's WebSocket… renderer reconnects on this signal
webContents.send('hermes:power-resume')

// apps/desktop/src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.ts
const offPowerResume = desktop.onPowerResume?.(() => reconnectNow())
```

`reconnectNow()` restores gateway connectivity (composer no longer stuck on “Starting Hermes…”). It does **not** walk open tabs and `hydrateFromStoredSession` / resume from stored id after reclaim.

## Recreatability

| Mode | Status |
|------|--------|
| **Natural hit** | **High confidence** — multi-tab Desktop left open overnight / across macOS sleep; observe blank open tabs; confirm DB rows + `end_reason` ∈ {`ws_orphan_reap`,`idle_timeout`}; new chat works; restart restores |
| **Forced deterministic e2e** | **Not automated yet** — should be straightforward without multi-hour sleep: open 2+ keep-alive tabs → inject/simulate `session.reclaimed` for their runtime ids (or trigger orphan reap) → assert open tab either rehydrates or shows explicit restore UI; currently only unit tests assert cache drop |
| **Token-heavy sleep repro** | **Not required** for triage if natural DB + log evidence accepted |

Suggested minimal unit/e2e direction (no overnight wait):

1. Mount multi-tab / keep-alive surface with runtime A + stored S and non-empty messages.
2. Fire `session.reclaimed` with `session_id=A`, `stored_session_id=S`, reason `ws_orphan_reap`.
3. **Today:** messages gone, tab still open/blank.
4. **Desired:** auto-hydrate from S **or** explicit “click to restore” empty state (not silent blank live chrome).

## Suggested fix direction (no patch attached)

Preferred (small, matches existing resume path):

1. On `session.reclaimed`, if any open tab/pane still references that runtime id:
   - map to `stored_session_id` from event payload / session list
   - call existing `hydrateFromStoredSession` / `resumeSession` for that tab
   - or demote tab to stored-id-only and load history read-only until next send resumes a runtime
2. On `hermes:power-resume` / successful post-wake reconnect, reconcile open tabs whose runtime is missing from live pool (same hydrate path).
3. If auto-resume is too aggressive, at minimum replace silent blank with an in-pane restore CTA so users do not think history vanished.

Regression: two mounted keep-alive tabs; reclaim B while A focused → B either repaints history or shows restore; A untouched. Restart must not be required.

## User workaround / recourse (current)

1. **Quit and relaunch Desktop** — observed full self-correct (reporter path).
2. **Re-click the session in the sidebar** (forces resume/hydrate from stored id) or close blank tab and reopen same title.
3. **Do not panic-delete sessions** — check `state.db` `message_count` / active rows first; blank UI ≠ missing history.
4. Optional hygiene after long sleep: one clean relaunch to shed zombie open tabs on dead runtimes.

## Related issues (cross-link; not pure duplicates)

| Issue | Why related / why distinct |
|-------|----------------------------|
| #44183 | orphan reap grace / session lost after sleep — backend timing; this issue is **open-tab blank after reclaim with DB intact** |
| #53374 | Windows sleep creates **new** session / context lost — different symptom |
| #67502 | draft “session not found” when live dies — draft path, not keep-alive blank transcript |
| #72046 | empty UI when **state.db corrupt** — here DB is healthy |
| #69940 / #77127 | WS disconnect / orphan / resume races — adjacent transport class |
| #74551 | sleep/wake wires wrong profile backend — different identity bug |

Please **do not close as dupe of #44183/#53374** without checking: those are about losing/replacing the live session; this report is specifically **keep-alive tabs left blank after intentional cache drop without rehydrate**.

## Labels / triage ask

- `type/bug` `comp/desktop` `area/sessions` **`P3`**
- Optional: leave off `needs-repro` if natural hit + source map is enough; otherwise natural repro steps above are sufficient (no multi-M forced repro needed)

## Reporter note

Identified on a live machine after wake; full app reset recovered UI. Filing so the reclaim/power-resume gap is explicit: **dropping runtime cache is fine; leaving open tabs silently empty is not.**

items.title: Telegram gateway hangs at 'Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)' on macOS 26 — init deadlock (reproducible in fresh uv venv)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary
`hermes gateway run` hangs indefinitely at:
```
WARNING ...adapter: [Telegram] Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS…
WARNING ...adapter: [Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…
```
The Telegram adapter never completes initialization. No timeout fires, no error is logged, no connection to Telegram is ever opened. The gateway stays "running" but is deaf.

This affects **both long-polling and webhook modes** — webhook registration (`setWebhook`) may succeed, but the adapter still deadlocks immediately after, so no updates are ever received.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), upstream `c9411b72`, local `3d7dda4c`
- Install method: git
- Python 3.11.15 (bundled venv at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv`)
- macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Reproduced with the desktop app (Hermes.app) fully closed and no other Hermes process running.

## What works (rules out network / credentials)
- `curl https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getMe` → `ok`, returns bot username.
- `curl .../getUpdates` → `ok`.
- DoH providers `dns.google` and `cloudflared-dns.com` resolve in <0.25s (HTTP 200).
- `cloudflared` quick tunnel to localhost:8443 produces a reachable `*.trycloudflare.com` host.
- `setWebhook` via the gateway registers successfully: `getWebhookInfo` returns `last_error: None`, `pending_update_count: 0`. Yet the adapter still hangs right after.
- Token, `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`, and `.env` are all correct.

Conclusion: the bug is in the **gateway/adapter startup path on macOS**, not in credentials, network, DNS, or the Telegram Bot API.

## Reproduction
1. Configure a valid `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` in `~/.hermes/.env`.
2. Close the Hermes desktop app (if running).
3. Run `hermes gateway run` (or `hermes gateway`).
4. Observe it logs "Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs…" then "Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…" and never proceeds.

## Thread dump (evidence of the deadlock)
Captured with `sample <pid> 1` while hung. Main thread is parked in the asyncio selector (`kevent`); worker threads are all blocked in `SimpleQueue.get` waiting for work that never arrives. **No network socket to Telegram is open** at the time of the hang.

```
    847 Thread_6751098   DispatchQueue_1: com.apple.main-thread  (serial)
    +                         ! 846 kevent  (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) + 8
    847 Thread_6751125
    +                       847 _queue_SimpleQueue_get  (in python3.11) + 216
    +                         847 _queue_SimpleQueue_get_impl  (in python3.11) + 284
    +                           847 PyThread_acquire_lock_timed  (in python3.11) + 340
    (Threads 6751229–6751237: identical — blocked in SimpleQueue.get / pthread_cond_wait)
```

`lsof -i` on the gateway PID shows **zero** TCP connections to Telegram — it never reaches the connect phase.

## Additional confirmation
A **fresh venv built with `uv sync --frozen`** (replicating the exact dependency set) reproduces the **identical** deadlock (same `kevent` + `SimpleQueue.get` frames, zero Telegram connections). This rules out a corrupted/broken local venv build (e.g. `cryptography`/`cffi`) as the cause — the bug is in the gateway/adapter startup code interacting with macOS 26 (Tahoe) + Python 3.11 + the asyncio event loop.

## Analysis
- The adapter logs "attempt 1/8" from the retry ladder but the ladder never advances, never escalates, and never times out.
- The code contains an internal diagnostic for exactly this symptom (`#63309` / `_LOOP_BLOCKED_DUMP_GRACE`, "the loop thread appears BLOCKED in a synchronous call"), but that only *reports* the hang — it does not recover.
- Multiple async timeouts exist in `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` (`_UPDATER_START_TIMEOUT`, `_POLLING_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT`, etc.), yet none fire. The event loop is alive (in `kevent`) but the initialization task that should drive the connect is never scheduled/completed, so worker threads wait forever on an empty `SimpleQueue`.
- The deadlock is **not** specific to polling: it occurs identically in webhook mode after `setWebhook`, confirming it is in the shared adapter init path, not the polling loop.

## Impact
Telegram integration is completely non-functional on macOS v0.20.0. Users cannot chat with their agent via Telegram at all. Webhook mode does not bypass it.

## Suggested direction for a fix
The init task appears to be dropped/never awaited on macOS under the gateway supervisor. Likely culprits to inspect:
- The cold-start readiness gate / `_await_with_thread_deadline` path in `adapter.py` (anyio cancellation shielding around `initialize()`).
- Whether the Telegram init coroutine is correctly scheduled onto the gateway's event loop vs. a loop that has already stopped processing.
- The fallback-IP / DoH discovery (`telegram_network.py`) interleaving with PTB's `start_polling`/`start_webhook` init — even though DoH itself returns fast, the *sequencing* of the discovery task and the connect task may leave the connect task unscheduled.

A minimal recovery would be: if the init task is not done within a bounded window, surface a fatal error and let the reconnect ladder (or `KeepAlive`) restart cleanly — instead of silently parking forever.

items.title: Gateway suppresses final send on interrupted stream — partial with ▉ cursor left as only delivery (streamed=True previewed=False content_delivered=True)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

On Telegram, an interrupted stream can leave only a partial message ending with the streaming cursor `▉` in the chat, while the gateway logs:

```
Suppressing normal final send for session <key>: final delivery already confirmed (streamed=True previewed=False content_delivered=True).
```

and the complete response is never delivered (or arrives ~20s later only via a separate path). On agent-to-agent channels this reads as message loss: the recipient only ever sees a truncated fragment ending with the cursor.

## Evidence

1. **Windows gateway**, after a session recovery/recreation event: the agent transcript contains the full ack text, but the chat only ever received a short partial ending with `▉`. Two further attempts froze after only a few characters.
2. **Windows gateway**: the suppression line above was logged for a ~200-char response; the first visible copy was a partial ending with `▉`; the full text arrived only ~20s later as a second message (not an edit).
3. **macOS gateway**: the same suppression for a ~2000-char response immediately after the max-iterations summary path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the Hermes gateway against a Telegram group (edit-based streaming, default cursor ` ▉`).
2. Trigger a stream interruption mid-generation: session recovery/recreation (ended-but-live routing key), max-iterations summary, or a model/API failure while the reply is being generated.
3. Observe: the first visible message is a partial ending with `▉`; the log shows `Suppressing normal final send ... (streamed=True previewed=False content_delivered=True)`; the complete text never arrives (or only much later via a second delivery).

## Expected Behavior

The complete final text is always delivered. A partial preview with a stuck cursor must never satisfy the "final delivery already confirmed" check — `previewed=False` with no verifiable delivered payload should never suppress the normal final send.

## Actual Behavior

Suppression fires with `previewed=False`; only a partial-with-cursor is visible.

## Suspected Cause

`gateway/run.py` suppression block (~L26520–26600): `_stream_confirmed_final_delivery()` returns True via the legacy-trust path — `final_response_sent=True` with `delivered_final_matches` returning `None` (no payload record on an interrupted/non-split path) is trusted even though the visible content was a partial. The #71643 reconciliation only overrides on an explicit `False` mismatch; a missing record on an interrupted stream is indistinguishable from a clean one. The stream consumer also sets `final_content_delivered=True` after delivering only a prefix (the `Flushing text batch` partial), and the failed-finalize cursor-strip (`_try_strip_cursor` in `stream_consumer.py`) is not guaranteed when the stream is interrupted.

Suggested fix direction: do not suppress when `previewed=False` **and** the consumer cannot produce a payload record matching the final text; on interrupted streams, always fall through to the normal final send. This is the mirror case of #51605 (double reply when `previewed=True` but `content_delivered=False`).

## Environment

- Hermes gateway, Python 3.13+; Windows and macOS
- Telegram supergroup (forum topics enabled)
- `streaming.enabled: false` in config does **not** prevent the partial+cursor first delivery

## Related

- #71643 — successful finalize edit can carry only the last preview snapshot
- #51605 — inverse: double reply when previewed=True but content_delivered=False
- #55806 — queued follow-up resends when stream delivery confirmation fails
- #49687 — Feishu streaming: final_content_delivered flagged too early
- #78541 — payload-less multi-message split delivery

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop app does not self-heal a dropped remote connection (SSH / HTTP) — manual re-entry of connection details is required to recover
items.body:
### Bug Description

The Hermes desktop app, when used in remote mode (over SSH, and previously over HTTP), does not recover on its own after a connection drop. It gets stuck in a boot/connection error state and keeps failing until the user manually deletes and re-enters the connection details. The remote host is healthy the whole time; the app simply does not attempt to reconnect.

Observed error messages:
- "Could not verify the existing SSH backend"
- "Desktop boot failed"
- "Hermes couldn't start ... SSH connection failed"
- (over HTTP, earlier) "Remote gateway incomplete", "ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE / ERR_CONNECTION_RESET"

Re-entering the same connection details (host, user, port, key path) makes the connection work again immediately, which proves the server was never the problem.

### Steps to Reproduce

Configure the desktop app in remote mode over SSH (host, user, port, key path) and connect successfully.
Cause the connection to drop in any way — e.g. close the SSH socket, restart the app, or interrupt the network between client and host.
Relaunch / attempt to reconnect.
Observe that the app does not reconnect on its own. It shows a boot/connection error ("Could not verify the existing SSH backend") and no further connection attempt is made.
Note that deleting and re-entering the exact same connection details restores the connection immediately.

### Expected Behavior

A dropped remote connection should be treated as a normal, recoverable condition. The app should automatically reconnect (with bounded retries and backoff) instead of requiring the user to manually re-enter the connection data.


### Actual Behavior

After any remote connection drop, the app remains stuck in a failed state and does not attempt to reconnect. The user is blocked from all agent work (tools, terminal, files, model calls) until they manually delete and re-enter the connection details, which then works immediately. This happens over both SSH and HTTP remote modes.


### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
(sanitized)
version:          0.20.0 [326bdfb7]
os:               Darwin 25.6.0 arm64
python:           3.11.15
openai_sdk:       2.24.0
profile:          default
hermes_home:      ~/.hermes
model:            deepseek-v4-flash:0731
provider:         ollama-cloud
terminal:         local
features:
  toolsets:           hermes-cli
  memory_provider:    built-in
  gateway:            stopped (launchd)
  platforms:          none
  cron_jobs:          4 active / 4 total
  skills:             91
config_overrides:
  display.streaming: True
  display.show_reasoning: False
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.6.1 (arm64, Darwin 25.6.0)

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) · commit 326bdfb7a

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
The server side shows no error — SSH over Tailscale succeeds (ssh returns OK, hostname correct), and the remote host is reachable. No server-side failure is logged during the client-side "SSH connection failed" state, confirming the failure is client-side reconnect handling only.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The desktop app appears to cache a stored remote-connection state (SSH and HTTP) and does not invalidate/rebuild it after a connection drop. Instead of treating the drop as a normal recoverable condition and re-establishing the connection, it stays in a failed state until the connection is manually re-entered. The identical symptoms over both SSH and HTTP point to a shared remote-connection lifecycle gap rather than a transport-specific bug.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Implement automatic reconnect for remote mode: on a dropped connection, invalidate the cached connection state and re-establish it (with bounded retries and backoff), so the user is not forced to manually re-enter connection details. This should cover both SSH and HTTP remote modes via the shared remote-connection lifecycle.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

items.title: Desktop fails to boot — react-router duplicated across chunks breaks the Router context

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
What happens
A clean install never reaches the UI. The window renders the root error boundary:

Something broke in the interface useLocation() may be used only in the context of a <Router> component.

Retry and Reload window do not help. Clearing the Electron caches under %APPDATA%\Hermes\{Cache,GPUCache,Code Cache} does not help. The crash is logged before the backend has even finished starting, so it is independent of backend state or provider configuration.

From %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\desktop.log:

[renderer console] Error: useLocation() may be used only in the context of a <Router> component.
  (…/app.asar/dist/assets/vendor-react-R-OdkZd7.js:8)
[renderer console] [error-boundary:root] Error: useLocation() may be used only in the context of a <Router> component.
    at Z8e (…/assets/index-DQ0KkR40.js:256:57639)
    …
    at Ee (…/assets/command-DWj4Isno.js:1:2728)
    at dt (…/assets/command-DWj4Isno.js:1:12400)
Steps to reproduce
Install Hermes Desktop on Windows via Hermes-Setup.exe
Launch the app
Root cause
main.tsx mounts <HashRouter> correctly, so the Router is present. The problem is that react-router is emitted into three separate chunks, so the Router context object the provider writes to is not the one the consumer reads from:

$ grep -rl "may be used only in the context of a" apps/desktop/dist/assets
apps/desktop/dist/assets/command-DWj4Isno.js
apps/desktop/dist/assets/hooks-CwQiRfzw.js
apps/desktop/dist/assets/index-DQ0KkR40.js
command-*.js is the chunk in the stack trace above: the command palette gets its own copy of react-router, and useLocation() there cannot see the HashRouter mounted from the entry chunk.

In apps/desktop/vite.config.ts, react-router is matched by neither the vendor-react group nor resolve.dedupe:

{ name: 'vendor-react', test: /node_modules[\\/](react|react-dom|scheduler)[\\/]/ },
…
dedupe: ['react', 'react-dom']
The (react|react-dom|scheduler)[\\/] alternation requires a path separator directly after the package name, so node_modules/react-router/ does not match. The comment right above the group list already predicts this failure mode — "an unmatched module shared by the entry and a heavy chunk gets merged INTO the heavy chunk" — it just was not applied to react-router.

Fix
-            { name: 'vendor-react', test: /node_modules[\\/](react|react-dom|scheduler)[\\/]/ },
+            { name: 'vendor-react', test: /node_modules[\\/](react|react-dom|scheduler|react-router)[\\/]/ },
-    dedupe: ['react', 'react-dom']
+    dedupe: ['react', 'react-dom', 'react-router']
Verification
After npm run build && npm run builder in apps/desktop:

$ grep -rl "may be used only in the context of a" apps/desktop/dist/assets
apps/desktop/dist/assets/vendor-react-QKvrQxCl.js
One chunk instead of three; the app boots normally.

A regression guard would be cheap here — a post-build assertion that react-router resolves to exactly one chunk, in the same spirit as the existing scripts/assert-dist-built.mjs.

items.title: Settings → Plugins tears down the whole view when a plugin row has no key
items.body:
What happens
Opening Settings → Plugins replaces the entire app with the root error boundary:

Something broke in the interface Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')

Steps to reproduce
Connect Desktop to a Hermes backend (reproduced against 0.20.0 over Remote gateway, and against the bundled local backend)
Open Settings → Plugins
(Requires the Issue 1 fix to be reachable at all.)

Root cause
apps/desktop/src/store/agent-plugins.ts declares key as required:

export interface AgentPluginRow {
  name: string
  /** Canonical registry key (e.g. `image_gen/fal`) — names can collide. */
  key: string
  …
}
The gateway does not always send it. The row renderer already accounts for that (plugins-settings.tsx:239):

<AgentPluginRowView key={row.key || row.name} row={row} />
…but two other call sites in the same file dereference key unguarded, and both run before rendering, so a single keyless row takes down the whole Settings tree rather than one entry:

// line 42 — the filter
const isDesktopRelevant = (row: AgentPluginRow) =>
  !HIDDEN_KEY_PREFIXES.some(prefix => row.key.startsWith(prefix))

// line 188 — the search filter
row.key.toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
Fix (UI side)
-const isDesktopRelevant = (row: AgentPluginRow) => !HIDDEN_KEY_PREFIXES.some(prefix => row.key.startsWith(prefix))
+const isDesktopRelevant = (row: AgentPluginRow) =>
+  !HIDDEN_KEY_PREFIXES.some(prefix => (row.key || row.name || '').startsWith(prefix))
         !needle ||
-        row.name.toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
-        row.key.toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
-        row.description.toLowerCase().includes(needle)
+        (row.name || '').toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
+        (row.key || '').toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
+        (row.description || '').toLowerCase().includes(needle)
Worth deciding on your side
The patch above stops the crash, but it treats a symptom. The real question is which side of the contract is wrong:

If key is genuinely optional, the interface should say key?: string so TypeScript surfaces every unguarded access — there may be more beyond this file.
If key is meant to always be present, the gateway is the bug and it should be fixed there instead.
Either way, an error boundary scoped to the plugin list (rather than the root) would keep one malformed row from taking out all of Settings.

items.title: [Bug]: projects.tree returns sessionCount=1 but an empty lane "sessions" array for a non-git project (server-side, not a client cache issue)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

A project backed by a non-git workspace folder reports a correct session count in projects.tree but returns an empty lane sessions array in the same payload. The desktop app renders the project lane as empty, even though the server knows a session belongs to it.

This is server-side, not a client cache issue: fully deleting and re-creating the remote connection (which forces a fresh project-tree fetch) does not change the result. Verified by querying projects.tree directly against the serve backend with hydrate: true — the same payload reports the count and an empty lane.

Related but distinct from existing issues:

#62165 (non-git project renders a session TWICE — backend lane is clean, client overlay duplicates)
#65004 (chats lose their project association over time / disappear from the sidebar) Those are client- or lifecycle-side. This one is backend-side: the lane sessionCount and the lane sessions contents disagree in the server's own response.

### Steps to Reproduce

Have an explicit project whose primary folder is NOT a git repository.
Have a session whose cwd equals that project folder (git_branch and git_repo_root are null on the session).
Query the projects.tree RPC against the serve backend with hydrate: true.
Observe that the project reports sessionCount: 1 but the lane's sessions array is empty in the same payload.
In the desktop app (SSH or HTTP remote mode), the project shows as empty.
Fully re-creating the remote connection does not change the empty lane.

### Expected Behavior

When `hydrate: true`, the lane `sessions` array should contain the sessions the
project counts. `sessionCount` and the lane contents should always agree.

### Actual Behavior

The `projects.tree` payload reports `sessionCount: 1` for the project but the
corresponding lane `sessions` array is empty, with `hydrate: true`. The desktop
app renders the project lane empty even though the server counted a session.
Re-creating the remote connection has no effect, confirming the failure is in
the backend response.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation, CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
(sanitized)
Version:          0.20.0
os:               Darwin 25.6.0 arm64
python:           3.11.15
profile:          default
terminal:         local
features:
  memory_provider:    built-in
  platforms:          none
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.6.1 (arm64, Darwin 25.6.0)

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) · commit 7aecab56d

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Verified by querying projects.tree directly with hydrate=true:
project sessionCount=1 but lane sessions=[] in the same payload. The backend
grouping logic (_project_for_session) correctly assigns the session to the
project; the failure is in lane session hydration for non-git workspace folders.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The session is correctly assigned to the project (count=1), and lane placement
(_place in tui_gateway/project_tree.py) resolves correctly for the non-git cwd
(returns is_main=true with the cwd as the lane key). However, with hydrate=true
the lane's sessions array comes back empty while the count is preserved. This
points to lane session hydration not being populated for non-git workspace
folders on the projects.tree RPC path.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Ensure that when hydrate=true, the lane sessions array is populated with the sessions the project counts, including sessions in non-git workspace folders. sessionCount and the lane contents should always be consistent.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Desktop: UI zoom silently drops to 100% (settings still show 90%) when launching/exiting another Electron app (Antigravity) on macOS
items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, **launching or quitting Antigravity IDE** (Google's Electron-based app) while Hermes desktop is running makes the Hermes window visibly "jump" once, and the entire UI (fonts, icons, spacing) renders ~11% larger — i.e. at Chromium's 100% baseline instead of the configured **90%**. The UI Scale control in Settings **still shows 90%** and there is no way to re-apply it from the UI (clicking the already-selected 90% emits no change). Restarting Hermes restores 90%. This belongs to the known zoom-reset family (#60693, #81879, #79863), but with a distinct trigger and a specific gap in the reassert logic.

## Environment

- macOS 26.6.1 (Apple Silicon, MacBook Pro 16", display 3456×2234 @ 120 Hz, DPR 2.0)
- Hermes desktop **client (Electron shell): v0.17.0** — running binary `apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app` (verified: `Info.plist` `CFBundleShortVersionString` = 0.17.0, `app.getVersion()` = 0.17.0)
- Hermes agent **backend: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)** — `hermes --version` / `pyproject.toml`. (The client and backend version independently; the status bar shows both.)
- Antigravity IDE v2.5.0 (Google, Electron 41.0.2, arm64 native)
- Settings → Appearance → UI Scale: **90%**

## Steps to reproduce

1. Hermes desktop running, UI Scale set to 90% (confirmed in `zoom-state.json`).
2. Launch Antigravity; then quit it. (Happens on **both** open and exit.)
3. Observed: the Hermes window "jumps" once; every in-window element (text, icons, spacing) renders ~11% larger.
4. Settings → Appearance still shows **90%**; clicking the 90% preset does nothing. `Cmd+0` (View → Actual Size), switching 100%→90% in Settings, or restarting Hermes restores 90%.

Note: the window *frame* (native titlebar/traffic lights) does **not** change size — only the page content scales, consistent with a `webContents` zoom change rather than a display-level change.

## Expected vs. Actual

- **Expected:** UI stays at the persisted 90% zoom.
- **Actual:** the runtime zoom silently becomes 100% while every persisted layer (main-process state file, Chromium Preferences, Settings UI) still says 90% — the desync is invisible to the app itself.

## Evidence chain

1. **Runtime really is 100% (pixel-measured).** The sidebar width is a fixed design token (`14.8125rem` = 237 CSS px). In a 2× Retina capture of the drifted state, the sidebar/content boundary was measured at **473 px** (boundary x=585, window content origin x=112), i.e. `237 × 2.0` = 100%. At 90% it should be 426.6 px. (Screenshot available on request.)
2. **All persisted layers say 90%.**
   - `~/Library/Application Support/Hermes/zoom-state.json` → `{"zoomLevel": -0.5778829311823857}` = `log(0.9)/log(1.2)`
   - Chromium `Preferences` → `partition.per_host_zoom_levels` → every URL record = `-0.5778829311823857`
3. **Settings UI mirrors the persisted value, not the runtime.** The renderer `$zoomPercent` store (`apps/desktop/src/store/zoom.ts`) only updates when the main process emits `hermes:zoom:changed`. The main process is never told the runtime zoom was dropped, so the UI is stuck showing 90% and there is no UI path that forces a re-apply.
4. **Reassert gap (source-level, current `main`, commit 244d296646).** `installZoomReassertOnWindowEvents` (`apps/desktop/electron/zoom.ts`, `zoomReassertWindowEvents`) only listens to `show / restore / resized / moved`. During the trigger, a poller sampling `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` + `CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode` every 250 ms recorded **no window bounds change and no display mode change** — so none of the reassert events fire. `display-metrics-changed` is wired in `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` only to `reposition` (~line 12412), **not** to zoom reassert.
5. **Why Antigravity specifically.** Both apps are Electron. There is upstream evidence of Antigravity disrupting the display/GPU stack of *other* Electron apps on recent macOS (desktop/desktop#22237, electron/electron#51761). The transient re-normalization occurs below the CGWindow/CGDisplay layer — invisible to the poller above — so the jump + zoom reset happen with zero window-level events, and the reassert never runs.

## Workarounds (user-visible)

- `Cmd+0` (View → Actual Size) → resets to `DEFAULT_ZOOM_LEVEL`, which is 90% by design (`zoom.ts`). Instant, no restart.
- Settings → switch UI Scale to 100% then back to 90% (forces the IPC + re-apply).
- Restart Hermes.

## Suggested fix

1. **Add `display-metrics-changed` (Electron `screen` module) to the reassert trigger set** — same approach as #76908, but covering per-app display re-normalization, not just sleep/wake/connect/disconnect topology.
2. **More robust: compare-and-reassert.** After any app activation and/or on a low-frequency timer, read `webContents.getZoomLevel()` and re-apply the persisted level on mismatch. The drift is currently undetectable by *any* event Hermes listens to; `getZoomLevel()` is cheap and closes the class of bugs, not just this trigger.
3. **Related latent path:** stale `partition.per_host_zoom_levels` records can override the applied zoom on SPA navigation (#79863) — clearing those records for the app origin would remove a second silent-reset path.

## Related

#60693 (umbrella), #76908 (display-topology PR), #75305, #75495, #81879 (focus/Alt+Tab), #79863 (per-URL zoom records)

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop plain-Enter submit silently deleted ~65 messages — stale truncate_before_user_ordinal + auto-attached confirm_truncate (3rd occurrence after #70516, #80763)

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Third occurrence of silent session-history loss on the Desktop client.
Previous cases: #70516 (308 messages) and #80763 (244 messages). Both merged
fixes left this path open — this report shows an in-range, valid ordinal with
`confirm_truncate: true` executing a destructive `replace_messages()` while the
user did nothing but press Enter.

## Evidence (session 20260810_005823_2ff555)

gui.log:
```
04:19:13  truncating session ad9ba5fc history 364 -> 326 messages (ordinal=103)
04:20:22  truncating session 50b1c3f6 history 328 -> 298 messages (ordinal=89)
```

Earlier truncations in the same session (03:52, 03:55, 03:57) used ordinals
107 / 110 / 110. The 04:19:13 truncation used ordinal=103 — moving BACKWARD by
7 with no user rewind/edit action. A plain Enter submit at 04:19:14 (persisted
as id 39055) ran against the already-truncated 326-message history. The
session's DB copy ends at 299 messages (ids 38757→39055); ~65 messages are
gone and unrecoverable (WAL empty, FTS external-content table deleted in sync,
no backup).

## Why the existing guards don't cover this

- #70895 (after #70516) only blocks empty truncation (ordinal 0).
- #80802 (after #80763) only blocks submits WITHOUT `confirm_truncate`; the
  Desktop front-end auto-attaches it in `truncateSubmitParams()` (rewind.ts)
  whenever an ordinal is present, so the gateway can't distinguish a genuine
  rewind from a stale leaked ordinal.
- #69109 (open) fixes stale BACKEND in-memory history (cross-client); here the
  gateway's history was fresh — the ordinal itself was stale on the FRONT-END
  side.
- #82514 (open) maps out-of-range ordinals to 4018; ordinal=103 was in-range
  and valid, so it wouldn't be rejected.

## Root cause hypothesis

The truncation point is addressed by `truncate_before_user_ordinal` — an index
into a front-end-derived user-message list. The ordinal can go stale (edit /
composer / history-browse state leakage) while the gateway treats any in-range
ordinal with `confirm_truncate` as authorized and executes `replace_messages()`
— an unrecoverable hard delete with no snapshot.

## Suggested fix direction

Replace ordinal-based addressing with **message_id**-based truncation:
- Front-end sends `truncate_before_message_id` instead of (or in addition to)
  the ordinal.
- Back-end resolves the id against the DB, validates it still exists and
  belongs to the session, then truncates. Unknown/out-of-range id -> refuse
  without touching data.
- Keep the ordinal path for backward compatibility.
- Add soft-delete/snapshot before `replace_messages()` as a data-safety floor.

I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR.

items.title: Test sessions leak into the developer's production state.db (fixture-escape class) — 700+ junk open keyed rows

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
# Test sessions leak into the developer's production state.db (fixture-escape class)

## Evidence

Read-only sweep of a production `~/.hermes/state.db` (during the #82616 investigation) found hundreds of zero-message "open" gateway session rows with test-fixture identities, dated Jul 24–29 2026:

- `agent:main:telegram:dm:123` — **516 rows** (bursts of 8-10 rows per second, e.g. 09:30:27–09:31 on Jul 28)
- `agent:main:telegram:dm:chat-1` — 112 rows (+28 under `dm:chat-1:topic-1`)
- `agent:main:telegram:dm:a` / `dm:b` — 10 each
- `agent:main:weixin:dm:wx-chat` — 15
- `agent:main:telegram:dm:42`, `dm:1` — stragglers (dm:1 rows dated Aug 8, so the escape may still be live)

All are `ended_at IS NULL` with `message_count=0` — permanent junk "open keyed rows".

## Why it matters beyond hygiene

1. **The `_isolate_hermes_home` autouse fixture is supposed to make this impossible** — something bypasses it. Candidate classes: module-level `SessionDB()` / `SessionStore()` construction that resolves `HERMES_HOME` before the fixture patches it; subprocesses spawned by tests without the patched env; direct `_default_db_path()` callers. Note `hermes_state.py` gained `_ensure_test_isolation()` (fail-hard when a pytest-context process resolves the production DB) — these rows either predate it or come through a path it doesn't cover (non-pytest-context subprocess?).
2. **Junk open keyed rows are exactly the population restart-recovery queries scan.** #82633's recency ranking makes a wrong pick unlikely, but hundreds of open rows per key is adversarial input to any resolution logic, and it skews `sessions stats`, hygiene sweeps, and retention pruning.

## Suggested work

- [ ] Identify the escaping path: grep test tree for the fixture identities (`dm:123`, `chat-1`, `wx-chat`, `dm:a`/`dm:b`) and audit which of those tests spawn subprocesses or construct stores at import time; check whether the Aug 8 `dm:1` rows reproduce on current main (would prove the guard hole is still open)
- [ ] Extend the isolation guard to cover the escaping path (env-inheritance for subprocess-spawning tests; forbid production-path resolution in any process whose ancestor is pytest)
- [ ] One-shot cleanup: extend `hermes sessions prune`/gc to drop zero-message, never-active keyed rows older than N days (safe by construction — nothing references them)

Found during #82616; separate class, filed separately.

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
