items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Users who opt in to native OpenAI Responses server-side compaction need temporary provider failures to follow the normal retry policy without disabling compaction for the rest of the session. A transient failure that merely mentions `context_management` or `compact_threshold` can currently look like an explicit parameter rejection and silently downgrade the session.

The opt-in also needs the same boolean semantics as the rest of Hermes configuration. False-like string values such as `"false"` and `"off"` must remain disabled instead of becoming truthy Python strings.

### Proposed Solution

Require a status 400 response plus explicit rejection language before using the one-shot fallback that removes native compaction. Pass the parsed HTTP status from the conversation loop into that predicate, keep all transient failures on the normal retry path, and parse `compression.codex_responses_native` with the shared truthy-value helper.

Add focused behavior tests for non-400 failures, transient errors that name the fields, and true-like and false-like string configuration values.

### Alternatives Considered

- Matching field names alone was rejected because transient provider and transport failures can include those names without rejecting the parameter.
- Disabling native compaction after every related failure was rejected because it converts temporary provider failures into a session-long feature downgrade.
- Using Python `bool()` was rejected because every non-empty string, including `"false"`, evaluates to true.

### Feature Type

Performance / reliability

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

N/A - verified with focused automated regression tests on current main.

items.title: [Bug] agent.max_turns accepts 'none'/'unlimited' in config.yaml but crashes or silently falls back to default

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Description

`agent.max_turns` in `config.yaml` only accepts positive integers. Setting it to natural "no limit" spellings — `none`, `unlimited`, `0`, `-1` — either crashes `int()` or is silently skipped by `or` checks, falling back to the default. There is no way to express "unlimited turns" through config.

YAML parses unquoted `none` as the string `"none"` (not Python `None`). Since `"none"` is truthy, `or`-chain fallbacks like `_cfg.get("max_turns") or 500` never trigger, and downstream `api_call_count < "none"` raises `TypeError`.

## Reproduction

1. In `config.yaml`, set `agent.max_turns: none`
2. Start the gateway or run a cron job
3. Cron scheduler: `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'` in `conversation_loop.py`
4. Gateway: `int("none")` raises `ValueError`, or the `or` fallback silently uses default 90

## Affected code paths

- `cron/scheduler.py:~3256` — `max_iterations = _cfg.get("max_turns") or 500` (same or-chain bug)
- `gateway/run.py:~1662` — `_current_max_iterations()` resolves max_turns without type coercion
- `cli.py:~4105` — `__init__` max-turns resolution

All three sites use bare `int()` or `or`-chains that break on string spellings.

## Proposed solution

Add a single `resolve_turn_limit()` normalization point in `hermes_cli/config.py` that handles: numeric strings, unlimited spellings (none/null/unlimited/infinite/0/-1), YAML None, and garbage → default. All config-reading sites call this instead of bare `int()`.

Related: #75097 (iteration budget semantics diverge), #41050 (goal_mode turn cap). This is the config-layer fix that unblocks both.

items.title: Session auto-title generation fails 100% of the time (HTTP 400) on OpenAI-compatible providers that reject response_format json_schema (vLLM guided_grammar / xgrammar)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

Automatic session title generation silently fails **100% of the time** when the auxiliary `title_generation` provider is an OpenAI-compatible endpoint whose backend translates `response_format: json_schema` into a vLLM `guided_grammar` parameter. The provider rejects the request with HTTP 400 (`compile_grammar_error: No module named 'xgrammar'`), Hermes classifies the 400 as non-retryable, and the session keeps its truncated (derived) title forever. No user-visible error is shown; the only trace is a WARNING in `agent.log`.

The bug shipped with the two-stage title generator (commit `244d296646`), which hardcodes a strict JSON-schema `response_format` on every title-generation call. Providers that honor `json_schema` work; providers that reject it get zero titles.

## Environment

- Hermes agent **backend: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)** — verified via `hermes --version` / `pyproject.toml`
- Hermes desktop **client (Electron shell): v0.17.0** — verified via running binary `Info.plist` (`CFBundleShortVersionString`)
- Commit: `3bd844edf17` (main, 2026-08-09) — title generator file identical to upstream `origin/main`
- OS: macOS 26.6.1; Python 3.11.15 (venv)
- `auxiliary.title_generation`: a custom OpenAI-compatible provider (vLLM-based gateway)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure `auxiliary.title_generation` to use an OpenAI-compatible provider whose backend does not have `xgrammar` installed (i.e. any vLLM endpoint that converts `response_format` `json_schema` into `guided_grammar`).
2. Start a new session and send a message.
3. Observe: the session title is the truncated first message (`title_source = derived`), and `agent.log` contains:

```
WARNING agent.title_generator: Title generation failed: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'guided_grammar \'{"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"title":{"type":"string"}},"required":["title"],"type":"object"}\' has compile_grammar_error: No module named \'xgrammar\'', 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'code': '400'}}
```

## Expected vs. actual

- **Expected:** the title is upgraded to an LLM-generated summary shortly after the first exchange (or the client degrades gracefully when the provider can't do structured output).
- **Actual:** every title-generation attempt fails with HTTP 400; titles stay truncated; failure is invisible to the user.

## Root cause

Three independent problems compound:

1. **Hardcoded strict `json_schema` (no escape hatch).** `agent/title_generator.py:94-104` defines `_TITLE_RESPONSE_FORMAT = {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...}, "strict": true}` and line 404 passes `extra_body={"response_format": _TITLE_RESPONSE_FORMAT}` unconditionally. The call-site `extra_body` **overrides** any config-level `response_format` (`agent/auxiliary_client.py`, `effective_extra_body` merge), so there is no per-provider way to disable structured output for title generation.

2. **400 is treated as non-retryable and non-fallbackable.** In `_call_llm_impl`, only transient transport errors (connection/408/5xx), payment, rate-limit, timeout and auth errors trigger retry or provider fallback. A `400 invalid_request_error` falls into the generic `except` bucket with `is_retryable=False` — no retry, no fallback, no request reshaping. The `_is_transient_transport_error` gate (line ~9103) explicitly excludes 4xx.

3. **The existing loose-JSON fallback is unreachable for this failure mode.** `title_generator.py` already has a loose JSON scan fallback (`_extract_title_text`) intended for providers that *ignore* `response_format` and return plain text — but it never runs when the provider *rejects* the whole request with 400.

## Evidence chain

1. **Real-path reproduction (no curl, no mock):** calling the shipped `generate_title()` through the normal `call_llm` path returns `None` and logs the exact 400 above.
2. **Parameter isolation:** the same call with `response_format: json_schema` → 400; without `response_format` → 200 OK with usable output; with `response_format: json_object` → 200 OK with a valid `{"title": ...}`. This isolates the fault to the `json_schema` type specifically.
3. **Not vendor-specific:** a second, unrelated OpenAI-compatible endpoint also returns 400 for `response_format: json_schema` (`This response_format type is unavailable now`), confirming this is a general "provider doesn't support strict json_schema" gap, not a single-vendor quirk.
4. **Registry evidence:** `state.db` shows `title_source = derived` for every session created after the title generator shipped, and **zero** sessions with an `llm`-generated title on this configuration.
5. **Upstream state:** `git diff HEAD origin/main -- agent/title_generator.py` is empty — the bug is present on current upstream `main`.

## Suggested fix

1. **Degrade on 400 (minimal fix):** when title generation returns `400 invalid_request_error`, retry the same request without `response_format` (or with `json_object`), which the loose-JSON scan already handles. This is a few lines in the title-generator's exception path.
2. **Provider capability signal (better fix):** let providers declare `supports_structured_output` (or auto-probe once), and have `title_generator` skip `response_format` when unsupported — the same guard would benefit other auxiliary tasks that use structured output.
3. **Consider relaxing `strict: true`:** even OpenAI-compatible providers that support `json_schema` often reject `strict` mode; accepting non-strict schemas widens compatibility with no cost to a 1-field title schema.

## Related

- #20305 (title generation silently fails with reasoning models — `max_tokens`) — adjacent symptom, different root cause.
- #18529 (title output contains `<thinking>` tags) — same code path.

items.title: normalize_usage misses reasoning tokens when usage details are dicts (silent 0)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/usage-cost
labels.description: Token accounting, usage reporting, billing, cost tracking

items.body:
## Summary

`normalize_usage` reads the reasoning-token detail with `getattr` only, so it silently returns `0` whenever a provider hands back `usage` whose detail objects are plain `dict`s rather than attribute-bearing objects. The session then records `reasoning_tokens = 0` for a model that is in fact spending most of its output budget on reasoning.

This is the same failure mode the code already documents one line above — just through a different door.

## Where

`agent/usage_pricing.py`, in `normalize_usage` (v0.20.0):

```python
    reasoning_tokens = 0
    # Responses API shape: output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens.
    # Chat Completions shape (OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, etc.):
    # completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens. Reading only the former
    # left reasoning_tokens=0 for every chat_completions reasoning model —
    # hidden thinking was invisible in session accounting even though it
    # dominates output spend on models like deepseek-v4-flash (measured:
    # single calls burning 21K reasoning tokens to emit 500 visible tokens).
    output_details = getattr(response_usage, "output_tokens_details", None)
    if output_details:
        reasoning_tokens = _to_int(getattr(output_details, "reasoning_tokens", 0))
    if not reasoning_tokens:
        completion_details = getattr(response_usage, "completion_tokens_details", None)
        if completion_details:
            reasoning_tokens = _to_int(
                getattr(completion_details, "reasoning_tokens", 0)
            )
```

The comment already names the consequence of missing a shape ("hidden thinking was invisible in session accounting"). The remaining gap is the *container type*, not the key name.

## Why a dict shows up

When usage arrives as JSON that the SDK keeps as an extra/unmodeled field, the nested value stays a `dict`. Then:

```python
output_details = getattr(usage, "output_tokens_details", None)   # -> {'reasoning_tokens': 37}  (truthy)
getattr(output_details, "reasoning_tokens", 0)                   # -> 0   (dict has no attribute)
```

Both branches fall through and `reasoning_tokens` ends as `0`. Verified against `anthropic` 0.87.0 / pydantic 2.13.4:

```
extra flat key   usage.reasoning_tokens        -> readable via getattr
nested extra key usage.output_tokens_details   -> dict, getattr(..., "reasoning_tokens", 0) -> 0
```

There is a related asymmetry worth noting: a provider that reports the value as a **flat** `usage.reasoning_tokens` is readable by `getattr`, but no branch looks for that name, so it is dropped too.

## Impact

Session accounting reports `reasoning_tokens = 0` for models where reasoning is the dominant cost. In one measured deployment the true figure was **68% of output tokens** (16,038 of 23,521 over 15 calls), and ~59% of end-to-end latency was reasoning generation. With `0` in the session table, the natural reading is "this model barely reasons", which points latency investigations in the wrong direction — we spent a while looking at input-context size before pulling the numbers from the proxy's own logs.

The values are not lost upstream; only Hermes's view of them is.

## Suggested fix

Accept both containers, and fall back to the flat key:

```python
def _detail_get(container, key):
    if container is None:
        return 0
    if isinstance(container, dict):
        return container.get(key) or 0
    return getattr(container, key, 0) or 0

reasoning_tokens = _to_int(
    _detail_get(getattr(response_usage, "output_tokens_details", None), "reasoning_tokens")
    or _detail_get(getattr(response_usage, "completion_tokens_details", None), "reasoning_tokens")
    or _detail_get(response_usage, "reasoning_tokens")
)
```

Behaviour is unchanged for every shape that works today; it only adds the dict and flat cases. Given the existing comment's framing — a silent `0` is worse than a crash because nobody notices — being permissive about the container seems consistent with the intent.

## Environment

- hermes-agent v0.20.0, Linux container
- Reached through an OpenAI-compatible proxy using `api_mode: anthropic_messages`

items.title: [Bug] Desktop: clicking a mermaid diagram to expand shows a blank dialog
items.body:
## Bug Description

In the Hermes **desktop app**, clicking a rendered mermaid diagram to open it in the fullscreen zoom viewer shows a **blank/empty panel** — the dialog opens, the bottom toolbar (zoom out / reset / zoom in / copy / close) renders fine, but the diagram itself is not visible.

Inline (non-expanded) mermaid diagrams render perfectly. The ` ```svg ` fence renderer (no zoom wrapper) is unaffected.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop (packaged build v0.20.0, build `2446c8b`), macOS 15.1.
2. Have the assistant send a mermaid diagram, e.g.:

   ````text
   ```mermaid
   flowchart LR
       A[Agent 模型] --> B[聊天消息]
   ```
   ````

3. The inline diagram renders fine (confirming the mermaid lib itself works).
4. Click the diagram to expand (the whole diagram is wrapped in a click-to-expand button).

## Expected Behavior

A dialog (~90vw x 85vh) opens showing the diagram, with pan/zoom via `useZoomPan`.

## Actual Behavior

- The dialog opens, the bottom toolbar is visible.
- The diagram area is **completely blank**.
- Clicking **Reset** (which sets transform to `scale:1, x:0, y:0`) does not make it appear.
- Clicking **Copy** (which calls `copySvgAsPng`) falls back to copying the raw SVG markup as text (pasting into Word yields the SVG source), meaning the PNG rasterization path also fails inside the same context. The SVG string in React state is intact.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 15.1
- Hermes Desktop v0.20.0 (packaged build, `2446c8b`)
- Electron (Chromium renderer)

## Code Locations

- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/embeds/mermaid-embed.tsx` — wraps the diagram in `Zoomable`; overlay is a `div` with `[&_svg]:mx-auto [&_svg]:h-auto [&_svg]:max-h-[80vh] [&_svg]:max-w-[85vw]` and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: svg }}`.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/ui/zoomable.tsx` — `ZoomPanViewer` renders the overlay inside `<div class="absolute inset-0 grid place-items-center"><div class="origin-center" style="transform: translate(0,0) scale(1)">`.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/svg-image.ts` — `copySvgAsPng` catches failure and writes the SVG text to clipboard (observed behavior).

## Root-Cause Leads (verified)

- `mermaid.render()` emits `<svg width="100%" style="max-width: <N>px" viewBox="...">` — width is a percentage, with an inline max-width.
- Inside the overlay, the SVG's width:100% resolves against a grid item whose width is shrink-to-fit (max-content) — a circular dependency. In a plain Chrome headless probe with the same structure the SVG degrades to the replaced-element default 300x150 and is *visible*, but in the real dialog it renders as nothing (blank).
- The SVG data is provably intact: `copySvgAsPng` receives the same string and successfully serializes it (the fallback proves the string round-trips).

Suggestions: give the overlay SVG an explicit width (e.g. drop `width="100%"` handling / set a concrete size, or replace `[&_svg]:h-auto` with a sized wrapper), and make `svgToPngBlob` robust to `width="100%"` (its `svgSize()` currently `parseFloat("100%")` → 100).

## Related

- #55679 ([Feature] Add "Copy Mermaid Source Code" button) is related but not this bug.

items.title: [Bug]: hermes update / bundled-skills sync deletes user-owned skills in bundled categories (2 events) and never restores missing bundled skills

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

A user-owned skill (`pr-signature-templates`, created via `skill_manage(create)`, `created_by=None`) stored in the bundled category directory `~/.hermes/skills/github/` **disappeared twice** within 24h, and the second event took out the *entire* `github/` category plus 49 other bundled skills. This is not a one-off: the sync path has left **50/77 bundled skills missing** from the local profile and **106/203 orphaned entries** in `.usage.json` (skills with `use_count>0` whose directories no longer exist).

## Observed Behavior

**Event 1 (2026-08-08, between 04:09 and 18:02 UTC):** `pr-signature-templates` vanished from disk. Logs show `Tool skill_view returned error: {"success": false, "error": "Skill 'pr-signature-templates' not found."}` at 18:02:49 UTC. The skill was recreated by the agent at 18:03:45 UTC and worked again (last successful `skill_view` 22:07:07 UTC).

**Event 2 (2026-08-09 03:16:42 UTC):** the **whole `~/.hermes/skills/github/` directory was deleted and recreated** (verified via directory birth time) — including the recreated `pr-signature-templates`, and the bundled skills that lived there (`github-auth`, `github-code-review`, `github-issues`, `github-issue-to-pr`, `github-pr-workflow`, `github-repo-management`, `codebase-inspection`). Only `DESCRIPTION.md` and a leftover `.evolution_cache/` skeleton survived.

**Magnitude beyond `github/`:** 50 bundled skills are absent from `~/.hermes/skills/` but present in the runtime bundle (`/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/skills/`, 77 manifest entries). Curator snapshots prove the timeline: `2026-08-02T20-27-14Z/skills.tar.gz` contains `github/github-auth/SKILL.md` etc.; `2026-08-09T21-03-16Z/skills.tar.gz` contains only `github/DESCRIPTION.md` + `github-pr-create/.evolution_cache/`.

## Root Cause

**Two cooperating defects**, both exercised by `hermes update`:

1. **A category-level wipe removes user-owned skills stored alongside bundled ones.** The directory `~/.hermes/skills/github/` was deleted and recreated in its entirety during the window of `hermes update` runs. Both events correlate 1:1 with `hermes update` runs that log "Syncing bundled skills..." (`update.log`: 16:17/16:20 UTC on 08-08 → Event 1; 02:51 UTC on 08-09 → Event 2; the 02:51 run was itself stuck on a "Restore local changes? [Y/n]" prompt). The fix for the closely-related category-wipe bug #75983 (PRs #76066 / #76302) is **closed but never merged**, so the class of bug remains live on main.

   ⚠️ **Open question on the mechanism:** Line-by-line review of `sync_skills()` (`tools/skills_sync.py` lines 675-948) shows that it operates **per skill**, not per category — its only `rmtree` calls (`_rmtree_writable`, lines 795/879/889/899) target individual `dest` paths (a single skill directory or a `.bak` backup), each with guards. The function does **not** contain a destructive `rmtree` of a parent category directory. However, `sync_skills()` is the only thing `hermes update` calls between the git pull and the end of the update that touches `~/.hermes/skills/`, and the wipe correlates 1:1 with those calls. The destructive category-level operation may originate from elsewhere in the update/sync path (e.g. `hermes skills install` as described in #75983, or an interaction with `git stash --include-untracked`), but it was not pinpointed to an exact line. We are reporting this as a correlation with high confidence, not a traced root cause.

2. **Missing bundled skills are never restored — they're classified as "user deleted".** In `tools/skills_sync.py` lines 914-916:
   ```python
   else:
       # ── In manifest but not on disk — user deleted it ──
       skipped += 1
   ```
   Any bundled skill absent from disk is permanently skipped; the sync never re-seeds it. This is the same mechanism documented in #48211 (open, P2) for `--clone`, but here it affects the **default profile via `hermes update`** — after any wipe, there is no automatic recovery path. Users must run `hermes skills reset <name>` individually (and only know to do so if they notice).

## Expected Behavior

- `hermes update` / `sync_skills()` must never delete non-bundled (user-owned or agent-owned) skills that share a category directory with bundled ones.
- Bundled skills missing from disk but present in the runtime should be **re-seeded automatically** unless there is positive evidence the user deleted them (e.g. a curator suppression entry), not silently skipped.
- Ideally, bundled and user skills should live in separate layers (#16852) so a bundled sync cannot touch user content at all.

## Proposed Fix (sketch)

1. **Identify and guard the destructive category-level wipe.** The wipe that deletes `~/.hermes/skills/github/` in its entirety does not come from `sync_skills()`'s per-skill operations (verified by reading the full function body). The update path must be traced end-to-end to find the directory-level `rmtree` — likely in `hermes skills install` / `tools/skills_hub.py` (per #75983) or another path activated during `hermes update`. Once found, guard it against deleting any directory that contains non-bundled skills. The unmerged PRs #76066 / #76302 are the starting point.
2. **Change the "in manifest but not on disk" branch** (lines 914-916) to *restore from the bundled source* unless the name is in the curator suppression list (`.curator_suppressed`) or a `--no-restore` flag/opt-out is set. Keep `skipped` only for genuinely suppressed skills.
3. **Cross-reference `.usage.json` entries** so users get a `hermes skills doctor`-style report naming missing bundled skills with a one-shot `hermes skills reset` recovery.

## Related

- #75983 — `hermes skills install` silently deletes entire category directory (same wipe class; fix PRs #76066/#76302 closed unmerged)
- #48211 — `--clone` copies stale `.bundled_manifest` entries, permanently blocking skill re-seeding (same "user-deleted" classification defect)
- #25120 — `hermes profile install/update` destructively replaces local skills (destructive-sync family)
- #16852 — Skills overlay architecture: separate bundled (upstream) from custom (user) layers (structural fix)
- #44386 / #25150 — preserve user-added skills on install/update (unmerged attempts)
- #56120 — allow rmtree on symlinked skill subtrees + manifest reconcile (unmerged attempt)
- #32497 — Hermes unexpectedly modifies its own skills during normal task execution (related symptom)
- #78004 — skills install resolves/caches by name, not source identifier (same family)

## Environment

- Hermes v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), Linux, default profile only (no named profiles in use)
- `~/.hermes/skills/` default profile
- Logs in local time America/Bogota (UTC-05:00), converted to UTC in this report

---

**🛠️ Dev:** Halldrix
**🤖 Sidekick:** Hermes Agent v0.20.0
**🐞 Reproduction:** ✅ Confirmed (2 events, 2026-08-08 / 2026-08-09, with logs + curator snapshots)

items.title: [Bug] async_delegation batch-complete notifications persist as role=user messages, flooding the transcript

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

Async delegation batch-complete notifications are persisted as **`role=user` messages** in the conversation transcript. In a session that makes heavy use of `delegate_task`, the sidebar/transcript becomes flooded with lines like `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE — deleg_xxx]`, indistinguishable from the user's real input.

Observed on commit `2446c8bb` (Desktop v0.20.0), session `20260809_221757_329ac0`:

- 310 messages total (user 24 / assistant 123 / tool 163)
- **10 messages** with `role='user'` whose content is `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE — deleg_<id>] ... A background fan-out of N sub...`
- **1 message** with `role='user'` whose content is `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY] Earlier turns were compacted into the summ...`

The user's actual inputs are present but buried among the injected notifications — the session reads as "all logs, no conversation".

## Evidence

- `messages` table rows (state.db) show the notifications stored as plain `role='user'` rows. The table has no display-kind column, so the frontend has no way to render them differently from real user input.
- `gui.log` shows the gateway's existing drop path: `Dropping unowned async_delegation notification (...) instead of delivering to session <id>` — notifications are dropped only when unowned; owned ones are delivered into the session as user-role messages.
- Same session also shows `message_count` (28) far below the actual row count (310) after compaction + orphan-reap — a secondary accounting drift, likely from the same abnormal-end path.

## Impact

- Users cannot tell real input from system notifications; transcripts of delegation-heavy sessions are visually corrupted.
- The notifications enter the model context as user turns, distorting the conversation history seen by subsequent turns.

## Suggested fix

- Persist async_delegation notifications with a distinct kind/display marker (e.g. a display-kind column or a dedicated notification store) so the frontend renders them as system notices, not user input.
- Alternatively, do not persist them as transcript rows at all — the batch-complete state is already surfaced through the delegation tool UI.

## Related

- #69227 — async delegation family (profile switch cancels active delegation; different symptom, adjacent subsystem)
- #82872 — ws_orphan_reap ghost tiles (same session population; independent defect)

items.title: [Bug] 2026.8.3 packaging omits all plugin.yaml manifests — platform plugins fail to register

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary
After upgrading 2026.7.20 → 2026.8.3 (brew), **no platform plugin registers** (feishu/discord/slack/teams/...). Gateway logs `No adapter available for feishu`; cron fails with `feishu plugin not registered or missing standalone_sender_fn`. (2026.7.20 was fine.)

## Root cause
The 2026.8.3 install ships **0 `plugin.yaml` manifests**:

```
$ find "$(brew --prefix)/Cellar/hermes-agent" -name plugin.yaml
(empty)
```

`hermes_cli/plugins.py` discovery requires a `plugin.yaml` per plugin directory to build a `PluginManifest`. With 0 manifests, no bundled platform plugin is registered via `_register_deferred_platform`, so `platform_registry` stays empty. `_create_adapter` (gateway/run.py) checks `platform_registry.is_registered("feishu")` → false, then falls through the built-in if/elif chain (which has no `Platform.FEISHU` branch) → returns None.

`plugins/platforms/feishu/` ships `__init__.py` (with a `register(ctx)` entry point) + `adapter.py`, but no `plugin.yaml`, so discovery skips it ("no plugin.yaml, depth cap reached").

## Reproduce
```
brew install hermes-agent          # 2026.8.3
HERMES_PLUGINS_DEBUG=1 hermes gateway run
# [plugins] DEBUG bundled/platforms: 0 manifest(s)
# [plugins] DEBUG Skipping .../plugins/platforms/feishu/__pycache__ (no plugin.yaml, depth cap reached)
# WARNING gateway.run: No adapter available for feishu
```

## Workaround
Create `plugins/platforms/feishu/plugin.yaml`:
```yaml
name: feishu
kind: platform
description: Feishu / Lark messaging platform adapter
```
After this, discovery registers feishu as a deferred platform → gateway connects:
`[Feishu] Connected in websocket mode` + `Gateway running with 2 platform(s)`.

## Expected
Bundled platform plugins should ship their `plugin.yaml` (or discovery should fall back for bundled platform dirs missing the manifest — they worked in 2026.7.20).

## Environment
- hermes-agent 2026.8.3 (brew formula `hermes-agent`)
- Python 3.14.6
- macOS Darwin 25.5.0 (Apple Silicon)

(Note: the separate `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor` / py3.14 `_initializer` crash is already tracked in #58596 and its duplicates; mentioning for completeness since both surface after the 2026.8.3 upgrade.)

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram fallback-IP transport bypasses platform_httpx_limits() — CLOSE_WAIT leak (~18/hr) → EMFILE when no fallback_ips are configured

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

On macOS with **no proxy and no configured Telegram fallback IPs**, the Telegram adapter leaks `CLOSE_WAIT` sockets to `api.telegram.org` at roughly **18/hour** until the process exhausts its file-descriptor limit. Unlike #69314, the adapter does **not** get stuck in `retrying` — it keeps serving traffic while steadily leaking, so the failure is silent until the fd ceiling is hit.

Root cause appears to be that the **fallback-IP transport is explicitly excluded from the `platform_httpx_limits()` keepalive fix**, and that transport is the *default* path for any host that has no `fallback_ips` configured (because the adapter auto-discovers them via DoH and then activates the fallback transport).

The exclusion is documented in-tree, in `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`:

```
# Wire the shared platform_httpx_limits() helper into the httpx client so idle
# keepalive sockets drain aggressively, while preserving PTB's max_connections
...
    A caller-supplied ``limits`` is left untouched; otherwise the
    CLOSE_WAIT-safe limits are injected. The fallback-IP branch does NOT use
    this helper -- see the ``_transport_kwargs`` note below for why.
```

`TelegramFallbackTransport` then sets its own limits with **no `keepalive_expiry`**, so httpx's 5s default applies — the exact value `gateway/platforms/_http_client_limits.py` says is too slow on macOS:

```python
_POOL_LIMITS = httpx.Limits(max_connections=8, max_keepalive_connections=4)
```

`_reset_fallback()` handles CLOSE_WAIT for *fallback* pools (#63311), but the primary pool inside that transport has no equivalent path, and the observed socket count (125 against a pool capped at 8 connections) suggests sockets are orphaned from transports replaced without `aclose()`.

### The failure is self-accelerating

1. Sockets leak on the fallback branch
2. FD pressure rises → **DNS resolution itself begins failing** (`[Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known`)
3. The adapter interprets that as the primary path being dead and switches to a **sticky fallback IP**, permanently
4. Which leaks faster → back to step 2

Log evidence of step 3:

```
WARNING plugins.platforms.telegram.telegram_network: [Telegram] Primary api.telegram.org connection failed
  ([Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known); trying fallback IPs 149.154.166.110
WARNING plugins.platforms.telegram.telegram_network: [Telegram] Primary api.telegram.org path unreachable;
  using sticky fallback IP 149.154.166.110
```

Downstream, fd exhaustion surfaced as failures that look unrelated to Telegram:

```
ERROR cron.scheduler: Job 'followup-tracker' failed: RuntimeError: No reply: the turn was stopped because
  session storage could not be written (the transcript would have been lost on restart)
WARNING gateway.drain_control: drain-control: failed to read .drain_request.json: [Errno 24] Too many open files
WARNING tools.tirith_security: tirith spawn failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **0.20.0** (`v2026.8.3`)
- macOS (Apple Silicon), Python 3.13.14, httpx 0.28.1, httpcore 1.0.9, python-telegram-bot 22.6
- **No proxy.** No `fallback_ips` configured → auto-discovered via DoH
- Default macOS per-process fd limit (256)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the Telegram gateway on macOS with **no** `fallback_ips` configured and no proxy.
2. Observe the adapter log `Auto-discovered Telegram fallback IPs: …` then `Telegram fallback IPs active: …`.
3. Let it run several hours.
4. `lsof -p <gateway-pid> -a -i -n -P | grep -c CLOSE_WAIT` — grows steadily against `api.telegram.org`.

## Measurements

| Metric | After 6h51m uptime | After the workaround, 4h+ |
|---|---|---|
| `CLOSE_WAIT` to api.telegram.org | **128** | **0–1** |
| Total open fds | 353 (ceiling 256) | 147–163 |
| Gateway RSS | **4,033 MB** | 276–398 MB, plateaued |
| `Too many open files` log lines | 4,311 in one day | **0 in 4+ hours** |

The RSS correlation is notable: memory tracked the leaked sockets and dropped ~10× on restart, so this is not only an fd problem.

## Attribution check

The HTTP stack is **byte-identical** between the previously running 0.17.0 and 0.20.0 on this host — `httpx 0.28.1`, `httpcore 1.0.9`, `h11 0.16.0`, `anyio 4.12.1`, `python-telegram-bot 22.6`, `certifi 2026.5.20`. Log history also shows **zero** fd-exhaustion lines before the upgrade day (logs retained back ~2 weeks, including a 14.7h run of the older build). So this looks like a code-path change rather than a dependency regression.

## Workaround (confirmed effective)

```bash
HERMES_TELEGRAM_DISABLE_FALLBACK_IPS=1
```

This routes Telegram onto the direct-DNS branch, which **does** receive the tuned keepalive limits. Log confirms `Telegram fallback-IP transport disabled via env`, and the leak stops (table above). Fallback IPs are only needed on censored/blocked networks, so this is safe for ordinary deployments — but it means the default configuration is the leaky one.

## Suggested fix

Wire `platform_httpx_limits()` into `TelegramFallbackTransport`'s `_transport_kwargs` (both the primary and per-IP fallback pools) so the fallback branch gets the same `keepalive_expiry` as the direct/proxy branches. If the branch is excluded deliberately, it may be worth documenting why in the `_transport_kwargs` note, since the current comment points to a rationale that isn't stated.

A secondary hardening option: treat DNS failure caused by local fd exhaustion differently from a genuinely unreachable primary, so the adapter does not latch onto a sticky fallback IP during a local resource problem and accelerate its own failure.

## Related

- #18451 — the CLOSE_WAIT keepalive class this helper was created for
- #63311 — referenced in `_reset_fallback()` for fd exhaustion via fallback pools
- #69314 — Telegram CLOSE_WAIT **behind a proxy** with the adapter stuck `retrying` (different path: general-vs-polling pool drain; this report is proxy-free and stays "healthy" while leaking)
- #30230 — gateway hitting the macOS 256 fd limit
- #79094 — Mattermost adapter, same missing-connector-tuning class
