items.title: gateway/desktop: durable row-id addressing for rewind truncation (truncate_before_row_id)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

#82756 asked for message-id-based truncation addressing so stale front-end ordinals can never mis-aim a rewind. #82766 (@StanleyStetson) attempted it, but the review found the addressing scheme couldn't resolve in production: the desktop sent `ChatMessage.id` — the renderer's ephemeral synthetic (`${timestamp}-${index}-${role}`) — which no gateway history entry ever carries, so every rewind would have returned 4018. The composite fix that shipped (#82950) corrected the ordinal address space and made the write recoverable, but truncation targeting is still ordinal-based.

This issue tracks the durable version of the idea.

## Design sketch (from the #82766 review)

- **Identity = durable `messages.id` (row id).** The desktop already holds it: `chat-messages.ts` (~L1074) maps gateway `row_id` / REST numeric `id` onto `ChatMessage.rowId` (it exists today for reactions). `SessionMessage`'s doc comment already warns that renderer ids are ephemeral and durable addressing must use `row_id`.
- **Gateway side:** resumed history entries already carry `_row_id` (`hermes_state._rows_to_conversation`, `include_row_ids=True`). Live in-memory appends do NOT — the gateway would need to stamp `_row_id` onto history entries at append/flush time (or resolve the target against the DB instead of the in-memory list).
- **Protocol:** `prompt.submit` accepts `truncate_before_row_id`; gateway resolves it against the session's rows, validates it's a user turn in THIS session, cross-checks the ordinal when both are supplied (refuse on mismatch), and refuses without touching data when unknown.
- **Keep the ordinal path for back-compat**; new clients send both.

Pitfalls the next implementation must cover (all hit by #82766):
- Renderer-synthetic ids never reach the gateway; tests must use production-shaped history (no hand-seeded `"id"` keys).
- Optimistic/live rows have no `rowId` until persisted — the client needs a fallback (ordinal) for rows not yet flushed.
- The desktop `isStaleTargetError` retry must NOT silently degrade a failed targeted rewind into an untruncated resend (zombie duplicate turns).

Credit: direction proposed in #82756 by @RichardGuan1, first attempt #82766 by @StanleyStetson, failure analysis in the #82950 review chain.

items.title: [Bug] Gateway clarify reply bypass misses on profile-namespaced session keys — follow-up messages queued instead of resolving pending clarify (Telegram)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

Follow-up to #78069 (child issue): a Telegram reproduction reported in that thread (comment by cxbitz, 2026-08-09) shows a **second, distinct failure mode** for the same user-facing symptom (pending `clarify()` never binds the user's answer; the turn hangs until the 3600 s clarify timeout).

In the original Discord report, the user's free text *did* reach the gateway runner (the `inbound message:` log line was present) and was silently rejected by the strict native-choice coercion. In the Telegram report, **none of the follow-up messages produced an `inbound message:` line at all** — meaning they never reached the runner's agent dispatch. They were queued by the adapter-level busy guard instead of being routed to the pending clarify resolver.

The likely failure point is the adapter-level clarify reply bypass in `gateway/platforms/base.py` (`handle_message`, active-session branch, ~line 6033): it checks `clarify_gateway.get_pending_for_session(session_key, include_choice_prompts=True)` using a session key built **without** the profile namespace (`build_session_key(..., profile=None)`), while the runner registers the pending clarify under `ctx.session_key` which **includes** the profile namespace (`profile=self._resolve_profile_for_key(source)`). For a named-profile multiplex these keys diverge, so the bypass lookup returns `None` and the user's answer is queued as an unrelated follow-up instead of resolving the pending clarify.

### Steps to Reproduce

Reported timeline (Telegram topic-threaded group, Hermes 0.19.1, from the #78069 thread):

1. Agent issues a native multi-choice `clarify()`; user resolves the **first** clarify via a button (13:16:53, `tool clarify completed`).
2. Agent continues the same turn and issues a **second** `clarify()` (13:17:23, API call #26).
3. User sends follow-up messages (photo batches flushed under `...:3:photo-burst`, text batches under `...:3`) between 13:18 and 13:38 — **no `inbound message:` log line and no `Gateway intercepted clarify text response` log line** for any of them.
4. Second clarify times out at 14:17:23 (3600.08 s); queued follow-ups drain at 14:17:33.

Not yet reliably reproduced locally; the mechanism (profile-namespace key divergence between adapter lookup and runner registration) is visible in the code and needs a named-profile multiplex environment to trigger.

### Expected Behavior

- Follow-up messages sent while a native choice `clarify()` is pending must reach the clarify resolver (bind to the pending call) or, at minimum, not be silently queued behind the very turn they should answer.
- If binding fails, the turn should fail visibly instead of hanging until the 3600 s timeout.
- Photo bursts while a clarify is pending should have a defined outcome (the current behavior silently drops them into the queue).

### Actual Behavior

Four follow-up messages during the pending second clarify were queued by the adapter busy guard and never reached the runner's clarify interception. The pending clarify remained unresolved until its 3600 s timeout, then the queued messages drained as a normal follow-up turn. No user-visible error or indication during the hang.

### Affected Component

- Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform

- Telegram

### Debug Report

Not available from the reporter yet — the original evidence is the gateway log timeline in the #78069 thread comment (2026-08-09). To confirm the root cause, we need the reporter's `config.yaml` multiplex/profile settings (`multiplex_profiles`, active profile name) and the session keys visible in their `gateway.log` for the failing session.

### Operating System

Linux (per original #78069 environment; Telegram reporter's OS not stated)

### Python Version

3.11.15 (original #78069 environment)

### Hermes Version

0.19.1 [1f8acb34] (2026-08-03) — original #78069 environment; Telegram reporter also 0.19.1

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Two hypotheses were evaluated in the #78069 thread:

1. **Stale oldest-entry selection** in `get_pending_for_session` (returns the oldest id in `_session_index[session_key]`; a button-resolved first clarify still indexed could shadow the live second clarify). **Refuted empirically**: `wait_for_response` synchronously removes its own entry from the index on return, and the 30 s gap between the first clarify completing and the second opening leaves no stale window. A two-clarify probe on current `main` confirms the lookup returns the live entry.
2. **Session-key divergence between adapter bypass and runner registration**: the adapter builds its lookup key without `profile` (`gateway/platforms/base.py` `handle_message`), the runner registers with the profile-namespaced key (`ctx.session_key`). Under named-profile multiplex these differ → bypass lookup misses → message queued. This is the leading hypothesis and needs the reporter's multiplex configuration to confirm.

Related: #78069 (parent issue), #75732 (runner-side prose-rejection deadlock fix — does NOT touch `gateway/platforms/base.py`), #71946 (native-choice clarify deadlock class), #72742 (Discord button-expiry variant).

items.title: [Bug]: Concurrent correlated plugin launches can execute twice

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

Two plugin callbacks can concurrently launch separate subagents with the same non-empty `correlation_id` under one parent session. Both children execute, but the lifecycle registry retains only the later child for that correlation key.

This can duplicate delegated work and its side effects while making one child unreachable through correlation-based lifecycle tracking.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Bind one parent session and create a `SubagentLifecycleService`.
2. Start two threads that call `launch()` with the same non-empty `correlation_id`.
3. Pause the first child construction after it passes duplicate detection, then start the second launch before registration completes.
4. Release construction and observe two valid handles and two child executions, while one correlation mapping remains.

### Expected Behavior

For one parent session and one non-empty correlation ID, at most one launch succeeds. A concurrent duplicate should receive `SubagentLifecycleError`.

### Actual Behavior

Both launches can pass duplicate detection, construct and execute distinct children, and overwrite the same correlation mapping.

### Impact

- Delegated work and plugin-triggered side effects can run twice.
- One launched child is no longer represented by the correlation map, so correlation-based lifecycle tracking becomes inconsistent.
- The race affects concurrent launches sharing both parent session and non-empty correlation ID. Empty IDs and equal IDs under distinct parents are not affected by the uniqueness contract.

### Affected Component

- Plugin subagent lifecycle service
- `agent/subagent_lifecycle.py`

### Debug / Diagnostics

N/A - reproduced locally with synchronized child construction; accompanying PR will link here.

### Operating System

Windows 10

### Runtime Version

Reproduced on `hermes/main` at `893792c9934447e80f40519437e7c64b4479fc3a`.

### Root Cause Analysis

**Trigger:** `agent/subagent_lifecycle.py` / `SubagentLifecycleService.launch()` when concurrent calls use the same parent-scoped non-empty correlation ID.

**Causal chain:**
1. The first launch checks the correlation map under the registry lock, sees no entry, and releases the lock before child construction.
2. A second launch checks during that construction window and also sees no entry, so both build and submit children.
3. Each launch later writes its child ID to the same correlation key; both children execute, but the later write hides the earlier child from correlation tracking.

**Why it is wrong:** Duplicate detection and correlation registration are separate critical sections with slow child construction between them, so the uniqueness check is not atomic with claiming the key.

**Working sibling / contrast:** Sequential duplicate launches are rejected because the first launch has registered its correlation before the second checks. Equal correlation values under distinct parents correctly use distinct keys.

**Ruled out:** Empty correlation IDs are intentionally not deduplicated and do not explain the race. The failure was reproduced with a non-empty ID and one shared parent.

**Verified on tip:** The synchronized race reproduced two handles and two executions on the stated default-branch tip.

### Proposed Fix

Reserve each non-empty parent-scoped correlation key before child construction without holding the registry lock during slow setup. Roll back only the caller's reservation and record if construction, identity assignment, or executor submission fails, so a later retry can succeed.

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Feature]: client-only ("thin client") install mode for Hermes Desktop — UI without the local agent runtime

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

### Summary

Allow Hermes Desktop to be installed as a **UI-only client** that connects to a Hermes
Agent running on another machine, without bootstrapping the agent runtime locally
(Python, portable Git, ripgrep, venv, `HERMES_HOME` layout). Ideally the remote gateway
endpoint and its credentials can be supplied **at install time**, so the app is usable on
first launch with no local install step at all.

### Motivation / use case

I run a single Hermes Agent instance on a homelab server (Linux, reachable over
Tailscale) and I want to talk to it from several client machines: a Windows desktop, a
laptop, and occasionally a low-spec machine. On every one of those clients I only need
the chat UI — the agent, its tools, its filesystem access, and its credentials all live
on the server, which is exactly the boundary I want.

Today the Desktop app already supports connecting to a remote gateway, but the
distribution model assumes a local runtime:

- The prebuilt installer and the first-launch bootstrap install the full agent runtime
  into `HERMES_HOME`, which is unnecessary weight and unnecessary attack surface on a
  pure client machine.
- `apps/desktop/README.md` describes remote mode as "a remote operating mode, not a
  separate client-only application", and the backend resolution ladder ends at "the
  first-launch bootstrap installer".
- On locked-down or corporate Windows machines, installing Python + Git + a venv is
  often not viable, while installing a signed Electron app is.
- Provisioning several clients means repeating the local-install flow on each of them
  even though none of them will ever execute agent work.


### Proposed Solution


1. **A client-only installer variant / install flag.** For example
   `HermesDesktop-Setup-<version>-client.exe`, or an existing installer with a
   "Remote gateway only" option in the setup wizard (equivalent flags for the macOS DMG
   and the Linux AppImage/deb/rpm). This variant skips the runtime bootstrap entirely
   and never creates a managed install under `HERMES_HOME`.
2. **Connection details at install time.** The installer (or an unattended/silent
   install parameter set) accepts the gateway URL, transport, and auth token, e.g.: HermesDesktop-Setup.exe /S /GATEWAY_URL=wss://hermes.my-tailnet.ts.net:8787 /GATEWAY_TOKEN=...
  plus environment-variable and config-file equivalents, so the app opens straight into
   chat against the configured host. This also makes the client deployable via MDM/Intune,
   Group Policy, or a config-management tool across a fleet.
3. **Graceful degradation of local-only features.** Anything that depends on a local
   runtime (local file browser rooted on the client, local terminal, managed updates of
   the agent) should be hidden or clearly marked as server-side, since in remote mode the
   gateway host is already the execution boundary.
4. **No local-install prompts in this mode.** If the connection fails, the app should
   offer to fix or change the connection rather than fall back to "install Hermes locally".

### Alternatives considered

- Using the browser dashboard against the remote gateway: works, but loses the native
  window, voice, and OS integration, and is awkward to pin/launch like a normal app.
- Installing the full agent on every client and leaving it unused: wasteful, and it
  duplicates credentials and config on machines that should hold neither.
- Building `apps/desktop` from source with `HERMES_DESKTOP_HERMES_ROOT` pointing nowhere:
  not a supported or reproducible path for non-developer clients.


- Platforms: primarily Windows, but the same need applies to macOS and Linux.
- Related: the Desktop app already implements the remote-capability path for remote and
  cloud connections, so this request is mainly about **packaging and first-run/install
  flow**, not about new transport work.
- Happy to help test on Windows + a Linux gateway reachable over Tailscale.


### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Feature Type

New tool

### Scope

None

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

```shell

```

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop pane resize sash blocks scrollbars and can feel one-directional
items.body:
### Bug description

Hermes Desktop pane resize sashes conflict with scrollbars on the same boundary. The resize hit target takes pointer priority, making the scrollbar thumb difficult or impossible to drag across multiple layouts, including Files and Terminal.

A related usability issue occurs when Files/Review reaches its fixed `20rem` maximum: dragging toward a wider pane produces no movement while the opposite direction works. At non-default desktop zoom this cap is reached at a visually smaller physical width, so the sash appears broken.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, open a layout with Workspace + Files and Terminal.
2. Populate Files until its vertical scrollbar is visible.
3. Drag the scrollbar where it shares the pane boundary with the resize sash.
4. Resize Files to its maximum, then drag the sash both ways.

### Actual behavior

- The centered resize target intercepts the adjacent scrollbar.
- At maximum width the sash only moves in the shrinking direction, without constrained-state feedback.

### Expected behavior

- Scrollbar thumbs remain fully draggable on resizable boundaries.
- Resize constraints remain usable at common zoom/window sizes or clearly indicate the limit.

### Technical notes

- `apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/tree/renderer/tree-split.tsx`: `Sash` centers a 9px, z-20 hit target over the boundary. This overlaps the app-wide 4px scrollbar.
- A local proof-of-concept placing a 5px target entirely on the incoming pane side restored the previous pane right/bottom scrollbar.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/layout.ts`: `FILE_BROWSER_MAX_WIDTH = '20rem'` causes the one-directional behavior at the cap.

### Environment

- Windows 11 build 26200
- Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 / Electron 40.10.2
- Hermes Agent 0.20.0
- Remote backend over SSH

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — "+" new session on a non-Git explicit project fails: "无法切换到 <project> / Branch name is required."

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Bug Description

In Hermes Desktop, clicking the **"+" (new session)** button on a project lane whose root directory is **NOT a Git repository** (an explicit project pointing at a plain folder, no `.git`) fails with `无法切换到 <project>` / "Branch name is required." — the new session is **never created**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an explicit project whose primary path is a plain folder with **no `.git`** (e.g. a documents directory added to the Projects sidebar).
2. In the sidebar Projects section, hover the project lane and click the **"+"** (new session) button.
3. Observe the error toast: `无法切换到 <project>` with detail `Branch name is required.` — no session is opened.

## Expected Behavior

A new session should be created with its cwd seeded to the project path. The git branch-switch step only makes sense for lanes that actually correspond to a Git repository; for non-repo projects it should be skipped entirely.

## Actual Behavior

The session is never created. The error toast is shown and the flow aborts.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 (native)
- Hermes Desktop: 0.17.0
- Local checkout: `main` @ `cd6585abf` (2026-08-02)

## Root Cause Analysis

`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-group.tsx`, `handleNewSession` (~lines 99–107):

```tsx
// Main-checkout lanes are branch-labeled views over the same repo root path.
// Clicking "+" on `main` should open on `main`, not whatever branch the root
// currently sits on (`test0`, etc.), so explicitly switch first.
if (group.isMain && group.path && group.label) {
  try {
    await switchBranchInRepo(group.path, group.label)
  } catch (err) {
    notifyError(err, t.statusStack.coding.switchFailed(group.label))
    return   // <-- aborts; onNewSession never runs
  }
}
onNewSession(group.path)
```

Every project (repo or not) gets a **main-checkout lane** with `isMain: true` (see `workspace-groups.ts` — main lanes are folded into a home lane, and with no probe/home branch they are kept as-is). So for a non-repo explicit project this branch fires and calls `switchBranchInRepo(path, label)` on a directory without `.git`. The git ops then fail, and `apps/desktop/electron/git-worktree-ops.ts` throws `Branch name is required.` (line 220 in `addExistingBranchWorktree`; also line 357), which is surfaced via `notifyError(err, switchFailed(label))`; the `return` skips `onNewSession(group.path)`.

Verified locally: `projects.db` lists the affected project as explicit (`projects.primary_path` = plain folder), while `discovered_repos` only contains actual `.git` roots — the folder itself is not a repo, yet its lane goes through the repo-switch code path.

## Trigger Condition (why this broke "suddenly")

The lane label is the switch: `handleNewSession` only runs `switchBranchInRepo` when `group.isMain && group.path && group.label` — a **null/empty label skips the git step entirely and creates the session directly**. For a non-repo project the backend only assigns a label (the folder basename — `_place_by_heuristic` in `tui_gateway/project_tree.py`) after its first probe; until then the lane label is null ("Null until the first probe" — `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts`).

Reporter's timeline: the same "+" button worked for days on the same non-repo project, and started failing right after an unrelated backend restart / repo re-scan (triggered by config changes while working on another project). The restart flipped the lane from *unprobed* (label=null → git step skipped → session created fine) to *probed* (label="国创大赛" → git step runs on a non-repo path → `Branch name is required.` → aborted). So this is a **latent bug activated by the first probe of any non-repo project**, not a regression in the click path itself.

## Suggested Fix

1. In `handleNewSession`, skip the branch-switch when the path is not a Git repository — probe `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` (or make `switchBranchInRepo` a no-op for non-repo roots) — so `onNewSession(group.path)` always runs for non-repo projects.
2. Alternatively, gate the main-lane `isMain` marker (or the "+" switch behavior) on actual repo detection so non-repo projects never take the branch-switch path.

items.title: [Bug]: Session can be poisoned into a permanent non-retryable 400 — whitespace-only user block built at request time

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Bug Description

A session can reach a state where **every** subsequent turn fails with a non-retryable `400`, permanently. It does not self-heal, retries cannot help, and the end user has no way to clear it.

One agent could not answer a single message for ~4 hours. Seven sibling agents on the same host — same image, same upstream, same model — were unaffected throughout.

The block that causes the `400` is **built at request time and does not exist in `state.db`**. That is the part worth reading twice: inspecting stored history finds nothing wrong.

### Steps to Reproduce

Not reproduced from a clean start — found in the wild, so I can only describe the observable state rather than a recipe. Everything below is verifiable on an affected session:

1. A gateway session reaches a state where its stored `system_prompt` is `NULL` (sibling sessions on the same host hold 15–19 KB).
2. Every turn from then on logs `Stored system prompt for session <id> is null; rebuilding from scratch this turn.`
3. Every request built for that session contains, at `messages[0]`, a role `user` message whose `content` is a list with one `{"type": "text"}` block holding **a single whitespace character**.
4. The provider rejects it, non-retryably, every time.
5. Inspecting `messages` for that session shows ordinary short user messages — nothing empty, nothing whitespace-only.

### Expected Behavior

A whitespace-only text block should never be sent — the API rejects it unconditionally, so emitting one is never correct. It should be dropped when the request is assembled, and a message left with no blocks dropped with it.

Separately, a session whose stored `system_prompt` is `NULL` should be repaired or ended, not merely logged about on every turn.

### Actual Behavior

```
ERROR agent.conversation_loop: Non-retryable client error: Error code: 400 -
  {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'invalid_request_error',
   'message': 'messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text'}}
ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 400 - ...
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=BadRequestError
  provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-5 summary=HT...
❌ Non-retryable error (HTTP 400): HTTP 400: messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text
❌ Non-retryable client error (HTTP 400). Aborting.
```

28 identical occurrences over ~4 hours, interleaved with:

```
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: Stored system prompt for session <id> is null;
  rebuilding from scratch this turn. Prefix cache will miss until the rebuild persists.
  Investigate the previous turn's update.
```

The end user only sees:

> The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat; check gateway logs for diagnostics.

which is indistinguishable from the provider being down.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Debug Report

```
Not attached — deliberately.

`hermes debug share` uploads config and recent logs to a public paste service. These are
production agents serving real end users, so the gateway logs and the request dump both
contain third-party conversation content that I cannot publish.

I do have the full request dump that demonstrates this, showing the whitespace-only block
at messages[0] alongside the stored history that does not contain it. Happy to share it
privately with a maintainer — please say where to send it.

Everything needed to locate the bug is in Root Cause Analysis below.
```

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), in Docker

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30) · upstream 470cf66b · install method: docker

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```
Two facts that rule out the obvious explanations:

1. NOT the model or upstream. The same model answered normally on all seven sibling
   agents throughout. Verified with a direct request to the same endpoint using the same
   credential — 200, normal completion.

2. NOT corrupted stored history. The `messages` rows for the failing session are ordinary
   short user messages. No empty content, no whitespace-only content, nothing malformed.
   The offending block exists only in the outbound request.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The request builder emits a content block that has no counterpart in stored state.

From `sessions/request_dump_<session>_<timestamp>.json` on a failing turn:

- 3 messages in the request body
- `messages[0]`: role `user`, `content` = a list with one `{"type": "text"}` block whose text is a single whitespace character

No row in that session's `messages` table holds that value.

Occurring in the same session, repeatedly, is `Stored system prompt for session <id> is null` — where sibling sessions hold 15–19 KB. Hermes' own warning says *"Investigate the previous turn's update"*, which looks like the right instinct: some earlier turn appears to leave the session's cached state in a bad shape, and the builder then regenerates an invalid block on every subsequent request.

That is what makes it permanent rather than intermittent — a retry replays the same poisoned state, so retrying can never succeed. The `(attempt 1/3)` in the logs is doing nothing but spending the user's time.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Three, independent, roughly in order of cost:

1. **Drop whitespace-only text blocks when assembling the request.** A block whose text `.strip()`s to empty should be dropped; a message left with no blocks dropped with it. This alone turns a permanent outage into a no-op, regardless of how the bad state arises.

2. **Treat a null stored `system_prompt` as state to repair rather than to log.** The warning already concludes something went wrong on a previous turn — rebuilding and persisting it, or ending the session, would clear the condition instead of narrating it every turn.

3. **Bound the blast radius.** A non-retryable 4xx that recurs for the same session N times running is a session-level fault, not a provider fault. Ending or auto-resetting the session at that point costs one turn instead of every future one.

**Workaround for anyone else hitting this:** remove the session's entry from `sessions/sessions.json` (the `session_key` → `session_id` map). The next inbound message starts a fresh session; `state.db` is untouched, so message history survives and stays searchable. Back the file up first — this is what I did to recover the affected agent.

items.title: [Feature]: Make gateway maintenance notices configurable, and tell users when the gateway is back

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

When the gateway restarts, every active chat receives:

> ⚠️ Gateway shutting down — Your current task will be interrupted.

That is written for an operator, and it is delivered to end users. Someone chatting with an assistant on Telegram has no model for the word "gateway", and the ⚠️ frames routine maintenance as a fault.

On a managed deployment this is not an occasional event. Any persona change, model change or toolset change restarts the gateway, so end users see this several times a day — none of them incidents. Today a customer received it three times in an afternoon while we rolled out a model change, and it read to them as the product breaking.

Two related gaps make it worse:

**There is no notice when the gateway comes back.** `_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown` announces the departure and nothing announces the return, so the warning is the last message in the thread. The user finds out it is over by trying — which, if they have already given up, means they do not. The gateway is the only component that knows when its adapters have actually reconnected, so it is the only thing that can say this accurately.

**The wording is not configurable.** No env var or config key reaches it. An operator who wants softer wording has to patch `gateway/run.py`, which is baked into the published image — so the patch is lost on every `docker pull`.

### Proposed Solution

Two env vars, defaulting to the current behaviour so nothing changes for existing users:

- `GATEWAY_MAINTENANCE_MESSAGE` — replaces the shutdown/restart notice
- `GATEWAY_RESUMED_MESSAGE` — sent to the same chats once adapters have reconnected; unset means send nothing, preserving today's behaviour

In `gateway/run.py`, `_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown` currently builds:

```python
action = "restarting" if self._restart_requested else "shutting down"
hint = (
    "Your current task will be interrupted. "
    "Send any message after restart and I'll try to resume where you left off."
    if self._restart_requested
    else "Your current task will be interrupted."
)
msg = f"⚠️ Gateway {action} — {hint}"
```

Reading an override at that point is a small change. The resume notice needs a counterpart on the startup path, after adapters report connected.

Softer defaults would also help on their own, independent of configurability — the user does not need to know the word "gateway", only that their assistant is briefly away, and then that it is back.

### Alternatives Considered

**Patching `run.py` in the image.** Works, but `/opt/hermes` is baked into `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` rather than mounted, so it is silently reverted by any image pull — the kind of drift that is invisible until a customer sees the old wording again.

**Sending the resume notice from our own control plane.** We have done this as a stopgap: our daemon restarts a tenant's gateway and then sends a message. It works, but it is guessing — the control plane knows it asked for a restart, not that the adapters have reconnected and the agent can actually answer. Only the gateway knows that.

**Suppressing the notice entirely.** Rejected. Telling someone their assistant is briefly away is genuinely useful; the problem is the wording and the missing other half, not the notification.

### Feature Type

Configuration option, Gateway / messaging improvement

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

### Debug Report (optional)

```
Not attached. These are production agents serving real end users, so the gateway logs
contain third-party conversation content that I cannot publish to a paste service.

Nothing here depends on logs — the behaviour is visible in gateway/run.py,
_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown, in the current release.
```

Environment, for completeness: Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30) · upstream 470cf66b, docker install, Debian 13, Python 3.13.5, Telegram and WhatsApp adapters.

items.title: Sidebar unread dot never clears when the session's tab is already open

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
# Sidebar unread dot never clears when the session's tab is already open

## Summary

The sidebar unread (emerald) dot stays lit after the user opens/views the session, as long as that session's **tab was already open** (session tile) when the turn finished. The dot only clears when the session is re-loaded from scratch (tab closed first) or the app restarts. This is a desktop app bug in `apps/desktop`.

## Repro steps

1. Open session A in a **tab** (session tile / ⌘-click), while the main session is B (any other session).
2. In session A, run a turn to completion (e.g. ask a question and wait for the answer).
3. When A's turn finishes, A's sidebar row shows the unread emerald dot — even though its tab is open right next to you and you watched it finish.
4. Click A's sidebar row to "read" it → the tab is fronted, but the **dot stays**.
5. Close A's tab, click A again in the sidebar → the dot disappears.
6. Alternative: restart the app → the dot disappears (state is in-memory only).

## Expected behavior

- A session whose tab is already open (or which is the selected session) should not be marked unread when its turn finishes — the user is already looking at it.
- Opening/clicking a session should clear its unread marker in **all** code paths, including "jump to already-open tab".

## Root cause

Two compounding issues in `apps/desktop`:

### 1. Marking ignores open tabs — `src/store/session-states.ts`, `handleTransition` (~lines 179–191)

```ts
} else if (!next.busy && wasWorking) {
  markSettled(storedId)

  if (storedId !== $selectedStoredSessionId.get()) {
    const cur = $unreadFinishedSessionIds.get()

    if (!cur.includes(storedId)) {
      $unreadFinishedSessionIds.set([...cur, storedId])
    }
  }
}
```

Unread is marked whenever the finished session is not the **selected** session. It never checks whether that session is already open in a session tile (`$sessionTiles`), so a tab you are literally watching gets flagged unread.

### 2. Clearing is skipped on the "already open" path — `src/app/open-session.ts` + `src/store/session-states.ts` `focusOpenSession`

Sidebar clicks go through `openSession()`. Inside:

- `focusOpenSession(storedSessionId)` returns `'tile'` when the session already has an open tab, or `'main'` when it is the selected session — and `openSession` **returns immediately** in both cases (no navigation, no re-selection).
- The **only** place unread is cleared is `setSelectedStoredSessionId` in `src/store/session.ts` (~lines 612–620):

```ts
export const setSelectedStoredSessionId = (next: Updater<string | null>) => {
  updateAtom($selectedStoredSessionId, next)
  // Opening a session clears its unread state — the user is now looking at it.
  const id = $selectedStoredSessionId.get()

  if (id && $unreadFinishedSessionIds.get().includes(id)) {
    $unreadFinishedSessionIds.set($unreadFinishedSessionIds.get().filter(x => x !== id))
  }
}
```

So "jump to already-open tab" never reaches the clearing code. Only the fallback path (session not on screen → navigate → select) clears it. Restart clears it because `$unreadFinishedSessionIds` is a plain in-memory atom.

### 3. (Minor) clearing is not lineage-aware

`setSelectedStoredSessionId` clears by exact id match, while marking/display propagate through `lineageAliases` (`src/store/session.ts`, `src/app/chat/session-status-dot.tsx`). After a compression rotates a session's stored id, the sidebar row holds the new tip id but the unread list holds the old one — exact `includes(id)` misses and the dot survives even on the "reload" path.

## Suggested fix

1. **Marking**: in `handleTransition`, skip the unread marker when `storedId` is present in `$sessionTiles` (any open tab) or equals `$selectedStoredSessionId`.
2. **Clearing**: clear the unread marker at the top of `openSession()` (all branches), using `idsShareLineage` instead of exact match, so jump-to-tab, jump-to-main, and post-compression clicks all clear it.

## Environment

- Windows 10 (21H2), Hermes desktop app (locally built from source)
- Reproduced on current `apps/desktop` at commit of 2026-08-10

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop new-session cwd polluted by localStorage — terminal.cwd config silently bypassed

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

On the Desktop app (local backend), setting `terminal.cwd` in `config.yaml` has no effect on new sessions. The configured path is silently bypassed because `$currentCwd` (persisted in localStorage) is non-empty, and the new-session cwd resolution prioritizes it over `resolveNewSessionCwd()` → `workspaceCwdForNewSession()` (which reads the config).

This is a **different code path** from the CLI override tracked in #42961 (`cli.py:653` unconditional `os.getcwd()` for local backend). The Desktop app routes through the gateway, not the CLI entry point — `cli.py:653` is never reached. The root cause here is in the renderer's localStorage-backed `$currentCwd` atom.

## Root Cause

### The pollution chain

1. **Electron launches** → process cwd = `C:\Users\<user>` (or wherever the app was launched)
2. **Gateway subprocess inherits** this cwd
3. An early session's cwd falls back to `os.getcwd()` = `C:\Users\<user>` (via `_safe_getcwd()` in `terminal_tool.py:1356`)
4. **Desktop switches to that session** → `session-view.tsx:83`: `$cwd: primaryField(state => state.cwd, $currentCwd)` → the session's cwd (or `$currentCwd` fallback) is written to `$currentCwd` via `setCurrentCwd()`
5. `setCurrentCwd()` (`session.ts:624-626`) persists to localStorage: `persistString(workspaceCwdKey(), ...)`
6. **Every new chat** → `index.ts:363-368`:
   ```typescript
   const cwd =
     workspaceTarget === null
       ? ''
       : typeof workspaceTarget === 'string'
         ? workspaceTarget.trim()
         : $currentCwd.get().trim() || resolveNewSessionCwd()
   ```
   `$currentCwd.get()` is non-empty (the polluted value from localStorage), so `resolveNewSessionCwd()` is **never called** — the `||` short-circuits.
7. `desktopSessionCreateParams(cwd)` (`index.ts:178`): `...(cwd && { cwd })` — non-empty cwd is sent to gateway as an explicit override.
8. Gateway receives `cwd` in `session.create` → stores it in `sessions.cwd` in state.db → step 4 repeats.

### Why `terminal.cwd` is never read

`workspaceCwdForNewSession()` (`session.ts:639-651`) is the function that reads `getConfiguredDefaultProjectDir()` (which bridges from `terminal.cwd`). It's the last fallback in `resolveNewSessionCwd()` (`projects.ts:216-243`). But `$currentCwd.get().trim()` is non-empty, so the `||` in `index.ts:368` never reaches `resolveNewSessionCwd()`.

The config value is only read when `$currentCwd` is empty — but the pollution chain ensures it's never empty after the first session.

### Design intent vs actual behavior

`workspaceCwdForNewSession()` comment (`session.ts:644-650`):
> A bare new chat starts DETACHED — no inherited cwd … Only an explicit default-project-dir setting pre-attaches.

This intent is correct: a bare new chat should either be detached (empty cwd) or use the configured `terminal.cwd`. But the `||` priority in `index.ts:368` defeats it — `$currentCwd`'s localStorage-persisted dirty value wins over the config.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `hermes config set terminal.cwd E:\hermes-workspace\default`
2. Launch Hermes Desktop (from `C:\Users\<user>`, the default launch dir)
3. Open a session, run `pwd` → returns `C:\Users\<user>` (process launch dir, not config)
4. Switch to a different session or create a new chat
5. Run `pwd` → still `C:\Users\<user>`
6. Check localStorage: `hermes.desktop.workspace-cwd` = `"C:\Users\<user>"`
7. `hermes config get terminal.cwd` → `E:\hermes-workspace\default` (config is correct, just not read)

## Expected Behavior

If `terminal.cwd` is explicitly set to a non-placeholder value, new Desktop sessions should use it — not a localStorage-persisted dirty value inherited from the process launch directory.

## Proposed Fix

Two complementary changes:

### 1. Desktop: don't let dirty `$currentCwd` override config

In `index.ts:368`, the priority should be reversed for bare new chats (no explicit workspace target):

```typescript
// Before:
$currentCwd.get().trim() || resolveNewSessionCwd()

// After:
resolveNewSessionCwd() || $currentCwd.get().trim()
```

Or better: when `workspaceTarget` is `undefined` (bare new chat, no explicit pick), call `resolveNewSessionCwd()` directly — it already handles the "inherit focused session's workspace" case via `focusedSessionWorkspaceCwd()` and falls through to `workspaceCwdForNewSession()` (config) when there's nothing to inherit.

### 2. Desktop: sanitize `$currentCwd` on startup

`ensureDefaultWorkspaceCwd()` (`session.ts:190-225`) runs on startup and calls `sanitizeWorkspaceCwd()`. But it only seeds `$currentCwd` when `$activeSessionId` is empty (`seedLiveCwd` guard at line 201). If a session was active on last exit, the dirty localStorage value is kept without validation.

A startup check should verify that the remembered `$currentCwd` is either:
- A valid workspace directory that still exists, OR
- Empty (detached)

If it's a stale process-launch-dir path (e.g. `C:\Users\<user>` on Windows, `/` on Linux), clear it.

### Workaround

Clear localStorage in Desktop DevTools:
```javascript
localStorage.removeItem('hermes.desktop.workspace-cwd')
```
Then reload. New sessions will use `terminal.cwd` until the pollution recurs.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Hermes Desktop (local backend)
- `terminal.cwd` set to `E:\hermes-workspace\default` in `config.yaml`
- Gateway PID confirmed running; `TERMINAL_CWD` env var correctly set to config value
- localStorage `hermes.desktop.workspace-cwd` contained `C:\Users\jhye` (process launch dir)

## Related Issues

- #42961 — `terminal.cwd` ignored for local backend (CLI override at `cli.py:653`). Same symptom, different code path. The CLI fix does not address the Desktop renderer's localStorage pollution.
- #14044 — Earlier report of `terminal.cwd` not respected by terminal tool.
- #19214 — `terminal.cwd` foot-gun discussion (CLI/TUI launch-dir semantics).

items.title: react_to_message leaks its dedicated SessionDB on every call

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

`tools/react_to_message_tool.py::react_to_message_tool()` opens a dedicated `SessionDB` for every desktop reaction, but never closes it. Successful reactions and every error return after `_open_session_db()` therefore retain the SQLite handle and its file descriptors for the lifetime of a long-running gateway.

This is the same ownership bug class as #83027, but a separate call site and surface. I searched open/closed issues and PRs for `react_to_message`, `SessionDB`, fd leaks, and handle cleanup and found no existing fix.

## Reproduction

On current `main` (`a1da384c6`), replace `_open_session_db()` with a fake dedicated handle that records `close()` calls, then exercise:

1. a successful reaction;
2. no matching user message;
3. a failed `set_message_reaction()` call.

All three paths return without calling `close()`. A close failure also currently cannot be observed because close is never attempted.

The production path has the same shape:

```python
db = _open_session_db()  # returns a fresh SessionDB()
if db is None:
    return ...

# multiple success/error returns; no db.close()
```

## Expected behavior

The tool owns the handle returned by `_open_session_db()` and must close it exactly once on every return path after a successful open. Cleanup failures should be logged at debug level without replacing the tool result.

## Actual behavior

Each reachable reaction call leaves its dedicated `SessionDB` open. In a long-lived desktop gateway, repeated reactions accumulate SQLite descriptors and contribute to eventual `EMFILE` failures in unrelated features.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent current `main`: `a1da384c6`
- macOS
- Python 3.11.15

## Root cause

The tool was introduced with a lazy `_open_session_db()` helper but no ownership cleanup. Unlike shared caller-owned handles, this handle has no other owner and must be closed by the tool call that created it.

## Proposed fix

Wrap the post-open body in `try/finally`, close the dedicated DB in the `finally`, and add behavior-level regression tests covering success, early error, write failure, and cleanup failure.

I have a focused fix with regression tests ready to submit.

items.title: [Bug]: Masked test failures can be recorded as passing verification

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

After a workspace edit, a failed canonical verification command can be recorded as passed when shell control flow masks its exit status. For example, `pytest || true` and `pytest | tee log.txt` both return shell exit code 0 even when pytest fails, so Hermes persists fresh passing verification evidence and suppresses its verify-on-stop reminder.

This creates a false verification signal: an edited workspace can appear verified even though the actual test process failed.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a project whose detected canonical verification command is `pytest`.
2. Mark the workspace edited through the normal Hermes file-edit path.
3. Run a deliberately failing test as `pytest || true` or `pytest | tee log.txt` in a shell without `pipefail`.
4. Inspect the verification ledger and invoke the verify-on-stop guard.

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should record passing or failing verification evidence only when the terminal exit status can be safely attributed to the matched verifier. Ambiguous compound commands and pipelines should not upgrade the workspace to verified.

### Actual Behavior

The overall shell command exits 0, Hermes records canonical command `pytest` with status `passed`, and the verify-on-stop guard suppresses its continuation even though pytest failed.

### Impact

- Failed tests can be represented as fresh passing evidence after code edits.
- The agent can stop without the verification reminder that should remain active for an unverified workspace.
- The exact frequency and broader blast radius were not measured.

### Affected Component

- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
- Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Debug Report

N/A - reproduced locally against the current main branch; an accompanying PR will link here.

### Operating System

Windows 10

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

main at `92dd230c8c3bdbc900f29a3d6cedca1ce1450b50`

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```text
Both masked commands displayed a deliberate pytest failure but returned exit code 0. Before the fix, the verification ledger stored canonical command pytest as passed and the stop guard was suppressed.
```

### Root Cause Analysis

**Trigger:** `agent/verification_evidence.py` in shell segment parsing, canonical matching, and `classify_verification_command()`.

**Causal chain:**
1. A canonical verifier runs inside shell control flow such as `pytest || true` or `pytest | tee log.txt`.
2. Shell parsing drops the operators connecting command segments, while canonical matching accepts the verifier found in any segment.
3. Classification assigns pass or fail from only the compound command's final exit code, so a successful fallback or pipeline consumer turns the failed verifier into passing evidence.
4. The verification stop guard sees current status `passed` and suppresses its reminder after an edit.

**Why it is wrong:** The compound shell status does not necessarily represent the matched verifier's status. Evidence is upgraded without a safe attribution relationship.

**Working sibling / contrast:** A simple `pytest` command, a successful `&&` chain, or a final verifier after `;` has an attributable status. Canonical and ad-hoc verification paths share the ambiguous attribution problem and should use the same conservative gate.

**Ruled out:** The problem is not stale baseline behavior or pytest output parsing. It reproduced on the current main tip and follows directly from shell exit semantics even when pytest's failure is visible in output.

**Verified on tip:** Reproduced in a real Hermes environment on `92dd230c8c3bdbc900f29a3d6cedca1ce1450b50` with both `pytest || true` and `pytest | tee log.txt`.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Preserve top-level shell control operators during tokenization and accept evidence only when the overall exit status can be safely attributed to the matched canonical or ad-hoc verifier. Keep simple commands, quoted operator arguments, successful `&&` chains, and final verifier segments working, with behavior tests covering ledger state.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Desktop in-app update: PowerShell window freezes ('Not Responding'); force-close then desktop app crashes on next launch
items.body:
## Summary

The desktop app's in-app update (which auto-launches a PowerShell window) frequently **freezes / becomes unresponsive** during the update. The window shows "Not Responding" and the user has to force-close it, after which the desktop app often **crashes on next launch** or cannot be opened.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes Desktop app (win-unpacked), installed at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent` (git checkout, main branch)
- Update triggered from the desktop app UI (auto-opens PowerShell)

## Repro steps

1. In the desktop app, click the in-app update button (it auto-launches a PowerShell window).
2. The PowerShell window appears and soon becomes **unresponsive** ("Not Responding" in the title bar) for a long time.
3. User force-closes the PowerShell window (kills the update).
4. Re-opening the desktop app: it **crashes / fails to open**. Repeated attempts pile up multiple `Hermes.exe` instances (we observed 5+), each spawning its own backend (`hermes serve` on different ports), and the app keeps crashing.

## What the logs show

- `update.log` actually shows the update **completes** ("✓ Update complete!"), but the command **hangs at the final step "Restarting Windows gateway profile(s): default"** — this step waits 1–2 min and looks like a freeze.
- `errors.log` shows the gateway then exits **UNCLEANLY** (SIGKILL / no exit path ran) after the user force-closes the window.
- After that, launching the desktop app is unstable (crashes; multiple instances; backend port conflicts).

## Expected behavior

- The update window should not appear frozen during the long build steps (git fetch / npm ci / electron packaging take 5–15 min with no console output — Windows marks the window "Not Responding" although it is still working). Progress output or a dedicated progress UI would help.
- If the update is interrupted (window force-closed), the desktop app should still start cleanly afterwards (clean up residual gateway/venv state), instead of crashing on next launch.

## Notes / suggestions

- The "restart gateway" step at the end of `hermes update` hangs the console; consider making it non-blocking or printing a clear "waiting for gateway restart" message.
- On Windows, the console window being marked "Not Responding" during long silent operations is a known UX trap — consider launching the update in a separate visible window with streaming output, or suppressing the "Not Responding" state.
- After an interrupted update, the app should detect residual gateway/instance state and clean it up on next launch.

Thanks!

items.title: Desktop/WebSocket reconnect must recover persisted turns without duplicates

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Problem

Desktop and attached TUI clients can remain bound to a silently dead or replaced
WebSocket while an accepted turn continues and persists on the backend. The
renderer can then miss `message.complete` and keep showing a stale running state
until the user sends another message or manually changes sessions.

This is a delivery/recovery failure, not necessarily an agent or persistence
failure.

## Current-main reproduction

Reproduced on official `main` at
`3139a30e52b560ea96c69b003cf9eb49652fa11f` with focused behavior tests:

- A client receives `gateway.ready`, the connection is silently blackholed, and
  no native `close` event fires. The shared browser client remains `open`
  indefinitely because it has no negotiated application heartbeat.
- A real replacement socket opens, but React observes only `open` before and
  after the replacement. The selected route is not activated because recovery
  depends on observing the intermediate `closed -> open` state.

Focused baseline: 2 failing recovery assertions, 14 existing assertions passing.

## Required recovery contract

- Advertise heartbeat capability from `gateway.ready`; only capable backends
  enable the client heartbeat so older runtimes remain compatible.
- Detect a silent/half-open socket within 60 seconds, invalidate only that socket
  generation, reject its pending calls, ignore its late frames, and let the
  bounded reconnect owner redial.
- Advance a per-profile connection epoch on each actual socket open and
  reactivate the routed session whenever that epoch advances.
- Reconcile messages, runtime identity, inflight state, and `running` from
  authoritative backend state after reconnect.
- Never automatically replay an ambiguously delivered `prompt.submit`.
  Reconnect and inspect the stored session; if acceptance cannot be proven,
  restore the composer and show a retryable delivery-not-confirmed error.
- Clear stale running state only when a registered prompt worker exists and is
  confirmed dead. Do not disturb a live or not-yet-registered worker.
- Rebind a session stream from the same, closed, detached, or heartbeat-expired
  transport, while returning a conflict if another recently live client owns it.
- Preserve intentional shutdown and prevent reconnect storms.

## Acceptance matrix

- Disconnect after prompt acceptance but before `message.complete`: the persisted
  final appears automatically after reconnect, the session returns idle, and
  there is exactly one user message, one assistant response, and one terminal
  completion.
- Silent blackhole without native close: heartbeat expiry causes bounded
  reconnect and the same authoritative recovery.
- Ambiguous accepted submit is never resubmitted.
- Batched reconnect still activates the selected route exactly once.
- Dead worker state is repaired; live and not-yet-registered workers remain live.
- A second healthy client retains stream ownership.
- Intentional shutdown causes zero reconnect attempts.
- Older backends that do not advertise heartbeat remain usable.

## Related work

The still-valid behavior and tests in #71475, #40168, and #60727 should be
salvaged onto current `main` rather than merged or cherry-picked blindly.
Related reports: #32997, #40164, and #48564.

## Non-goals

- Durable event outbox / delivery acknowledgement redesign
- Readiness authentication changes
- Relay concurrency changes
- Proxy, tunnel, or infrastructure lifetime policy
- Deployment or backport work

items.title: Windows: failed venv recreate falls back to a destructive in-place delete, leaving the install gutted with no rollback (and the blocker probe cannot run afterwards)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Summary

On Windows, the bootstrap installer's `venv` stage recreates the virtual
environment by **renaming it aside first, and falling back to an in-place
delete when the rename is denied**. When that in-place delete then fails on a
single locked `.pyd`, the stage aborts *after having already removed most of
the environment*. There is no rollback: the installation is left with
**2 packages out of 212** and Hermes is unusable until a full reinstall.

A second defect turns this from "recoverable" into "undiagnosable": the
product's own blocker probe, `hermes_cli/_scan_venv_blockers`, needs `psutil` —
which the same failed delete has already removed. It then prints
`psutil is not available` and returns `{"ok": false, "blocked": false, "processes": []}`.
A tool that cannot run reports **no blockers**, which reads exactly like "clear".

This is the same *class* as #37881 (closed 2026-06-04) but a different code
path: there the failure was `shutil.rmtree` + a missing `pyvenv.cfg`; here
`pyvenv.cfg` and `python.exe` survive and only `site-packages` is destroyed.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), installed via the desktop bootstrap installer
- Python 3.11.15 (managed uv)

### What the log shows

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\bootstrap-installer.log`:

```
INFO bootstrap.log: -> Virtual environment already exists, recreating... stage=venv
INFO bootstrap.log: -> Stopping any running hermes processes before recreating venv... stage=venv
INFO bootstrap.log: [!] Could not rename venv aside (Access to the path '...\hermes-agent\venv' is denied.); falling back to in-place delete stage=venv
INFO bootstrap.log: {"skipped":false,"ok":false,"reason":"Cannot remove item ...\venv\Lib\site-packages\setproctitle\_setproctitle.cp311-win_amd64.pyd: Access to the path '_setproctitle.cp311-win_amd64.pyd' is denied.","duration_ms":7506,"stage":"venv"}
ERROR hermes_bootstrap_lib::bootstrap: bootstrap FAILED stage=Some("venv") error=Cannot remove item ... is denied.
```

Note the ordering: the installer **did** try to stop Hermes processes first,
and still could not rename the directory — because the holder was not a Hermes
process (see "How it got locked" below).

### Resulting state

- `venv\Lib\site-packages`: **2 directories** (was 212)
- `python.exe`, `pyvenv.cfg`, `hermes.exe` still present, so the CLI starts and
  then fails on missing imports
- `_scan_venv_blockers` → `psutil is not available`, exit 1, `"blocked": false`
- Recovery required re-running `bootstrap-cache/install-main.ps1 -NonInteractive`
  and reinstalling `setproctitle` by hand

### How it got locked (relevant to #22054)

The blocker was **not** a Hermes process. The Windows installer puts
`hermes-agent\venv\Scripts` **first** on the user `PATH` so that `hermes` is
globally available (#22054, #52508). A side effect is that bare `python`
resolves *into the installation* for every process on the machine. Any
unrelated project whose tooling runs `python tools/whatever.py` therefore holds
`.pyd` files inside the Hermes venv and becomes an update blocker.

Confirmed with Windows Restart Manager (`RmStartSession`/`RmRegisterResources`/
`RmGetList`) against the venv's files — several holders were another
repository's scripts:

```
[hermes ] PID 28748 python.exe  ...\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run
[foreign] PID 15008 python.exe  ...\venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/falsify.py
[foreign] PID 31852 python.exe  ...\venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/test_package_check.py
```

Restart Manager is worth adopting for the preflight generally: it names the
holder even when the process renamed itself with `setproctitle` (which the
gateway does, and which is why its `CommandLine` reads as empty in WMI, and why
`tasklist /m` finds nothing).

### Suggested fixes

1. **Never fall back to a destructive delete.** If renaming the venv aside is
   denied, abort the stage with the working installation still intact. A failed
   update should leave the previous version running.
2. If in-place delete must stay, make it **transactional**: copy aside first,
   or verify every file is removable (open each for `FileShare.None`) before
   deleting anything.
3. **A probe that cannot run must not report "clear."** `_scan_venv_blockers`
   already distinguishes `ok:false` from `blocked:false` in its JSON, but the
   caller treats a failed probe as a clear one; and shipping the probe inside
   the environment being replaced means it dies exactly when it is needed.
   Consider a stdlib-only fallback (Restart Manager via ctypes needs no
   third-party package).
4. Verify the **installation**, not the commit, after an update: package count,
   a few imports, `hermes --version`. A failed update currently reports success
   by git position while the environment is empty.

### Related

- #37881 (closed) — same class, earlier code path (`shutil.rmtree`, missing `pyvenv.cfg`)
- #73381 — Windows file locking during `uv pip install`
- #22054 / #52508 — venv `Scripts` on PATH; the mechanism that turns unrelated projects into blockers
- #77422 — a non-Hermes process blocking the update
- #66765 — desktop build stamp caching a broken build (the GUI was destroyed by the same failure and never rebuilt)

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — latest prompt and answer appear halfway up the chat (mid-thread)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

On **Hermes Desktop**, after sending a new prompt, the **latest user prompt and its assistant answer do not stay at the bottom of the transcript**. They appear **mid-thread** (“halfway up the chat”), with older messages both above and below the live exchange. That breaks the basic chat spine: you lose the live turn, have to hunt for it, and multi-turn work becomes unusable.

Priority: **P0/P1** — core conversation surface; every multi-turn Desktop session is affected when it repros.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop on **macOS**.
2. Open a session that already has a long transcript (enough messages to scroll; multi-turn history present).
3. Scroll so you are roughly at the bottom (or let the thread follow output).
4. Send a new prompt.
5. Watch where the new user bubble and the streaming/final assistant bubble land in the message list and viewport.

## Expected Behavior

- New user message is appended at the **end** of the transcript.
- Assistant stream/final is appended **after** that user message at the end.
- If stick-to-bottom / follow-output is active, the viewport keeps the live turn in view at the bottom (not mid-list).

## Actual Behavior

- The latest prompt and answer appear **halfway up** the chat (mid-thread), not as the bottom-most exchange.
- Older content remains below the live turn and/or the viewport centers on mid-history so the live turn is easy to lose.

## Affected Component

- Product: **Hermes Desktop** chat transcript
- Code area (suspect runway on current tree):
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/index.ts` — `mutateStream` (seeds/appends live assistant bubble; `streamId` bookkeeping)
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/submit.ts` — optimistic user append (`setMessages(current => [...current, buildUserMessage()])`)
  - `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/list.tsx` — `useStickToBottom` / `scrollToBottom` / follow-output
  - `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/timeline.tsx` — `scrollToPrompt` (jump-to-prompt paths)
  - `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages.ts` — `appendStreamPart` / `mergeFinalAssistantText` (if bubble reuse merges into a non-tail message)
  - Related stream family: prior Desktop stream/bubble issues (e.g. dual-final / prefix-replay class around `streamId` + finalize)

## Root Cause Analysis

Two failure modes can produce the same user report; file should cover both until one is ruled out:

| Mode | Symptom detail | Likely code |
|------|----------------|-------------|
| **A. Wrong list order / insertion** | Live user+assistant are not the last items in `messages[]` (or branch/group projection puts them mid-list) | Submit/optimistic path, `mutateStream` seed, history merge/reload, branch groups |
| **B. Correct list order, wrong viewport** | Messages are at the end in data, but scroll jumps to mid-thread so the live turn looks “halfway up” | `useStickToBottom`, `scrollToBottom` on `thread.runStart`, timeline `scrollToPrompt` |

Smoking-gun checks for whoever picks this up:

1. On repro, log or inspect whether the new user id and `streamId` are the last two visible messages in session state.
2. If yes → Mode B (scroll). If no → Mode A (order/merge).
3. Confirm `mutateStream` still seeds with `[...prev, new]` when `!prev.some(m => m.id === streamId)` and that `message.start` does not reuse a non-null `streamId` from a prior turn (`state.streamId ?? next(...)` pattern — hard-reset on `message.start` is the known fix class for cross-turn bubble bugs).

```ts
// use-message-stream/index.ts — mutateStream (approx.)
const streamId = state.streamId ?? nextStreamMessageId('assistant-stream')
if (!prev.some(m => m.id === streamId)) {
  nextMessages = [...prev, { id: streamId, role: 'assistant', parts: seed(), pending: true, ... }]
} else {
  nextMessages = prev.map(m => m.id === streamId ? { ...m, parts: transform(...) } : m)
}
```

```ts
// submit.ts — optimistic user (approx.)
scope.setMessages(current => [...current, buildUserMessage()])
```

If order is correct in state but the UI still shows the live turn mid-viewport, treat `list.tsx` stick-to-bottom / runStart scroll as the primary fix surface.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Determine Mode A vs B** with the two checks above (state tail vs viewport).
2. **Mode A:** Ensure optimistic user + stream assistant always append at the tail; on `message.start`, hard-reset `streamId` so a stale id cannot map-transform a mid-list bubble; audit any history merge/reload that reorders by unstable timestamps or inserts by index.
3. **Mode B:** On `thread.runStart` / new user submit, force stick-to-bottom for the active session unless the user has explicitly scrolled up (preserve “reading history” intent); do not call jump-to-prompt/timeline scroll on ordinary send.
4. Add regression tests (below). Prefer the smallest correct change; do not paper over with only auto-scroll if order is wrong.

## Tests

- [ ] Unit/integration: N sequential turns → `messages` tail is always `[..., userN, assistantN]` (or stream then final) with no older messages after the live pair.
- [ ] `message.start` after a prior complete/interrupt always allocates a **new** `streamId` (no reuse of sealed bubble).
- [ ] Stick-to-bottom: when `isAtBottom` was true before send, after submit + first delta the live turn is in view at the bottom.
- [ ] User scrolled up intentionally: send does not yank them unless product explicitly requires it; document the chosen rule in the test name.
- [ ] Long transcript stress (50+ turns): new turn still ends at list tail; no mid-list insertion.
- [ ] Existing stream-flush / interim-sealing / dual-final guards still pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After sending a prompt in a long session, the new user message and assistant answer are the bottom-most exchange in the transcript list.
- [ ] With follow-output / stick-to-bottom active, the viewport keeps that live exchange at the bottom (not mid-thread).
- [ ] No regression of known stream bugs (previous-answer-at-head, dual final, unbounded growth).
- [ ] Automated test covers “long history + new send → tail position” and documents Mode A vs B if both paths remain.

## Environment

- **Operating System:** macOS
- **App surface:** Hermes Desktop
- **Backend tree reference (agent host install):** `hermes-agent` @ `0b33ee88e` (for path/symbol grounding only)
- **Notes:** UI-navigation/transcript bug; no external debug paste required. Symptom is in-chat message list/viewport, not sidebar row ordering.

## Priority signal

Ship-blocking for multi-turn Desktop use when it hits: every new prompt/answer pair is hard to find. Treat as **P0/P1** chat-spine defect.
