items.title: Gateway crashes with AttributeError when gateway.platforms is a list (standard setup format)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug

Every gateway message (Telegram, Discord, etc.) returns:
> Sorry, I encountered an unexpected error. Try again or use /reset to start a fresh session.

## Root cause

Commit 003b4c889 ("perf(gateway): per-platform skip_context_files") added this code in `gateway/run.py` (~line 4734):

```python
_platforms_gw_cfg = (ctx.user_config.get("gateway") or {}).get("platforms") or {}
_plat_gw_cfg = _platforms_gw_cfg.get(platform_key) or {}
```

It assumes `gateway.platforms` is a **dict** (so `.get()` works). But `hermes gateway setup` writes it as a **list**:

```yaml
gateway:
  platforms:
    - telegram
    - discord
```

When `platforms` is a list, `.get()` raises:

```
AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
```

This crashes every incoming turn on all messaging platforms.

## Impact

Anyone whose config.yaml has `gateway.platforms` as a list (the format produced by the setup wizard) is affected. Users without the `platforms` key are unaffected (falls back to `{}`).

## Reproduce

1. Set `gateway.platforms` as a list in config.yaml
2. Restart gateway
3. Send any message via Telegram or Discord

## Fix

```python
_platforms_gw_cfg = (ctx.user_config.get("gateway") or {}).get("platforms") or {}
_plat_gw_cfg = (_platforms_gw_cfg.get(platform_key) or {}) if isinstance(_platforms_gw_cfg, dict) else {}
```

Tested locally — gateway processes messages normally after this change.

## Environment

- Commit: 003b4c8893245ed96fef8b344c9e89c3e218cd3e (and later)
- Platform: Linux, Telegram + Discord

items.title: Bug: find-in-page bar (Ctrl+F) overlaps native window controls on Windows — verified, covered by #80244

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows (native Window Controls Overlay on the right), pressing `Ctrl+F` opens the find-in-page bar pinned to the top-right corner — underneath the OS-drawn minimize/maximize/close buttons. The bar's next/prev/close buttons are covered and unclickable; clicks land on the OS buttons instead, so a stray click near the bar can minimize or **close the whole Hermes window**.

## Root cause (verified against current main, 3139a30e5)

`src/components/find-bar.tsx:162`:

```tsx
'pointer-events-auto fixed right-4 top-[calc(var(--titlebar-height,0px)+0.5rem)] z-50',
```

The FindBar mounts **outside** the subtree that defines `--titlebar-height`:

- the main shell sets `--titlebar-height: 0px` on the layout wrapper (`src/app/contrib/controller.tsx:723`), but that wrapper is passed as `{children}` and rendered inside `ContribWiring`'s `contents` div (`src/app/contrib/wiring.tsx:1010`);
- `<FindBar />` renders at `wiring.tsx:1043` — a **sibling** of that div, so the variable never reaches it. The CSS fallback (`0px`) is what actually positions the bar.

Result: the bar renders at `top: 8px`, `right: 16px` — inside the native window-controls strip (34px tall, rightmost ~144px; `electron/main.ts` uses `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` + `titleBarOverlay { height: 34 }`). OS-drawn buttons always win hit-testing over web content, so the find bar's right-side buttons are dead.

## Status

Covered by **#80244** (fallback `0px` → `34px` moves the bar to 42px, clear of the 34px native strip). Verified that the fallback is indeed the effective value in the main window, so that fix lands. Closing this issue in favor of #80244.

## Environment

- Windows 10, packaged build (commit 3139a30e5, built 2026-08-10)
- macOS unaffected (traffic lights on the left)
- Linux with a right-side native overlay (KDE/GNOME) affected the same way

## Related

- #80244 — open PR fixing this exact overlap
- #72961 — older find-in-page bar overlap report
- #82896 — find bar vs. files-pane positioning (same component, different slice)

items.title: Desktop pet renders blurry on Retina displays — canvas ignores devicePixelRatio
items.body:
Bug description The petdex mascot in the Hermes desktop app renders at low resolution on Retina / high-DPI displays (e.g. MacBook Pro). The pet looks noticeably blurrier than the same sprite shown on the petdex website.

Root cause In apps/desktop/src/components/pet/pet-sprite.tsx, the canvas internal resolution is set to the frame size × scale only (drawW = round(frameW * scale), e.g. 192 × 0.5 = 96px), and never multiplied by devicePixelRatio:

ts // pet-sprite.tsx:149-150 const drawW = Math.round(frameW * scale) const drawH = Math.round(frameH * scale) // ... // pet-sprite.tsx:358-366 <canvas aria-label={...} height={drawH} ref={canvasRef} style={{ height: drawH, width: drawW }} width={drawW} />

Additionally ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false (line 328) is set for pixel-art style, which amplifies the blur when the browser upscales the low-res canvas to the physical pixel grid.

Suggested fix Render the canvas at drawW * devicePixelRatio internally while keeping the CSS size at drawW:

ts const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1 const drawW = Math.round(frameW * scale) const drawH = Math.round(frameH * scale) // canvas: width={drawW * dpr} height={drawH * dpr}, style unchanged (drawW x drawH)

Environment

Hermes 0.20.0, macOS, Retina display
Pet: yuexinmiao (any pet affected — frame size 192×208)

items.title: SQLite file descriptor leak — SessionDB connections not closed on exception paths (EMFILE crash)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
# SQLite file descriptor leak — SessionDB connections not closed on exception paths (EMFILE crash)

## Summary

The `hermes dashboard` process leaks SQLite file descriptors (`state.db` + `state.db-wal`) until it hits the process FD ceiling and crashes with `[Errno 24] Too many open files`. Root cause: `SessionDB` instances are created and passed to `_make_agent()` on the success path (ownership transfers to the agent), but on **exception paths** the connection is orphaned. An `atexit.register` in `SessionDB.__init__` pins the connection alive until process exit, so FDs accumulate over time.

## Evidence

Long-running dashboard process (`hermes dashboard --tui --no-open --host 0.0.0.0`) hit the soft FD limit of 1024:

```
$ cat /proc/2136/limits | grep "open files"
Max open files            1024                 1048576              files

$ ls -la /proc/2136/fd | awk '{print $NF}' | grep -oE '(socket|pipe|/[^/]*)' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
491 /state.db
490 /state.db-wal
 16 socket
 14 pipe
```

**981 of 1024 FDs** were leaked SQLite handles (491 × `state.db` + 490 × `state.db-wal`).

Error seen by the user:
```
API call failed after 3 retries: [Errno 24] Too many open files
```

After applying the fixes below and restarting, FD count stabilized at ~28–30 (was 1024).

## Root Cause

`SessionDB.__init__` registers an `atexit` handler that keeps the connection object referenced until process exit. When `_make_agent()` raises an exception, the `session_db` / `branch_db` local variable goes out of scope, but the `atexit` registration prevents garbage collection. Each failed agent build leaks one `state.db` + one `state.db-wal` FD pair.

The problem compounds under the 3× API retry loop: each retry can trigger another exception path, each leaking another FD pair.

## Leak Sites & Fixes

### 1. `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_start_agent_build()` exception path

`session_db` is created, then passed to `_make_agent()`. If `_make_agent()` raises, the connection is orphaned.

```diff
             agent = _make_agent(sid, key, **kw)
+        except BaseException:
+            if session_db is not None:
+                try:
+                    session_db.close()
+                except Exception:
+                    pass
+            raise
         finally:
             _clear_session_context(tokens)
```

### 2. `tui_gateway/compute_host.py` — agent build exception path

Same pattern — `session_db` created for profile-scoped compute host, orphaned if `_make_agent()` raises.

```diff
-            agent = server._make_agent(
-                sid,
-                key,
-                session_id=key,
-                model_override=frame.get("model_override"),
-                reasoning_config_override=frame.get("reasoning_config_override"),
-                service_tier_override=frame.get("service_tier_override"),
-                platform_override=frame.get("source"),
-                session_db=session_db,
-            )
+            try:
+                agent = server._make_agent(
+                    sid,
+                    key,
+                    session_id=key,
+                    model_override=frame.get("model_override"),
+                    reasoning_config_override=frame.get("reasoning_config_override"),
+                    service_tier_override=frame.get("service_tier_override"),
+                    platform_override=frame.get("source"),
+                    session_db=session_db,
+                )
+            except BaseException:
+                if session_db is not None:
+                    try:
+                        session_db.close()
+                    except Exception:
+                        pass
+                raise
         finally:
```

### 3. `tui_gateway/methods_session.py:329` — `session.resume` early return

Profile-scoped `db` created, then leaks on the "session not found" early return path.

```diff
+    _owns_db = False
     if profile_home is not None:
         from hermes_state import SessionDB

         db = SessionDB(db_path=profile_home / "state.db")
+        _owns_db = True
     else:
         db = _get_db()
     ...
         else:
+            if _owns_db:
+                try:
+                    db.close()
+                except Exception:
+                    pass
             return _err(rid, 4007, "session not found")
```

### 4. `tui_gateway/methods_session.py:2687` — branch agent build exception path

`branch_db` created for branch sessions, orphaned if `_make_agent()` raises.

```diff
             except BaseException:
+                if branch_db is not None:
+                    try:
+                        branch_db.close()
+                    except Exception:
+                        pass
+                raise
             finally:
                 _clear_session_context(tokens)
```

### 5. `gateway/slash_commands.py` — `/insights` command

`db.close()` was called on the success path but not in a `finally`, so exceptions between `SessionDB()` and `db.close()` leak.

```diff
             def _run_insights():
                 db = SessionDB()
-                engine = InsightsEngine(db)
-                report = engine.generate(days=days, source=source)
-                result = engine.format_gateway(report)
-                db.close()
-                return result
+                try:
+                    engine = InsightsEngine(db)
+                    report = engine.generate(days=days, source=source)
+                    result = engine.format_gateway(report)
+                    return result
+                finally:
+                    db.close()
```

### 6. `hermes_cli/sessions_cmd.py:96` — `sessions repair` command

Bare `SessionDB()` instantiation with no `.close()` at all.

```diff
-                n = SessionDB()._conn.execute(
-                    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions"
-                ).fetchone()[0]
-                print(f"✓ Repaired — {n} sessions recovered.")
+                _repair_db = SessionDB()
+                try:
+                    n = _repair_db._conn.execute(
+                        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions"
+                    ).fetchone()[0]
+                    print(f"✓ Repaired — {n} sessions recovered.")
+                finally:
+                    _repair_db.close()
```

## Suggested deeper fix

Beyond patching individual call sites, consider adding a `__del__` or `weakref.finalize` fallback in `SessionDB` so that even if a caller forgets `.close()`, the SQLite connection is cleaned up when the object is garbage collected — rather than relying on `atexit` which pins it alive until process exit.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest main (commit `a991dfc25d`)
- OS: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04
- Python: 3.12
- Process: `hermes dashboard --tui --no-open --host 0.0.0.0` (long-running, hours/days)

items.title: [Bug]: Degenerate compress_end makes handoff scan miss in-window summary — _previous_summary discarded as "cross-session", rich handoff replaced by one-turn summary

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

A degenerate `compress_end` (tail cut consuming nearly the whole transcript) makes the handoff self-heal scan miss an in-window compaction summary, which then triggers the #57835 cross-session guard to **discard a valid same-session `_previous_summary`**. `_generate_summary` falls to the from-scratch path over a tiny region, and the resulting one-topic summary **replaces** the previous rich handoff — silent loss of the entire distilled record of earlier work.

## Code path (`agent/context_compressor.py`, `compress()`)

1. Summary scan bounds (~6585-6589): when `compression_count >= 1` or `_previous_summary` is set, `summary_search_end = compress_end`. A handoff row sitting at an index **beyond** `compress_end` is invisible to the scan. (The full-transcript scan only runs when `compression_count < 1 and not _previous_summary`, i.e. first compaction after a restart.)
2. Scan misses → `elif self._previous_summary:` (~6658-6664) assumes the non-empty `_previous_summary` is stale cross-session leakage (cron job, prior `/new`) and **sets it to None** — without checking whether a handoff row exists elsewhere in the window.
3. `_previous_summary=None` → `_generate_summary` takes the from-scratch branch over `messages[compress_start:compress_end]` (which can be as small as one message).
4. Phase 4 still recognizes the old handoff row via the content prefix and strips it from the rebuilt transcript as a fossil — so the old summary vanishes from live context while the new (thin, possibly wrong) summary takes its place.

## Observed incident (2026-08-10, real session, same-process second compaction)

- `compression_count=1`, `_previous_summary` = the session's own previous handoff (9.1K chars, 27 numbered completed actions). The handoff row sat at window index 4.
- The tail cut degenerated (`compress_end=1`; separate cause, reported as its own issue) → scan range `[0:1]` missed the handoff → `_previous_summary` discarded as "cross-session".
- The aux-model request (verified against the provider-side log) contained literally **one** user turn in `TURNS TO SUMMARIZE` plus the auto-focus block. The output summary covered none of the prior work and asserted work items "had not started" that were in fact completed — while Phase 4 dropped the real handoff from the window.
- Net effect: compression reduced the window by only 4 messages **and** destroyed the session's distilled state.

## Expected behavior

- `_previous_summary` must never be discarded while a handoff row belonging to the current session is present **anywhere** in the window. When `_previous_summary` is truthy (or `compression_count >= 1`), the scan should cover the full window — the content-prefix check is cheap.
- The #57835 discard branch should only fire after a full-window scan provably finds no handoff (and ideally should also verify session lineage before clearing).
- Defense in depth: when the region is tiny relative to the previous summary, treat a from-scratch result (or an output dramatically shorter than the previous summary) as a failure and retry/fall back rather than committing the lossy summary.

## Related

- #57835 — origin of the cross-session discard guard this interacts badly with.
- #57814 — adjacent in-memory-vs-persisted compressor state issue (protect_first_n decay).
- The degenerate-`compress_end` trigger on thinking-replay providers is reported separately (tail-cut stale-thinking charge).

items.title: [Bug][Windows] Terminal tool spawns visible console windows for sub-agent commands — CREATE_NO_WINDOW not applied on terminal execution path

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
**Bug / Feature**: Windows: sub-agent terminal tool executions spawn visible console windows (`python.exe`, `cmd`, `docker build` etc.), regardless of the calling context.

**Environment**: Windows 10, Hermes v0.20.0, terminal.backend=local, desktop app.

**Reproduction**:
- A delegated sub-agent runs any command through the terminal tool (e.g. `python helper.py`, `python -c ...`, `git ...`).
- A visible console/cmd window pops up on the user's desktop each time (often repeatedly during long multi-step tasks like docker builds with polling scripts).
- Workaround today: force every helper script to use `pythonw.exe`, and plan tasks so they avoid plain `python` calls — brittle, and impossible for arbitrary commands.

**Findings**:
- `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py` already defines `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` handling and is applied to *some* call sites (git probe, shell_hooks, skill_preprocessing), but the terminal tool execution path is not covered — sub-agent commands still spawn windows.

**Suggestion**:
- Apply the existing `windows_hide_flags` / `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` consistently to the terminal tool's subprocess creation on Windows (Popen/Popen-like call sites), so no command executed through the terminal tool ever creates a visible console window.
- Consider a config escape hatch (e.g. `terminal.show_windows: true`) for users who actually want to see child console output.

This is a UX/desktop-polish bug that makes long-running agent tasks feel intrusive on Windows.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop image attachments silently fail or drop the turn when pre-analysis fails / is interrupted (no response)
items.body:
## Bug Description

On the desktop app, dragging image files directly into the chat (as image attachments) can result in **no response at all**, or a response delayed by minutes. Dragging a *folder* containing the same images works normally.

Root cause is in the desktop gateway's send path: direct image attachments are pre-analyzed by the auxiliary vision model before the turn is dispatched (`_enrich_with_attached_images`, tui_gateway/server.py:6826). Two failure modes compound:

1. **Pre-analysis failure is silent and has no retry.** Each image is analyzed serially via `vision_analyze_tool`; any exception is swallowed (`except Exception: parts.append(...)`) and replaced with the placeholder `[The user attached an image but analysis failed.]`. The user sees no error, no progress, no retry — and when the auxiliary vision provider has a network hiccup, the message is delivered to the model already degraded.

2. **If the user touches another session (or sends another message) during the slow pre-analysis, the turn is killed with zero API calls and the message is gone.** Pre-analysis of 3 photos takes ~60–90 s each serially. A turn that starts with `interrupted_by_user` (conversation_loop.py:1651) exits before the first API call (`api_calls=0/60`), and the persisted session history ends with the user message and **no assistant reply and no retry** — the user's request is effectively lost.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Desktop app, main model on provider A, `auxiliary.vision` configured on provider B.
2. Drag 3 large photos (≈3 MB each) directly into the chat with a text prompt; send.
3. During the pre-analysis wait (no UI progress indicator), switch to another session or send a new message in another window.
4. Observe: the turn never produces a reply. Session history contains only the user message; the agent log shows the turn ended with `reason=interrupted_by_user`, `api_calls=0/60`, `response_len=0`.
5. Alternative repro without interrupting: make provider B unreachable (offline / flaky). Pre-analysis fails with `Connection error`, the user message is sent with the `analysis failed` placeholder, and the model only sees the placeholder plus a `vision_analyze` hint — but the main model in this setup was text-routed, so the reply is degraded or absent.

## Expected Behavior

- Pre-analysis failure should be **visible** to the user (inline status + error) and **retryable**, or the image path should be handed to the main loop for `vision_analyze` (which has its own retry) instead of being replaced by a silent placeholder.
- An interrupt during the pre-analysis window should not drop the request: the user message should be preserved and re-dispatched (or at minimum surfaced as "your message was not processed — send again"), since the user cannot distinguish "still analyzing" from "dead".
- A progress indicator while pre-analysis runs would prevent the user from assuming the app is hung.

## Actual Behavior

Session timeline (log excerpts, sanitized):

```
23:24:49 WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 7.0s (GIL pressure suspected)
23:25:36 ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Connection error.
23:25:36 WARNING [sessionA] agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=APIConnectionError provider=kimi-coding ...
23:25:41 WARNING agent.stream_diag: Stream drop on attempt 2/3 — retrying ... RemoteProtocolError ... provider=kimi-coding
23:25:50 ERROR tools.vision_tools: Error analyzing image: Connection error.   <- pre-analysis failure (sessionB's images)
23:27:08 INFO  [sessionB] agent.turn_context: conversation turn: ... msg='[The user attached an image but analysis failed.] [You can examine it with visio...'
23:27:09 INFO  [sessionB] agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=interrupted_by_user model=kimi-k2.7-code api_calls=0/60 budget=0/60 tool_turns=0 last_msg_role=user response_len=0
```

Control case: same images attached via `@folder:` reference (folder path) — no pre-analysis path — the agent responds within seconds and analyzes the images itself with `vision_analyze` including retries.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
- Platform: desktop (macOS)
- Main model: kimi-k2.7-code (provider kimi-coding)
- Auxiliary vision: kimi-k2.6 (provider kimi-coding)
- Auxiliary title generation: ollama-cloud

## Root Cause Notes

- `tui_gateway/server.py:6826-6860` — `_enrich_with_attached_images`: serial pre-analysis, `except Exception` swallow, placeholder-only degradation.
- `tui_gateway/server.py:9899/9905/9907` — pre-analysis is on the critical path before `run_message` is built; the turn has not started yet.
- `agent/conversation_loop.py:1651` — `interrupted_by_user` exits the loop before any API call; nothing re-dispatches the original message.
- The CLI path (`cli.py:7690`) at least prints `⚠ vision analysis error — path included for retry`; the desktop/TUI path has no equivalent user-visible notice.

## Suggested Fixes (any combination)

1. Surface pre-analysis state/progress and failure to the desktop UI; on failure, pass the raw image path to the agent loop instead of the placeholder (the agent already has `vision_analyze` with retry).
2. Do not let an interrupt during the pre-analysis window discard the message: persist it and re-dispatch, or show an explicit "message was not processed" notice.
3. Consider bounding pre-analysis (timeout + concurrency) and/or moving it off the submit path (agent-side analysis in the loop, like the folder-reference path already does).

## Related

- #82339 — same function (`_enrich_with_attached_images`) but different symptom (session auto-title poisoned by the prepended vision description). A fix that removes/replaces the pre-analysis on the desktop submit path would address both.

items.title: DeepSeek 400: assistant messages with empty tool_calls:[] wedge sessions permanently

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Sessions on **DeepSeek** permanently wedge with HTTP 400 once an assistant message carrying `tool_calls: []` (an empty array) lands in replayed history. From that point on, **every** follow-up message to the session fails before delivery:

```
HTTP 400: Invalid 'messages[437].tool_calls': empty array.
Expected an array with minimum length 1, but got an empty array instead.
```

Observed across at least 6 different sessions on the same install, all with `provider=deepseek` / `model=deepseek-v4-flash`, all non-retryable (`BadRequestError`), all raised from the `_run_agent_streaming` thread in `agent.chat_completion_helpers`.

## Evidence

Full request dump captured on `non_retryable_client_error` (`request_dump_1f819f5dbd28_20260808_144115_112720.json`, POST `https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions`, 163 messages). The offending message:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "**Fix round 1 verified — ready for the closing review.** ...",
  "tool_calls": [],
  "reasoning_content": "User says \"status\" ..."
}
```

This is a **plain final text answer** — there is no legitimate reason for it to carry a `tool_calls` key at all. 1 of 68 assistant messages in the payload had the empty array; DeepSeek rejects the whole request.

## What we've verified

- `sanitize_api_messages()` (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`) — the pre-API chokepoint added for #56980 / #58755 — **correctly strips** `tool_calls: []` when run against the dumped payload in isolation (`conversation_loop.py` line ~900). So the empty array is **reintroduced after the sanitizer**, somewhere in the streaming request path (`interruptible_streaming_api_call` → `_run_agent_streaming`). I audited: `repair_message_sequence` merge, `_sanitize_tool_calls_for_strict_api`, `ChatCompletionsTransport.convert_messages`/`build_kwargs`, `build_assistant_message`, `copy_reasoning_content_for_api`, `drop_thinking_only_and_merge_users`, `_prepare_messages_for_non_vision_model`, plugin/middleware hooks — none should add the key, yet it reaches the wire.
- **In-memory only:** SQLite stores empty `tool_calls` as NULL (`json.dumps(tool_calls) if tool_calls else None`), so a fresh session load replays clean. A gateway restart (clears the per-session agent cache) un-wedges all affected sessions at once; the DB history is never corrupted.
- Each failure is immediately preceded by `Repaired N message-alternation violations before request` (N=4, then N=5 in the same session) — the consecutive-assistant merge in `repair_message_sequence` preserves a pre-existing `[]` on the surviving turn (this is documented in the sanitizer's own comment as a known source), and the repair log index correlates with the failing `messages[N]` position.

## Suggested fix

Guarantee the invariant at the **wire boundary**, not only mid-pipeline:

1. In `ChatCompletionsTransport.convert_messages()` (or `build_kwargs`), drop the `tool_calls` key from any assistant message whose value is an empty list — this catches every path that builds the request (main loop, summary path, retries, fallback re-builds).
2. In the streaming request builder, ensure the accumulated tool-call list is only attached to the message dict when non-empty.
3. Optionally: `repair_message_sequence` should not preserve a `[]` on the surviving turn of a merge (pop the key when the union is empty).

## Repro path

1. Run a long tool-heavy session on DeepSeek (v4 flash) — consecutive assistant turns are common (interim replies, background-process notifications).
2. At some point a turn ends with an assistant text message that carries `tool_calls: []` in the in-memory history.
3. Send any further message: HTTP 400 on every attempt, non-retryable. Session is wedged until the agent cache is cleared (gateway restart) or a new session is started.

items.title: hermes cron run reports 'failed' without executing the job (desktop-app shell)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
- macOS, running `hermes cron run` from a terminal inside the Hermes desktop app

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a no_agent cron job (same failure also affects agent jobs — the dispatch path is identical):
   ```
   hermes cron create --name test-x --schedule "30m" --script test-direct-exec.sh --no-agent
   ```
2. Run it from a terminal inside the desktop app:
   ```
   hermes cron run test-x
   ```
3. Observe the CLI prints `Ran now: failed.` while the job **never executes**:
   - `last_run_at` stays `null` in jobs.json
   - output directory stays empty
   - the execution row in `~/.hermes/cron/executions.db` is stuck at `status='claimed'` with `finished_at=NULL`

## Expected

The job executes (script runs, output saved) and the CLI reports the real outcome.

## Actual

The job never runs. The CLI reports "failed" immediately, and the execution stays `claimed` until scheduler-restart recovery happens to sweep it.

## Root cause (from code)

1. `tools/cronjob_tools.py` `cronjob_run` (~L997) calls `dispatch_async_delegation(...)` with a `session_key` resolved from the calling process environment. The CLI process **inherits the desktop session env**, so `_try_dispatch_background_run` resolves a session_key and takes the **background-dispatch path** — which is designed for the long-lived gateway, where the completion event re-enters the originating session.
2. The CLI then renders the result via `_job_action` in `hermes_cli/subcommands/cron.py`, which does not recognize `execution_mode="background"` responses (missing `execution_success` field) → it prints `failed`.
3. The CLI process exits right after printing, which kills the daemon worker thread (`tools/async_delegation.py` module-level daemon executor, `daemon=True`) → the job never runs, and the execution row stays `claimed`.

For comparison, triggering the same job from *inside* a session via the `cronjob` tool (`action='run'`) completes in ~125ms with `last_status=ok` and the output saved — so the cron engine itself is fine; only the CLI path is broken in this environment.

## Workaround

Trigger manual runs from inside a session via the cronjob tool (`action='run'`) instead of the `hermes cron run` CLI.

## Suggested fix

When the CLI detects the run was dispatched to the background daemon (e.g. the response carries `execution_mode="background"` / a `delegation_id`), print "running in background (delegation <id>)" instead of a terminal success/failure — or have the CLI wait for the daemon worker to complete before printing a final verdict.

items.title: Tracking: kanban multi-agent enhancements — review-loop gap, context handoff, cost split, merge reconciliation (Aug 2026)

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
# Kanban multi-agent enhancements — swarm-economics takeaways + community review-loop gaps (Aug 2026 tracking)

Tracking issue for a body of work spanning one deep PR review and three shipped PRs, driven by two inputs that arrived the same week and pointed at the same subsystem:

1. **Public agent-swarm economics research** (planner/worker cost splits, decorrelated review lenses, neutral merge arbitration, context-handoff-over-shared-state) — evaluated against what Hermes already has.
2. **A community Discord thread** where a user modeling a coder → reviewer → CI-remediation kanban pipeline hit two walls: the review-loop deadlock, and not knowing the parent-link context handoff existed.

## Where we were

- **No same-card review loop.** A coder card requiring review had to sticky-block with free-form `review-required:` text. Deterministic deadlock, confirmed on main: children gate on parent `done` (`recompute_ready`), a blocked parent never satisfies that, and done cards cannot reopen — so coder⇄reviewer required manual operator surgery every round. ~20 open PRs and issue #67963 orbit this gap; a community member hit it within days of setting up their first multi-profile board.
- **The parent-link context handoff was undocumented.** Creating a follow-up card with a *completed* card as parent (instant eligibility + parent's completion summary/metadata injected into the worker context) has worked all along — but it took a moderator three rounds on Discord to convey it. Users were trying to reopen done cards or pass context through branch state instead.
- **The planner/worker cost split was unsurfaced.** `delegation.model`/`delegation.provider` (pin all subagent children cheap) and kanban per-profile models + per-task `model_override` existed, but no doc framed them as the cost strategy: children/workers carry the large majority of tokens, so that is where spend lives.
- **No neutral path for agent-vs-agent merge conflicts.** When two workers' branches collided in parallel campaigns, the colliding agent (or a human) resolved — and an agent adjudicating against a peer's work reliably overwrites the peer or abandons its own change.

## What we did

**Deep review of PR #75451** (first-class kanban review lifecycle, +4,102/−446, 36 files) via 5-way parallel subagent fan-out (DB core / tool+CLI surface / dispatcher+gateway+dashboard / tests+docs+skill / premise+cluster):
- Premise confirmed line-by-line on main; design direction endorsed (review as a lifecycle role, not a dependency-graph node).
- Found 2 blockers (silent savepoint nesting in `write_txn` changing semantics for every existing caller; respawn guard's `active_pr` rule deferring reviewer spawns in exactly the canonical PR-review case), 3 majors (claim-lock-less CAS in `request_review`; `consecutive_failures` counter amnesia on review round-trips; dashboard-only descendant invalidation that can silently kill live workers), plus minors.
- Cluster mapped: merging supersedes ~8 open PRs; #68210 (prefix-based competing fix) is the rejected direction; the 10 open kanban_db god-file refactor slices should land *after* it.
- Verdict presented: salvage + fix on top, attribution preserved (frizikk / capybara-x / kaishi00). **Decision pending.**

**Shipped (all live-tested before PR, all rebase-merged):**

| PR | What | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| #83061 (`d3560b82c4`) | Docs: the parent-link context handoff — done parent → follow-up card, `## Parent task results` block, CI-remediation worked example, new-child-vs-reopen contrast (en + zh-Hans) | Every claim exercised against a real isolated board: child of done parent created straight into `ready`; `build_worker_context` carried parent summary+metadata verbatim; negative control held |
| #83062 (`21835cc951`) | Docs: frontier-planner / inexpensive-worker cost split for delegation + kanban, incl. verified resolution order and the corrected premise that `delegate_task` has **no** per-task model override (kanban's per-task override is the pin-back path) | Sentinel-model resolution proven against a temp HERMES_HOME; kanban spawn path + `model_override` existence verified in code |
| #83063 (`34b6bbb96a`) | Bundled `merge-reconciler` skill: neutral third-party arbitration of agent-vs-agent merge conflicts (classify hunks: disjoint/combine, same-question/decide, superseded/drop; impartiality contract; per-hunk decision report) + contract tests + kanban docs cross-ref | Skill executed against a real two-branch conflict fixture by following its own written procedure; one ambiguity found mid-run was fixed and re-verified |

## Where we are now

- Users get the parent-link handoff pattern from the docs instead of three rounds of Discord archaeology; the remediation-card workflow is a first-class documented shape.
- The single highest-ROI cost knob (cheap children, frontier parent) is documented with verified keys for both delegation and kanban.
- Parallel campaigns have a neutral, tested procedure for worker-branch collisions, discoverable from the kanban docs, with the kanban-native shape (reconciliation card, both conflicted cards as parents) spelled out.
- The review-loop deadlock remains the one open gap, with a clear path: **#75451 salvage** (blocker/major fix list ready). Queued behind it: review-lens variation for reviewer spawns, split-brain decision-ownership guidance for orchestrators, and collision-hotspot flagging for workers — all touch surfaces #75451 rewrites.

Follow-up work is tracked against #75451 and issue #67963; this issue closes as the record of the completed slice.

items.title: [Feature]: Allow selective multiplex profile serving

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Problem or use case

A host can contain multiple Hermes profiles with intentionally different capabilities:

- a general-purpose default profile
- a restricted guest profile with a deliberately limited toolset, isolated configuration, and no access to general-purpose credentials
- developer, worker, or test profiles used from the CLI or by other services

A specific messaging route may send selected traffic to the restricted profile while ordinary traffic continues to use the default profile. Both routed profiles need to share one gateway because adapter multiplexing and per-conversation routing are exactly what `gateway.multiplex_profiles` is designed to provide.

Today, enabling `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` makes this gateway serve **every** valid named profile it finds. It starts their secondary adapters, schedules their cron jobs, exposes their API/webhook prefixes, and makes them eligible for routes, even when this gateway should serve only a selected subset.

The more important failure mode is routing. `gateway.profile_routes` can explicitly match traffic to the restricted profile. If that target is unavailable, however, the current resolution path ultimately falls back to the default profile. In this scenario that is not graceful degradation: traffic intended for a restricted context can silently enter the general-purpose context instead. A matched route must therefore fail closed when its target is not being served.

### Why the existing workarounds are not sufficient

- **Run a separate gateway for every profile:** this duplicates process supervision, ports, adapter/webhook configuration, health checks, and operational state. It also gives up the shared routing model that multiplex gateways exist to provide. Separate processes remain appropriate for hard OS-level isolation, but they should not be required merely to select which installed profiles one multiplex gateway activates.
- **Delete, rename, or move unrelated profiles:** those profiles may still be needed for CLI work, another gateway, or scheduled workflows. Installation on the same host should not imply activation in every multiplex gateway process.
- **Use a standalone `HERMES_HOME` or restricted launcher:** that can constrain an interactive session, but it does not tell an already-running multiplex gateway which named profiles it may activate.
- **Use `profile_routes` alone:** routes choose a destination for matching traffic; they do not constrain adapter or cron startup, HTTP profile prefixes, or the gateway's served-profile inventory. They also do not distinguish “no route matched” from “a route matched but its target is unavailable.”

What is missing is a composition primitive: keep the operational benefits of one multiplex gateway, explicitly select the secondary profiles that gateway serves, and reject matched traffic rather than silently crossing into the default profile when its selected target is unavailable.

This is gateway-level defense in depth and operability, not a replacement for process or OS isolation where a hard security boundary is required.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional named-profile allowlist under `gateway`, for example:

```yaml
gateway:
  multiplex_profiles: true
  multiplex_profile_allowlist:
    - worker
    - guest
  profile_routes:
    - name: guest-channel
      platform: discord
      guild_id: "guild-demo"
      chat_id: "channel-demo"
      profile: guest
```

Suggested behavior:

- Allowlist unset: preserve historical behavior and serve the default profile plus every valid named profile.
- Empty allowlist: serve only the default profile.
- Explicit list: normalize and deduplicate entries, then serve the default profile plus selected valid named profiles.
- The default profile is always served and does not need to be listed.
- A malformed allowlist fails safely to default-only with a clear warning. Invalid or missing profile names in an otherwise valid list are skipped with warnings.
- One computed served-profile set governs secondary adapters, cron scheduling, API/webhook profile prefixes, runtime status, and route eligibility.
- If no route matches, preserve the historical default-profile path.
- If a route explicitly matches but its target is not served, reject/drop that ingress with a clear log. Do not convert it to the existing default-resolution sentinel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unset, empty, and selected allowlists have the compatibility semantics above.
- [ ] Names are normalized/deduplicated and the default profile is always served.
- [ ] Invalid configuration has documented, tested fail-safe behavior.
- [ ] Secondary adapters and cron receive exactly the computed served set.
- [ ] API server and webhook `/p/<profile>/` prefixes reject profiles outside that set.
- [ ] Runtime `served_profiles` reports exactly the active set.
- [ ] A route to a served profile resolves normally.
- [ ] A matched route to an unserved or unavailable profile fails closed rather than running the default profile.
- [ ] No route match retains the historical default behavior.
- [ ] User documentation includes a generic configuration example and the matched-route fail-closed rule.

## Alternatives considered

- Run a separate gateway per profile. This is still useful for stronger isolation, but it gives up the operational benefits of multiplexing.
- Remove or rename unrelated profiles. Profiles may be needed for CLI or other gateway workflows even when this gateway should not activate them.
- Use `profile_routes` alone. Routes select a target but do not constrain adapter/cron startup or the HTTP profile inventory, and they do not distinguish no match from a matched but unavailable target.

## Contribution

A draft implementation is available in #83400.

items.title: [Desktop] 产物页面两个Bug：时间戳显示1970年1月 + 生成的图片无法显示
items.body:
## 描述 (Description)

Hermes Desktop 的**产物页面（Artifacts）**存在两个独立 Bug：

### Bug 1：时间戳单位错乱，全部显示为 1970年1月

产物页面所有条目的时间都显示为 **1970年1月21/22日**，但实际对话发生在 2026年6月之后。

**根因**：数据库中的时间戳是**秒级**（如 `1781271088` = 2026-06-12），但前端 `new Date(timestamp)` 按**毫秒**解析（`app/artifacts/index.tsx` 的 `formatArtifactTime`），导致所有时间偏移到 1970年1月：

```
1781271088 秒   = 2026-06-12  ✅（数据库实际值）
1781271088 毫秒 = 1970-01-21  ❌（前端显示值）
```

**复现**：打开产物页面，任意条目时间均显示为 1970年1月21日左右。

### Bug 2：本地生成的图片无法在产物中显示

产物页面收集到了生成的图片（`D:\ComfyUI\output\*.png` 等本地路径），但**图片加载失败**，显示为裂图/占位（`failedImageIds` 机制触发）。

**根因**：`artifactImageSrc`（`app/artifacts/artifact-utils.ts`）对本地路径调用 `mediaExternalUrl(value)` 转换，但本地文件不在 Hermes 媒体服务可访问范围内，转换出的 URL 无法加载 → `onImageError` → 标记 failed。

**复现**：在任意对话中生成图片（image_generate 工具，输出本地路径），打开产物页面 → 图片条目存在但无法显示。

## 期望行为 (Expected Behavior)

1. 产物时间戳正确显示实际生成时间（2026年6月及之后）
2. 生成的图片能在产物页面正常预览

## 实际行为 (Actual Behavior)

1. 所有产物时间显示为 1970年1月21/22日
2. 图片条目存在但加载失败，无法预览

## 环境 (Environment)

- Hermes Agent: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
- 平台: Windows 11 Pro (zh-CN)
- 界面: Hermes Desktop (Electron)
- 图片生成: 本地 ComfyUI（D:\ComfyUI\output\）

## 相关代码位置 (Code Locations)

- `apps/desktop/src/app/artifacts/index.tsx` — `formatArtifactTime()` 用 `new Date(timestamp)` 按毫秒解析秒级时间戳
- `apps/desktop/src/app/artifacts/artifact-utils.ts` — `artifactImageSrc()` 对本地路径调用 `mediaExternalUrl()` 导致加载失败

## 备注 (Notes)

两个 Bug 相互独立，可分开修复。时间戳问题：将秒级时间戳转换为毫秒（×1000）再传入 `new Date()`；图片问题：本地路径应通过 `readDesktopFileDataUrl()` 读取文件内容，而非转换 URL。

---

## 截图证据 (Screenshot)

![产物页面截图](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

items.title: [Bug]: Teams pipeline fetch fails for Teams /meet/ short URLs unless using user-scoped onlineMeetings Graph path
items.body:
### Bug Description

`hermes teams-pipeline fetch --join-web-url` fails to resolve Microsoft Teams short meeting URLs in this format:

`https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE`

The command appears to query `/communications/onlineMeetings`, which Microsoft Graph rejects for this case.

The same meeting can be resolved successfully using the organizer-scoped endpoint:

`/users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings?$filter=JoinWebUrl eq 'https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE'`

Once resolved through the user-scoped endpoint, the transcript can be listed and downloaded successfully as `text/vtt`.



### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the `teams_pipeline` plugin with Microsoft Graph app credentials.

2. Grant Graph application permissions:
   - `OnlineMeetings.Read.All`
   - `OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All`

3. Enable Teams transcript Graph access in Teams PowerShell:

   `Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -EnableGraphTranscriptAccess $true -EnableAttributedTranscripts $true`

4. Create and assign a Teams Application Access Policy for the Hermes app:

   `New-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -Identity "Hermes-Meeting-Pipeline-Policy" -AppIds "MSGRAPH_CLIENT_ID" -Description "Allow Hermes Teams Meeting Pipeline to access meeting transcripts"`

   `Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -PolicyName "Hermes-Meeting-Pipeline-Policy" -Identity "ORGANIZER_UPN"`

5. Create a scheduled Microsoft Teams meeting with transcription enabled.

6. End the meeting and verify the transcript appears in Teams recap.

7. Run:

   `hermes teams-pipeline fetch --join-web-url "https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE"`

8. Observe that the command fails with a Microsoft Graph 400 error from `/communications/onlineMeetings`.

9. Use Microsoft Graph directly with the organizer-scoped endpoint:

   `GET /users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings?$filter=JoinWebUrl eq 'https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE'`

10. Observe that Graph successfully returns the `onlineMeeting` object.

11. Then query:

   `GET /users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings/ONLINE_MEETING_ID/transcripts`

12. Observe that transcript metadata is returned.

13. Download transcript content from:

   `GET /users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings/ONLINE_MEETING_ID/transcripts/TRANSCRIPT_ID/content`

14. Observe that transcript content downloads successfully as `text/vtt`

### Expected Behavior

`hermes teams-pipeline fetch --join-web-url "https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE"` should resolve the meeting and fetch the transcript.

If Microsoft Graph requires organizer-scoped lookup for these Teams short URLs, Hermes should support an organizer user ID or UPN option, such as `--organizer-user-id` or `--organizer-upn`.


### Actual Behavior

The command fails with a Microsoft Graph 400 error from `/communications/onlineMeetings`.

Error:

`Microsoft Graph API error 400 for GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/communications/onlineMeetings: InvalidArgument: Filter expression expected - /onlineMeetings?$filter=VideoTeleconferenceId eq '{vtcid}'.`

Manual Graph retrieval works when using the organizer-scoped endpoint:

`/users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings?$filter=JoinWebUrl eq 'https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE'`


### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
I did not upload a public debug report because `hermes debug share` warns that it may include personal data, recent message content, tool output, user IDs, and local filesystem paths.

Relevant local diagnostics:

`Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)`

`Install directory: /home/theunclebob/.hermes/hermes-agent`

`Python: 3.11.15`

`OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0`

`OS: Linux 6.8.0-136-generic x86_64 GNU/Linux`

`hermes teams-pipeline validate` returns `ok: true`.

Graph config status from validation:

`client_id: true`

`client_secret: true`

`tenant_id: true`

`webhook_enabled: true`

Warning from validation:

`Teams outbound delivery is disabled.`

`hermes teams-pipeline token-health --force-refresh` succeeds.

Token health:

`configured: true`

`last_refresh_succeeded: true`

`scope: https://graph.microsoft.com/.default`

Sensitive values, tenant IDs, client IDs, secrets, and tokens are redacted.
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.20.0 (2026.8.3)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The issue appears to be in the meeting-resolution path used by `hermes teams-pipeline fetch --join-web-url`.

For Teams short URLs such as `https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE`, Hermes appears to query `/communications/onlineMeetings`.

Microsoft Graph rejects that query for this case.

Manual testing showed that the same meeting resolves successfully when queried through the organizer-scoped endpoint:

`/users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings?$filter=JoinWebUrl eq 'https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE'`

Manual testing also showed that lookup by `joinMeetingIdSettings/joinMeetingId` works when using the organizer-scoped endpoint.

After resolving the meeting through `/users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings`, transcript metadata and transcript content can be retrieved successfully.

So the likely root cause is that the Teams pipeline resolver relies on `/communications/onlineMeetings` for `--join-web-url`, but this endpoint does not work for the newer Teams `/meet/` short URL format in this app-only scenario.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

Support organizer-scoped online meeting lookup for Teams short `/meet/` URLs.

Possible implementation options:

1. Add optional arguments to `hermes teams-pipeline fetch`, such as `--organizer-user-id` and/or `--organizer-upn`.

2. When an organizer identity is available, resolve `--join-web-url` through:

`/users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings?$filter=JoinWebUrl eq 'https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/MEETING_CODE?p=PASSCODE'`

3. Also support lookup by meeting code through:

`/users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings?$filter=joinMeetingIdSettings/joinMeetingId eq 'MEETING_CODE'`

4. After resolving the meeting, use the returned Graph `onlineMeeting.id` to list/download transcripts from:

`/users/ORGANIZER_USER_ID/onlineMeetings/ONLINE_MEETING_ID/transcripts`

5. Document that Microsoft Teams short `/meet/` URLs may require organizer-scoped Graph lookup.


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: browser_exec crashes: pydantic_core ModuleNotFoundError when PYTHONPATH points at Hermes venv (desktop app)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug Description

`browser_exec` (Browser Use mode) fails on every call with:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core'
```

The traceback shows `pydantic` being imported from Hermes's **own venv** site-packages (e.g. `/Users/<user>/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pydantic`) while the `browser-use` CLI runs under a different Python version.

## Search for existing issues

- [x] Open issues searched: `pydantic_core browser`, `browser-use PYTHONPATH`, `browser_exec`, `uvx pydantic` — no near-duplicates
- [x] Closed issues searched: same queries — no near-duplicates

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes from an environment whose `PYTHONPATH` points at the Hermes repo root + its venv site-packages (the **desktop app does this**; the env carries `PYTHONPATH=/path/to/hermes-agent:/path/to/hermes-agent/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages`).
2. Ensure no `browser-use` binary is on PATH (fresh install) so `_find_cli()` falls back to `uvx browser-use`.
3. Call `browser_exec` with any code (e.g. `new_tab("https://example.com")`).
4. CLI crashes before running the code with the `pydantic_core` `ModuleNotFoundError` above.

Also reproduces standalone from the same env: `uvx browser-use --version` → same traceback.

## Root Cause

- `_find_cli()` in `tools/browser_use_cli.py` falls back to `uvx browser-use`.
- `uvx` creates an isolated env on **uv's default Python (3.13)**.
- The subprocess env (`_base_subprocess_env()` → `_build_browser_env()` → `hermes_subprocess_env`) passes `PYTHONPATH` through unchanged, so the 3.13 CLI imports `pydantic` from the **3.11** venv listed on `PYTHONPATH`. Its compiled `pydantic_core` extension (`_pydantic_core.cpython-311-*.so`) cannot load in a 3.13 interpreter → `ModuleNotFoundError`.

## Expected Behavior

The `browser-use` CLI subprocess must not inherit Hermes's Python path. It manages its own interpreter/venv; `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a different-version venv breaks any Python CLI with compiled extensions.

## Proposed Fix

Strip `PYTHONPATH`/`PYTHONHOME` from the browser-use subprocess env in `_base_subprocess_env()`:

```python
def _base_subprocess_env() -> dict:
    from tools.browser_tool import _build_browser_env

    env = _build_browser_env()
    # The browser-use CLI runs under a uvx-managed Python whose version may
    # differ from Hermes's venv. PYTHONPATH inherited from the agent process
    # points at Hermes's venv site-packages, so the CLI imports packages like
    # pydantic from the wrong interpreter and crashes on compiled extensions.
    env.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
    env.pop("PYTHONHOME", None)
    return env
```

## Workaround (survives updates)

A `browser-use` wrapper earlier on the agent PATH than `uvx`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
unset PYTHONPATH PYTHONHOME
exec uvx browser-use "$@"
```

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- Hermes v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), desktop app (env sets `PYTHONPATH`; the CLI/gateway may not)
- browser-use CLI 0.1.8 via uvx, uv Python 3.13

items.title: [Bug]: hermes update does not restart hermes-serve (Desktop backend) — leaves stale code running until manual restart

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes update` restarts `hermes-gateway*` systemd units and managed dashboards, but does **not** restart `hermes-serve` — the backend that the Desktop app connects to. After an update, the Desktop client correctly detects the version mismatch and shows "backend out of date," but the user has to manually restart the service.

## Where the bug is

In `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`:

- **Line ~3470**: `_for_each_systemd_gateway_unit()` only matches `hermes-gateway*` units — `hermes-serve` is excluded.
- **Line ~621**: `_finish_dashboard_update_cleanup()` handles dashboards separately.
- **No equivalent exists for `hermes-serve`**.

The serve backend is the Desktop app's runtime — it should get the same post-update restart treatment as the gateway and dashboard.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install Hermes Desktop with `hermes serve` as a systemd user unit (`hermes-serve.service`)
2. Run `hermes update`
3. Observe: `hermes-gateway.service` and dashboards restart, but `hermes-serve.service` does not
4. Desktop app shows "backend out of date" on reconnect

## Expected behavior

`hermes update` should discover and restart `hermes-serve*` systemd units (and any manually-run serve processes) alongside gateways and dashboards.

## Workaround

Manually restart after each update:

```bash
systemctl --user restart hermes-serve.service
```

Or use git hooks (`post-merge` + `post-checkout`) to auto-restart on code changes.

## Environment

- **OS**: Linux (Ubuntu), systemd user units
- **Hermes version**: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)
- **Install method**: Git-based, systemd-managed services

items.title: [Bug]: multiplexed profiles inherit the default busy input mode

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

A single gateway process with `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` loads `display.busy_input_mode` once from the process's default profile into `GatewayRunner._busy_input_mode`.

Busy traffic routed to a secondary profile therefore uses the default profile's policy instead of the routed profile's own `queue`, `steer`, or `interrupt` setting.

This is distinct from #83345 / #83346, which concerns clarify-key routing, and from #75678, which concerns Photon split-media coalescing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the default profile with `display.busy_input_mode: queue`.
2. Configure a secondary profile named `research` with `display.busy_input_mode: steer`.
3. Enable `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` and start one gateway process.
4. Start a task through the `research` profile, then send a text follow-up while that task is running.

A behavioral regression test against `main` at `b614f7036` also reproduces the inverse case: default `interrupt`, secondary `queue` or `steer`.

## Expected Behavior

The busy-input policy is resolved from the routed profile. The default profile can remain on one mode while `research` independently uses another.

Missing or invalid secondary-profile values should safely fall back to the gateway default.

## Actual Behavior

The runner branches on the process-level `self._busy_input_mode` in both the normal busy-session handler and the priority running-agent path. A secondary profile configured for `steer` can interrupt or queue according to the default profile instead.

The base adapter's `_busy_text_mode` is also copied from the process default onto secondary adapters, so legacy queue-text handling is not profile-specific either.

## Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) and Configuration (config.yaml).

## Messaging Platform

Platform-independent. The reproduced path uses a `BasePlatformAdapter`-based channel.

## Debug Report

A public debug upload is intentionally omitted. The source-level reproduction uses only synthetic `default` and `research` profiles and contains no deployment logs or identifiers.

## Operating System

macOS

## Python Version

3.11

## Hermes Version

Current `main` at `b614f7036`.

## Root Cause Analysis

`GatewayRunner.__init__()` snapshots `display.busy_input_mode` and the legacy text mode from the default profile. Later busy-session decisions read those process-level fields directly, even though `MessageEvent.source.profile` already identifies the routed profile under multiplexing.

Temporarily changing `HERMES_HOME` or process environment variables during a busy event would be unsafe in a concurrent gateway and is unnecessary.

## Proposed Fix

At startup, snapshot each served profile's busy modes from its own config without mutating process-global state. Resolve the effective mode from `event.source.profile` in both busy paths, with the existing gateway value as the fallback. Keep default and non-multiplexed behavior unchanged, and configure each secondary adapter's legacy text mode from the same profile snapshot.

The regression test should cover default behavior, secondary `queue` / `steer` / `interrupt`, fallback for missing or invalid values, and no per-message config rereads.

## Contribution

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Regression] Kanban: empty top-level kanban.db persists across restarts — boards table never created (0.17.0)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

After Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (macOS, arm64) starts, `~/.hermes/kanban.db` exists but contains **zero tables** — including the `boards` table. The Kanban UI therefore shows no boards. The empty state survives a full Hermes restart: the file is rewritten as a 4 KB empty SQLite file (no schema), not as a 0-byte file, which suggests an init path runs but fails silently before any `CREATE TABLE` statement.

This is a regression of #30687 (closed 2026-05-23): the silent-recreation guard from that fix does not run in this code path, or its scope was narrower than the original report described.

## Reproduction (reproducible on macOS 26.6, Hermes 0.17.0)

1. Quit Hermes Desktop.
2. `rm ~/.hermes/kanban.db ~/.hermes/kanban.db-shm ~/.hermes/kanban.db-wal`
3. Start Hermes.
4. Inspect the freshly created file:
   ```
   $ sqlite3 ~/.hermes/kanban.db ".tables"
   (empty)
   $ sqlite3 ~/.hermes/kanban.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table';"
   0
   ```
5. Open the Kanban view in the desktop UI → still empty.
6. Quit and restart Hermes → DB is re-created as a 4 KB file with zero tables again. No backup, no warning.

For comparison, the original incident in #30687 reported a 106 KB file with a full schema but empty rows. In this 0.17.0 case the schema is **also** missing — strictly worse.

## Observed vs. expected

- **Observed:** `kanban.db` is created on startup but contains no `boards` table. The renderer requests `boards`, the gateway returns empty, the UI shows nothing.
- **Expected (per #30687):** either (a) refuse to recreate and surface an explicit error requiring `hermes kanban init`, or (b) create the full schema (`boards`, `tasks`, `task_comments`, `task_events`, `task_runs`, `task_attachments`, `task_links`, `kanban_notify_subs`) and seed the default board so the UI has something to render.

## Evidence from this machine

```
$ defaults read .../Hermes.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleShortVersionString
0.17.0

$ ls -la ~/.hermes/kanban.db*
-rw-r--r--  1 walterkuntner  staff    4096 Aug 10 22:55 kanban.db
-rw-r--r--  1 walterkuntner  staff       0 Aug 10 22:55 kanban.db.dispatch.lock

$ sqlite3 ~/.hermes/kanban.db ".schema"
(nothing — empty schema)

$ ls /Users/walterkuntner/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/src/plugins/kanban/
kanban.css
```

Only `kanban.css` is present in the desktop source under `src/plugins/kanban/`. The schema-creation code is not visible in the open-source tree — it must live in the packaged `app.asar` (`Hermes.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar`, 8.8 MB), which makes this hard to bisect from the outside. Worth confirming the schema-init path still runs on first open of the Kanban view (it does not appear to, on this machine).

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (build 0.17.0), bundle id `com.nousresearch.hermes`
- macOS 26.6, arm64
- No Kanban data present (empty default install; no board loss to grieve)
- Hermes Gateway: embedded, default profile

## Related

- #30687 — original silent-recursion bug, closed 2026-05-23. This looks like an unfinished corner of the same fix: the silent-recreate guard does not run when the top-level DB is missing entirely (only when it is corrupted), and the schema-init path itself appears not to execute on startup.
- #43243 — Kanban dashboard/watch resurrecting archived/deleted boards as empty DB-only stubs (adjacent, possibly overlapping)

## Suggested fix surface

1. Confirm the schema-init code path actually runs during the desktop app startup sequence, not only on first kanban command.
2. When the top-level `kanban.db` is created or replaced, create the full schema and seed the default board.
3. Mirror the #30687 expectations: backup-before-replace, integrity-check before wipe, explicit error instead of silent empty-DB.

items.title: [Bug]: text-mode kanban show queries task graph after closing database connection
items.body:
## Bug Description

Text-mode `hermes kanban show <task-id>` raises `sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Cannot operate on a closed database` on current `main`. The JSON form succeeds for the same task.

The regression was introduced when graph-aware diagnostics were added to the text renderer. It affects every existing task, regardless of task state or graph membership.

## Regression Source

The failing graph query was added in merged PR #83412 when graph-aware diagnostics were connected to `_cmd_show()`. The new call was placed after the existing `kb.connect_closing()` block, so it receives a closed connection. The proposed correction preserves the diagnostics feature and only fixes the connection lifetime.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a temporary Hermes home and initialize a synthetic Kanban task:
   ```bash
   export HERMES_HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
   task_id="$(hermes kanban create 'example task' | grep -o 't_[a-f0-9]*' | head -1)"
   ```
2. Run the JSON form and observe that it succeeds:
   ```bash
   hermes kanban show "$task_id" --json
   ```
3. Run the text form:
   ```bash
   hermes kanban show "$task_id"
   ```

## Expected Behavior

The text form prints the task and any graph-aware diagnostics, then exits successfully.

## Actual Behavior

The text form raises:

```text
sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Cannot operate on a closed database.
```

## Affected Component

CLI / Kanban

## Messaging Platform

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

Not applicable; the deterministic synthetic reproduction above exercises the failing branch.

## Environment

- Hermes: current `main` after PR #83412
- OS: Linux
- Python: 3.12

## Root Cause Analysis

In `hermes_cli/kanban.py`, `_cmd_show()` loads the task data inside `kb.connect_closing()`. After that context exits, the text renderer calls:

```python
graph=kb.task_graph_context(conn, task.id)
```

At that point `conn` is already closed. The JSON path returns before this call, which explains why `--json` is unaffected.

## Proposed Fix

Load the task graph context while the connection is still open, retain the resulting value, and pass that value to `compute_task_diagnostics()` after the context exits. Add a regression test that exercises text-mode `show` with a real temporary Kanban database and confirms that the output renders successfully.

## Pull Request

A focused fix with regression coverage is available in PR #83453.
